$comment: LP FIDELITY LEDGER. Each entry is a geometric quantity measured on real LilyPond,
paired with the difference Lily# currently shows. See README.md for how to add or
regenerate an entry. The 'lilypond' numbers are DATA: they change only by re-running
the probes in probes/ against lilypond.exe and pasting what it prints.
residual = lilysharp - lilypond, in staff-spaces. A non-zero residual MUST carry a
'why'. Naming the defect is the goal; where it is not yet isolated, say so with an
'OPEN:' prefix and state exactly what is unexplained. What is forbidden is a silent
baseline. Both directions of change are failures: a residual that grows is a
regression, and a residual that shrinks is progress that must be recorded on purpose
so it appears in the diff rather than being absorbed.
The count of exact entries and the total |residual| are the headline fidelity numbers.

barline.next.down-stems-after-clef.why: OPEN: appeared with the 2.26.0 font, and only its scale is accounted for. The quantity is 0.9 (next-note) plus the optical correction, and LilyPond's correction moved 0.189365 -> 0.189360 with that font's LILC rounding while Lily#'s stayed at 0.189365449. So the cause is the same rounding that moved the other nine measured values -- it is bounded by that rounding (<= 7e-5) and it arrived on the same commit -- but WHICH glyph metric carries the 5.4e-6 through Staff_spacing's /7 has not been isolated. Smallest residual in the corpus. The attribution is not settled.

barline.next.accidental-to-notehead.why: EXACT since LilyPond 2.26.0, and NOT because anything in Lily# changed. 2.26.0 rebuilt Emmentaler with the LILC bboxes rounded to three decimals in the design unit, which put accidentals.sharp's right edge on exactly 1.100000 (2.24.4: 1.100010). The skyline term that separated LilyPond's measurement from Lily#'s box measurement was -0.000010 and is now zero. The horizontal skyline is still not ported (accidental-placement.cc:412) -- this entry merely stopped being able to see it. barline.next.key-change-to-notehead is now the only entry that still measures it.

accidental.single-natural-to-notehead.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (-0.017672 -> 0). The single-note / grace accidental DRAW was a SECOND placement model: chords place accidentals through AccidentalColumn.CalculatePositions (position_apes, the REAL glyph right skyline) then DrawAccidentalAtInkLeft, but a single NoteItem (SharedRenderer.Noteheads.cs) and grace (GraceNotes.cs) drew via DrawAccidental at a FIXED AccidentalNoteGap 0.35. Measured on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score NAT, a c-natural in D major): HEAD anchor 11.569272 (ext 0 . 1.962), natural ACC anchor 10.535000 (ext 0 . 0.6666), so the natural's ink clears the head at 0.367672 -- NOT 0.35 -- and HEAD - ACC anchor = 1.034272. OPENED at residual -0.017672 (predicted to the digit): Lily# drew the natural at head - natWidth(0.6666) - 0.35 = head - 1.0166, so HEAD - ACC read 1.016600. THE FIX: route the single-note / grace accidental DRAW through AccidentalPlacement.CalculateSinglePosition (the real skyline, the SAME path the spacing reservation already uses -- so draw = reserve) then DrawAccidentalAtInkLeft. MEASURED after: Lily# 1.034272 (residual -0.00000007, within tolerance) EXACT. Sharps (Left 0, box) are byte-unchanged; naturals move 0.017672 LEFT onto LilyPond's position. This ALSO fixed a flat draw bug the same fix exposed -- see accidental.single-flat-to-notehead.

accidental.single-flat-to-notehead.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (+0.120000 -> 0). A SECOND defect the single-note-accidental unification exposed, NOT anticipated by the handoff (which claimed sharp/flat 'match'): the flat's ink starts 0.12 ss LEFT of its origin (LILC bbox left -0.12). The old DrawAccidental seated the glyph origin at head - accWidth - 0.35 with accWidth = the FULL width 0.92 (Right 0.8 - Left -0.12), so the flat's ink-right landed at head - 0.47 -- gap 0.47, NOT LilyPond's 0.35. Rendered on 2.26.0 (score FLAT, a c-flat): HEAD anchor 9.155 (ext 0 . 1.962), flat ACC anchor 8.005 (ext -0.12 . 0.8), ink gap 9.155 - (8.005 + 0.8) = 0.35, HEAD - ACC anchor = 1.150000. OPENED at residual +0.120000 (predicted to the digit): Lily# drew the flat origin at head - 0.92 - 0.35 = head - 1.27, so HEAD - ACC read 1.270000. THE FIX is the same one that closed the natural: routing the draw through CalculateSinglePosition + DrawAccidentalAtInkLeft, which anchors on the glyph's ink-left (bbox.Left aware) rather than assuming the ink starts at the origin, so the flat lands on LilyPond's 0.35 gap. MEASURED after: Lily# 1.150000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT. Sharp/natural (Left 0) have no overhang; only flats (and double-flats) move, ~0.12 onto LilyPond's position.

chord.accidental.sharp-column-gap-below.why: CLOSED (island 2). The real accidental glyph horizontal-skyline is now baked from Emmentaler (GlyphSkylinesGenerated.cs, extractor Extract-EmmentalerSkylines.py) and the column packer is position_apes: -ape->horizontal_skylines_[RIGHT].distance(left_skyline, 0.1) - padding (accidental-placement.cc:411-416), nesting the sharps' real outlines. Two sharps a third apart interlock to 1.284000 EXACTLY (the notch on each # right stroke lets the neighbour tuck 0.016 past the box). The box model and the inert 0.375 flat-merge branch are gone. PREDICTED +0.016 held; the port took it to 0. Mirror cross-check HELD: chord.accidental.sharp-column-gap-above reads the identical 1.284000.

chord.accidental.sharp-column-gap-above.why: CLOSED (island 2) -- the IDENTICAL 1.284000 its mirror now reads, the cross-check this pair exists for. Vertical reflection of chord.accidental.sharp-column-gap-below (eis''/gis'' above the middle line, stems down); direction-independence held through the port. Full account on chord.accidental.sharp-column-gap-below.

chord.accidental.flat-column-gap-below.why: CLOSED (island 2), the larger half of the same defect as the sharps. Two flats a third apart now interlock to 0.964561 (residual 4e-7, below tolerance, from bezier flattening quantization). The real flat outline nests its narrow lower-left past the neighbour, and the 0.375 is now where LilyPond puts it -- accidental.cc:76 fattens the flat's OWN right skyline to stencil.right*0.375 over the stencil Y-extent, verified against a live 2.26.0 horizontal-skylines dump (a flat's RIGHT skyline floors at x=0.30 = 0.80*0.375). The old flat-merge branch (overlap = min(width)*0.375), which measurement had shown inert, is removed. PREDICTED that the constant was mislocated, not misvalued -- confirmed. Mirror cross-check HELD: chord.accidental.flat-column-gap-above reads the identical 0.964561.

chord.accidental.flat-column-gap-above.why: CLOSED (island 2) -- the IDENTICAL 0.964561 its mirror now reads. Vertical reflection of chord.accidental.flat-column-gap-below (des''/fes'' above the middle line, stems down); direction-independence held through the port. Full account on chord.accidental.flat-column-gap-below.

barline.next.key-change-to-notehead.why: CLOSED (island 2). The note opening this measure is a c' under A major carrying a NATURAL, and the barline-to-note reach is that accidental's leftmost ink. The natural is vertically thin, so its real right skyline stands 0.017606 further out than its box; the old single-note reservation (SpacingRules: bbox.Width + gap) missed that AND the position_apes padding, so this sat at -0.017672. Now the single-note left extent comes from AccidentalPlacement.CalculateSinglePosition (the same skyline placement the drawing uses), so the reservation matches LilyPond exactly (residual 7e-8). Predicted to close with the accidental horizontal-skyline; it did.

barline.next.time-change-to-notehead.why: CLOSED to +0.000000433 by porting Pango's quantisation LITERALLY, from LilyPond's own constants rather than by fitting. The difference was never a wrong glyph metric: LilyPond snaps a text width to a whole device pixel, and one device pixel is INCH_TO_BP / (PANGO_RESOLUTION * output_scale) staff spaces = 72 * 72.27 / (1200 * 5 * 25.4) = 0.034143 ss (lily/pango-font.cc:109-112 scale_, PANGO_RESOLUTION 1200 at lily/include/pango-font.hh:75, INCH_TO_BP 72 / INCH_TO_PT 72.27 at lily/include/dimensions.hh:31,27). Round the true advance 1.600000 to that grid and it lands on 46.86 -> 47 pixels = 1.604735, matching all ten digits to 1e-15. The residual 4.3e-7 is float noise in that arithmetic, not an unexplained sliver. ⚠️ SAME MECHANISM AS staff.staff.dynamic-under-whole-note's -0.000076, and that one is STILL open on purpose: a width needs only this single snap of one advance, but a skyline needs the whole OUTLINE quantised, which is a larger port. ⚠️ NOT closed by this, and recorded so it is not mistaken for closed: Lily# quantises the FATTENED digit advance, which equals the ASCII fetaText digit LilyPond actually sets ONLY for the digit 4 (both 1.600000); the fattened '1' is 1.292 where the ASCII '1' is 1.268, so a non-4 signature digit would quantise the wrong base. No ledger point measures one yet. Original account, of how the source was first located, follows. ly:time-signature::print builds a MARKUP and hands it to grob-interpret-markup (scm/time-signature.scm:18-29), and markup text is measured by the text layout engine, not by the music-font path Lily# and the rest of this corpus use. Asked both ways on one and the same grob on 2.24.4: ly:font-get-glyph 'fattened.four' gives 1.600000 while (markup #:number "4") gives 1.604735. So Lily#'s 1.600000 is not a stale or wrong constant — it is exactly what LilyPond's own music-font path reports for that glyph; the two paths simply disagree. Ruled out as the source of 1.604735, for all ten digits: the LILC bbox, the raw outline bounds, the advance, the plain digit family at U+0030-0039 as well as fattened at U+E0B4-U+E0BF, and a font-build difference (LilyPond 2.24.4 ships a different-sized emmentaler-20.otf than the repo copy, but their digit metrics are identical). The markup widths group 0/2/8 at 1.468162, 3/5/7 at 1.331589 and 6/9 at 1.365732, a grouping no metric in the font file reproduces, and a two-digit string is not the concat of two one-digit widths (off by 0.102430 either way) — both consistent with a shaped text run. Closing this needs that text pipeline's metrics, not a constant. The 1.600000 rides through Staff_spacing untouched (the space-alist ideal binds here, not the 0.3 + min_dist correction), so the residual is exactly the width difference. Was -1.454735 before the boundary column existed.

midmeasure.key-cancel.key-to-next-note.why: EXACT since LilyPond 2.26.0, by the same rounding that closed barline.next.accidental-to-notehead: the sharp's skyline term went to zero. That the two closed together, both having read 0.000010, is what confirms the earlier reading that they were one cause and not two.

page.first-staff-refpoint.why: EXACT. LilyPond seats the first system with top-system-spacing's SPRING, and at force 0 a spring is max(min_distance, ideal_distance) (lily/spring.cc:219-237), so basic-distance 6 beats the ink floor -- ink above the refpoint (2.000000, the staff's own half height on this probe) plus padding 1 -- and the staff lands at top-margin + 6.000000 exactly. Lily# returned the floor alone and sat 3.000000 too high. Closing it took two steps IN ORDER, and the order is the finding: the placement had to move into the refpoint frame FIRST, because top-system-spacing aims at the staff's MIDDLE line while Lily# stacks systems by the top staff's TOP LINE. Porting the max() onto the unconverted anchor lands the top line on the value LilyPond puts the refpoint at -- measured 2026-07-22, that moves the residual -3.000000 -> +2.000000 rather than to 0. What this does NOT cover: the top spring's STRETCH under page justification (set_default_stretch_strength = ideal_distance, spring.cc:213-216). Lily# pins the first system and stretches only the inter-system springs; this probe is a natural-length page, so that difference cannot show here.

system.natural-distance.why: EXACT. system-system-spacing's basic-distance, 12, and the first Y quantity in this corpus to be confirmed rather than assumed: HANDOFF had it as 'a match' from an SVG reading at two decimals, which cannot tell 12.00 from 12.004. Measured through RecordingDocumentContext it is 12.000000 on both sides. Note what this does NOT cover: the probe is the LAST page of a score that fits one page, so the gap is the spring's natural length. The STRETCHED regime is now carried by system.stretched-distance.

page.stretched.first-staff-refpoint.why: Was -0.025482000 (seeded before the change, predicted exactly), closed to +0.000371455 by porting the chain. The remainder is NOT structural: it is the last-bottom spring's floor, and it is the same 0.044994 that system.stretched-distance carries -- see that entry. LilyPond builds ONE chain of springs per page -- top-system-spacing, one spring per system pair, then last-bottom-spacing -- and solves it against page_height_ = paper-height - top-margin - bottom-margin (page-layout-problem.cc:780-804, Simple_spacer). On a full page every spring in that chain carries the SAME force, so the top spring stretches too: measured on 2.26.0 the first refpoint sits at top-margin + 6.025482 rather than the natural 6.000000. The chain reproduces that to six digits from the source alone: (6 + 6f) + 12*(12 + 60f) + 4.544994 = 157.628268 gives f = 0.00424693, hence 6.025482 and 12.254816. The 4.544994 is last-bottom-spacing blocked at its own floor (padding 1 + 3.544994 of ink below the last refpoint). PREDICTION: Lily# currently pins the first system at its natural distance and stretches only the inter-system springs, so this should read 11.690551 (residual -0.025482) before the port and 11.716033 (residual 0) after. ★★ MOVED BY THE GLYPH-SKYLINE PORT 2026-07-28: a grob whose vertical-skylines come from its STENCIL is spaced by the glyph's OUTLINE, not by the designed LILC box its extent is (scm/define-grobs.scm:902 Clef and :35 Accidental, against lily/grob.cc:85-89 simple_vertical_skylines_from_extents which NoteHead:2595 falls back to). The two boxes differ by 0.024 above and 0.010 below on the G clef, 0.448 below on the F clef. Closed from -0.000041769 to -4.46e-7. The remainder this entry called 'the last-bottom spring's floor, the same 0.044994 that system.stretched-distance carries' was the clef's box, and both entries land together now.

system.stretched-distance.why: Was +0.089206333 before the chain was ported; the port took 96 percent of it. The remainder is ONE quantity, and it is not the spacing model: the ink hanging below the LAST system's refpoint reads 3.500000 in Lily# against 3.550000 in LilyPond. Everything else in the chain agrees to six digits. That 0.050000 was first mis-attributed here to half of LilyPond's staff-line thickness, from a figure (3.544994) that was arithmetic on a ROUNDED gap; reading the probe's raw per-system dump instead gives 3.550000000 exactly, on every system of both pages. The real cause is the notehead: the lowest note is c' with its head 3.000000 below the refpoint, so LilyPond's ink puts the head's half-height at 0.550000, while Lily# reads 3.545000. ⚠️ THE REST OF THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY the skyline seeded a nominal EngravingDefaults.NoteheadHeight = 1.0 and that wiring the LILC ink was worth 0.045000 of the gap and had not been done. BOTH HALVES WERE FALSE and the entry carried them for a session -- long enough for the HANDOFF to adopt 'wire the notehead ink' as its next move. The skyline has been on GlyphMetricsGenerated.NoteheadBlack (-0.545000 .. 0.545000) since cff877c8, the commit that wrote this why; NoteheadHeight survived only as a dead pass-through parameter through five signatures, which is what made it look live to grep. Tested rather than argued: seeding 0.550 instead moves nine ledger entries and changes this one by 0.005000 exactly, so what is left here IS the 0.005000 and nothing else is hiding under it. That last 0.005000 (LilyPond 0.550000 against LILC's 0.545000) is still NOT explained and must not be papered over -- it is a font-metric question, not a spacing one. ⚠️ Do NOT read the page.{stretched,compressed}.* entries as this same family: they were four readings of two forces and their cause was the STEM (stem.cc:519-555, a middle-line down stem shortened to 20/3 half-spaces), not the head. The system spring of the same chain as page.stretched.first-staff-refpoint, on the SAME page -- page 1 of book J, which is full. Uniform across all 12 gaps in LilyPond's dump. The predicted DIRECTION was right and the magnitude was not: Lily# solves its force over the inter-system springs ALONE (no top spring, no last-bottom spring in the chain), so the force comes out too large, but the guess of 'roughly 12.29' was copied from a stale HANDOFF figure rather than derived. Derived from Lily#'s own PASS 2 it is exact: it fills to the bottom margin with the last system's INK, leaving 4.128268 to share over 12 gaps at equal stretch = +0.344022 each, i.e. 12.344022. LilyPond instead gives that last spring last-bottom-spacing's floor (padding 1 + the ink) and lets it stretch (stretchability 30), and adds the top spring (inverse stretch 6) to the same chain. PREDICTION: 0 after porting the chain. Do NOT read this entry on the last page: ragged-last-bottom makes that page a fixed_force_solution of the PREVIOUS page's force, which is a different measurement (page-breaking.cc:565-575). ★★ MOVED BY THE GLYPH-SKYLINE PORT 2026-07-28: a grob whose vertical-skylines come from its STENCIL is spaced by the glyph's OUTLINE, not by the designed LILC box its extent is (scm/define-grobs.scm:902 Clef and :35 Accidental, against lily/grob.cc:85-89 simple_vertical_skylines_from_extents which NoteHead:2595 falls back to). The two boxes differ by 0.024 above and 0.010 below on the G clef, 0.448 below on the F clef. Closed from -0.000413686 to -4.63e-7. ⚠️ THE '0.005000 STILL NOT EXPLAINED, a font-metric question, must not be papered over' IS ANSWERED, and it was NOT the notehead: a notehead's skyline IS its extent by declaration (LilyPond dumps 0.545 for both, its outline being 0.544). What was 0.005 short is the ink below the last refpoint, which on this book the CLEF's box decides.

page.stretched.systems-on-first-page.why: MEASURED EXACT ON ARRIVAL, which is the finding: this probe does NOT catch the defect it was seeded for, and page.tight.* had to be built because of it. Everything else on this page describes how a page holding N systems is spaced; nothing has ever measured N. LilyPond prices a page against `page_height_ - min_whitespace_at_top_of_page(first) - min_whitespace_at_bottom_of_page(last)` (lily/page-spacing.cc:30-41), and those two terms are the page breaker's ONLY knowledge of the top-system and last-bottom springs. Each is `max(0, max(padding, minimum-distance -/+ translate))` (page-breaking.cc:1785-1823). On the shipping specs top-system-spacing and last-bottom-spacing both carry minimum-distance 0 and padding 1, and translate is the system's own up/down reach, so BOTH terms evaluate to exactly 1.000000 and LilyPond's usable band is 157.628268 - 2 = 155.628268. Lily#'s PageSpacing.CalcForce subtracts the MARGINS only, so it hands the breaker 157.628268 -- 2.000000 ss MORE room than LilyPond has. That is the whole of the divergence HANDOFF 2-8 records as `PageBreaker is out of sync with the chain`, expressed as a number for the first time. PREDICTION was: Lily# fits at least LilyPond's 13 and, if 2.000000 is enough for one more, 14 -- residual 0 or +1, never negative. MEASURED: 0. The prediction's bound held, and the answer is the uninteresting end of it: 2.000000 is not enough for a 14th system here. The reason turned out to be deeper than slack, and is worth keeping -- on default paper this count is not decided by capacity AT ALL. Raising the first system by up to four octaves (eight ledger steps, measured on 2.26.0) leaves LilyPond at 13 every time, so the breaker is choosing from the force each candidate page solves to, not from a rod hitting a ceiling. That is why this entry reads exact while the model behind it is wrong, and why page.tight.* had to shrink the paper before anything would bind. Keep it as the A4 control. LilyPond measured on 2.26.0: 13 on page 1, 8 on page 2.

page.stretched.page-count.why: The companion to page.stretched.systems-on-first-page: the per-page count alone cannot tell an over-filling breaker from one that simply paginates differently, because moving one system off page 1 and onto page 2 leaves the total unchanged. 21 systems at LilyPond's 13 + 8 fit two pages either way, so PREDICTION: 2, residual 0, BEFORE and AFTER the fix. An entry that is expected to stay green is worth having here precisely because it is the control -- if it ever moves, the change did something other than re-price the page, and the sibling entry alone could not tell me that.

page.tight.page-count.why: RE-MEASURED 2026-07-25 after book T was given `indent = 0`. It was the only page book in page-vertical.ly without one, so it engraved at LilyPond's DEFAULT 15mm while its Lily# twin ran at 0 (Lily# indents only for instrument names) -- the two sides were not setting the same page, and this entry's 2 was read off the indented one. Measured both ways on the same tight paper (jn-line-forces.ly, TPT and TPD): at indent 0 LilyPond takes FIVE systems of eight bars on ONE page; at the default indent SIX systems cut 6,7,7,7,7,6 over two. The six was the indent, not the page breaker and not paging. With the pair comparable LilyPond reads 1 page / 5 systems and so does Lily#, which is what this entry and page.tight.systems-on-first-page now record. ⚠️ THE OLD ZERO WAS CANCELLATION: Lily# reached six systems because the invented OverfullPenalty forbade the compressed five-system solution, and six systems then needed two pages -- an invented constant agreeing with an unintended indent. That is section 5.2's two-defects-cancelling shape. The paragraph kept below is the history that is still true of the PAGE arithmetic, which this correction does not touch. PREVIOUS TEXT: Now exact, and read together with page.tight.systems-on-first-page: at 70 staff spaces both sides take two pages and cut them 5 + 1. It was seeded at 72 where it read -1 (Lily# one page against LilyPond's two) and the three ports below closed that; the probe then moved to 70 because 72 became Lily#'s own flip point and the entry would have swung on unrelated changes. Re-measured 2026-07-22 with a one-line-per-BOOK dump after the earlier per-PAGE dump was found to be losing lines: LilyPond takes two pages for every height up to 75 and Lily# up to 76, so 70 sits five or six staff spaces inside BOTH plateaus. ⚠️ An earlier note here said LilyPond stayed at two pages through 77 and flipped at 79; that was read off truncated dumps and is WRONG. What actually happens at 76 and 77 is not a paging difference at all -- see page.tight.systems-on-first-page. History and model follow. Six systems on 72-staff-space paper: LilyPond takes two pages for every height from 69 to 77 and only reaches one at 79. Lily# reaches one page at 71 -- SEVEN staff spaces early -- so at 72 it prints one page where LilyPond prints two. Three LP-sourced divergences in the breaker, all measured: (1) constrained-breaking.cc:555 sets `inverse_hooke_ = full_height() + system_system_space_` = 7.35 + 12 = 19.35 per line, while Lily# uses `max(0.1, Stretchability/60)` = 1.0 -- a factor of 19 in the force denominator, and NOT the same formula at all (the breaker does not use stretchability). This is the /60 transcription cfdf85b4 abolished in the placement chain, still alive in the breaker. (2) page-spacing.cc:30-41 prices the page against `page_height_ - min_whitespace_at_top_of_page(first) - min_whitespace_at_bottom_of_page(last)`; each is `max(0, max(padding, minimum-distance -/+ translate))` (page-breaking.cc:1785-1823) and on the shipping specs both come to exactly 1.000000, so Lily# hands the breaker 2.000000 ss too much. (3) LilyPond's `bottom_padding_` is only ever assigned 0 (constrained-breaking.cc:621) so its term is inert, while Lily# subtracts the system's padding 1.000000 there. PREDICTION: 2 after all three are ported. If it lands on 2 with only some of them, the rest are still wrong and the entry is passing by cancellation -- page.tight.systems-on-first-page is the cross-check.

page.tight.systems-on-first-page.why: RE-READ 2026-07-25 with book T given `indent = 0` (see page.tight.page-count for why it had none and what the indent was worth). The VALUE is unchanged -- LilyPond still puts 5 systems on page 1 -- but what it means is not: at indent 0 those five are the WHOLE score on ONE page, not the first page of a 5 + 1 split. So this entry no longer says anything about where LilyPond cuts a two-page book; it says how many systems the line breaker makes, and both sides now make five of eight bars. ⚠️ The paragraph below is the account of the orphan penalty, which is still exactly right about the defect it names and is kept for that; its 5 + 1 framing belongs to the indented engraving. PREVIOUS TEXT: Closed. LilyPond puts 5 systems on page 1 and 1 on page 2 for every paper height up to 75, so the split is a property of the model and not of the exact height; Lily# cut 4 + 2 until the FOURTH divergence was found. ⚠️ ABOVE that plateau the two sides stop being comparable, and the reason is structural rather than arithmetic: at 76 and 77 LilyPond does not fit six systems onto one page, it RE-BREAKS the music into FIVE systems and puts those on one page (measured on a single-book probe: one SVG, 25 staff lines). LILYPOND-REF: lily/optimal-page-breaking.cc:139-173 -- Optimal_page_breaking::solve sweeps sys_count DOWNWARD from the line breaker's ideal, runs the full page spacing for every line-division configuration at each count, and keeps the global argmin of demerits; the page result therefore CHOOSES the line breaking. Lily# breaks lines once and pages afterwards, so that answer is unreachable for it at any spacing accuracy. Lily#'s own six-on-one-page threshold is 77 against LilyPond's 78 -- one staff space -- but do not read that as 'nearly right': the 76-77 window is a different shape of output, not a rounding. Keep this entry at 70 where both sides are in the same regime. It was not in the rod, and not in any of the three formulas ported before it: it was the ORPHAN PENALTY, charged on a condition LilyPond does not have. LilyPond spends orphan_penalty() only when lines_[page_start].last_markup_line_ or lines_[page_start-1].first_markup_line_ is set (page-spacing.cc:375-383) -- a multi-line markup PARAGRAPH split across a page boundary. Those flags come from a markup line's Prob (constrained-breaking.cc:633-636) and a music system's Line_details leaves both false with nothing ever setting them (constrained-breaking.hh:115-116), so music can never trigger it. Lily# was charging it for 'a lone system on the last page', which is exactly the shape of LilyPond's own 5 + 1, at 100000 against force-squared demerits of about 0.001 -- so that one invented condition decided every page break by itself. The old code cited page-breaking.cc:269 for it, which is where the VALUE is read from paper, not where it is applied: a LILYPOND-REF beside a formula is not evidence that the formula matches it (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (1)). Read with page.tight.page-count, which stayed exact throughout: the pair now agrees with LilyPond on both the number of pages and where the cut falls.

page.clef.first-staff-refpoint.why: Was +0.012727149; the clef is now seeded into the vertical skylines and it closes to -0.000082769. The seeded prediction was exact to the digit, and closing it needed a SECOND defect fixed: LayoutEngine's single-page path added SystemSpacing * 0.5 = 4 as the inter-system padding where LilyPond's system-system-spacing uses 1, so the clef's ink bound a spring LilyPond leaves at basic-distance. The remaining -8e-05 is the same LILC-vs-skyline sliver as system.clef-bounded-distance carries; see there. Original entry follows. Book S is book J's music moved inside the staff (b' on the middle line, up-stem stopping 3.5 above it) so that NOTHING hangs below the middle line and the deepest ink on every system is the CLEF. staff.staff.tuplet-bracket-up.why: CLOSED to +0.0000208 — from -1.700225 through -0.547717 — and all four tuplet entries land on the identical number, as this pair and its system-level twins require. ZERO NEEDS THREE THINGS, and only two of them are within reach: the seed, the stem guard, and the NUMBER'S OWN INK. LilyPond's TupletNumber is text-interface with font-shape italic and font-size -2 in the ORDINARY text font, not Emmentaler, so its 1.20045 of height comes out of the same text-layout path that leaves TimeSignature at -0.004735 and DynamicText at -0.000076. Lily# has no measurement of it. PREDICTED LANDING for seed + stem guard, with the bracket's own ink seeded and the number's not: -0.547717 on BOTH entries -- the digit's 0.627717 less the bracket half-thickness 0.08 that Lily# does reserve -- and if the two disagree, something other than the number is in play. Lily# has no glyph -- SharedRenderer.DrawArpeggios walks a parabola in four subdivisions per half wave, ArpeggioEngraver.WaveAmplitude 0.2 either side of the centre -- so PREDICTED: a centreline span of 0.400000 plus the butt-capped stroke's reach at the apex (under half of the 0.100000 line thickness per side, its exact value set by the segment slope there), i.e. a residual near -0.31. arpeggio.x.right-edge-to-head.black-head.why: EXACT since 2026-08-03, SEEDED AND CLOSED THE SAME DAY. The renderer's own comment warns about that ULP for the count; nothing states which side of it the corpus is on. ⚠️ 3.000000 IS AN EXTENT TOO -- three copies of a glyph whose LILC box is 1.000000 tall, while each copy's ink runs (-0.224000 . 1.224000), so a stacked pile's INK is 0.448000 taller than the number recorded here. Read the extent after the port, as on arpeggio.width.black-heads. READ ONCE, on AQ only: the length is head-blind on both sides -- LilyPond's dump gives AQ and AW the same y extent (-7.276000 . -4.276000) to six digits -- so the same reading on AW would be the same number twice.

PREDICTED Lily# 0.450000: SharedRenderer.DrawArpeggios draws the ticks from the spine's CENTRE (a.X to a.X + BracketProtrusion) rather than from its left edge, so the union of the butt-capped stroke rectangles is (-0.05 . 0.40). ⚠️ THIS IS THE POINT THAT CATCHES THE PLACEMENT, and the clearance point cannot: Lily#'s ArpeggioEngraver stands the bracket at columnLeft - padding - protrusion where LilyPond stands it at columnLeft - padding - (protrusion + thick/2), so the origin is half a thickness too far RIGHT while the ink is half a thickness too narrow on the LEFT -- and those two cancel exactly in chordbracket.x.right-edge-to-head, which reads EXACT. staff.staff.beam-under-notes.why: CLOSED this session by porting LilyPond's forced-direction stem shortening. History: opened at +0.95 (Lily# reserved a fixed DefaultStemLength 3.5 stem, ignoring the quanter), seeded to +0.69 (SkylineBuilder now reserves the drawn beam's outer edge via AddBeamsToSkyline), and the residual +0.69 was the DRAWN beam itself sitting too low -- Lily# placed this forced-down same-pitch beam at centre -7.5 ss where LilyPond places it at -6.81. THE CAUSE was the beam 'shorten property, missing from Lily#'s quanter. A stem forced into its UNNATURAL direction (here g at -9, whose natural stem is UP, forced DOWN by \voiceTwo) is shortened toward the staff: Beam::calc_stem_shorten (lily/beam.cc:1059-1090) returns beamed-stem-shorten[beam_count-1] (scm/define-grobs.scm:493 = (1.0 0.5 0.25)) times staff_space times forced_stem_count/normal_stem_count, where a stem is 'forced' when its head is off the middle line and its direction differs from its default-direction (lily/beam.cc:1277-1293). That beam 'shorten is subtracted from the IDEAL beam Y only (lily/stem.cc:1245 ideal_y -= shorten), NOT from shortest_y_; for BMD all 4 stems are forced so shorten = 1.0, moving the ideal from -7.52 to -6.52, which the quanter pulls to shortest_y (-6.74) and quantises to -6.81. NOTE: an earlier diagnosis in this ledger attributed the +0.69 to a dropped base_lengths_[i]/stem_ypositions_[i] grob-frame term (current_y = beam_y + base_lengths_[i]); that was disproved -- forcing candidates at -6.5/-6.19 showed LilyPond's limit_penalty fires against the UNSHIFTED beam_y with shortest_y_ = -6.74 (base_lengths_ = 0), and the shift is entirely on the ideal via the beam 'shorten. Verified: LilyPond and Lily# both draw -6.81; BMD == BMU (the pair holds). The same port matches LilyPond's shorten on tab (0.5/0/0), drums (1.0), and mixed forced beams (0.75/0.75/0.25). LILYPOND-REF: lily/beam.cc:1059-1090 calc_stem_shorten; lily/beam.cc:1277-1293 forced_stem_count; lily/stem.cc:1245.

With the clef's own left edge at the column origin that is max(clef-width, 5.0) = 5.0, because every engraved clef is under 5 ss wide -- so the clef width is ABSORBED by the max, not added. Measured on 2.26.0: an interior system (clef-only) and an \omit-time single system both put the treble clef anchor at 0.8 and the first head at 5.8, a clef-to-head distance of 5.000000 EXACTLY, and the WIDER bass clef (ink 2.683 against 2.565) prints the IDENTICAL 5.000000 (line-start.clef-to-first-note.bass) -- the pair's cross-check. THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND THE PAIR IS WHY THAT IS KNOWN: MEASURED, both twins read Lily# 7.264000000 for an IDENTICAL residual of +2.264000000. An equal residual on a treble and a wider bass clef FALSIFIES the per-clef-width double-count (that would differ by 0.118) and points instead to a FIXED +2.264 in Lily#'s clef-only prefix, width-INDEPENDENT -- the same shape of miss HANDOFF 5.2.1 records, where the pair disagreeing (or here, agreeing when a difference was predicted) is what exposes the true mechanism. CAUSE ISOLATED by instrumenting MultiStaffLayouter's line-start block (transient [PREFIX] dump on the interior systems): the clef-only case computes startX = CurrentIndent + prefixWidth with prefixWidth = the clef ink width (2.564 for treble), and springIdeal = the raw space-alist 5.0 (the FirstNoteSpring (5.0,5.0), unbumped -- s0.MinDistance is 0.2, so the Math.Max(min, s0.MinDistance) suspected earlier does NOT fire), so the first note lands at prefixWidth + 5.0 = clef-width + 5.0. That is the 5.0 measured from the clef's RIGHT ink (the prefix already reserved the whole clef width), where LilyPond's minimum-fixed-space measures it from the clef's LEFT ink with a max: note = last_ext[LEFT] + max(last_ext.length(), 5.0) = clef-left + 5.0, the 5.0 a TOTAL that ABSORBS the clef width rather than following it. So the clef width IS double-counted, exactly as first predicted -- what the prediction got wrong was the MEASUREMENT's behaviour, not the mechanism: the clef-anchor-to-note quantity reads clef-width-INDEPENDENT (+2.264 on both twins) because Lily#'s clef DRAW position co-varies with the clef width (its ink-left sits at clef-width - 2.264, so the width cancels in note-minus-clef-anchor). The residual still cleanly isolates this spring-frame defect at +2.264, relative to each side's own clef ink-left. Consistency check that the isolation is sound: Lily# draws the clef at 0.30 against LilyPond's 0.8 (a SEPARATE -0.5 left-edge-to-clef point, not this one), so the absolute first-note position differs by 2.264 - 0.5 = 1.76 -- exactly the ~1.76 ss system.slur-under-notes measured leaking through the bow under justification (Lily# first head 7.56 vs LilyPond 5.8). THE FIX (applied this session): BreakAlignSpacing.FirstNoteSpring now returns max(0, 5.0 - clefWidth) for the clef case, threading the same GClefWidth the prefix reserves, so the two cancel to max(width, 5.0) measured from the clef's LEFT ink -- the literal minimum-fixed-space arithmetic, NOT a baked constant. That put the first note at 5.000000 line-relative and this residual at -0.300000. THE SECOND PORT (defect-1, the missing left-edge-to-clef) closed the remaining -0.300000 to 0. Lily# reserved NO left-edge-to-clef space (its prefix started AT the clef, prefixWidth = clef width from 0) and drew the clef at an invented ClefGlyphXOffset of 0.30, where LilyPond seats the clef ink-left at 0.8 -- LeftEdge.space-alist (clef . (extra-space . 0.8)), LeftEdge extent (0 . 0) so the ideal is 0 + 0.8 (scm/define-grobs.scm:2091). Ported by making ClefGlyphXOffset 0.8 (its true LP value, no longer LILYSHARP-OWN -- one constant now read by DrawClef, SkylineBuilder AND CalculatePrefixWidth) and reserving it as the prefix's leading distance. That seats the clef ink-left at 0.8 and the note at 0.8 + max(clef-width, 5.0) - absorbed = 5.8, clef-to-note 5.000000 EXACTLY. The two ports together CLOSED sub-question 1: system.slur-under-notes -0.007709 -> +0.004203 (spring-frame) -> +0.000534 (left-edge-to-clef), and system.tie-under-notes -0.001883 -> +0.001469 -> +0.000442 -- both now at Pango-quantisation scale, the same named class as the slur's arc residual, not a defect. Twin sides differ in how they reach the clef-only prefix (LilyPond omits the meter on one system; Lily# reads an interior system, since it always draws a meter on system 0), verified equal -- the same documented harness asymmetry as the octave spelling.

line-start.clef-to-first-note.bass.why: CLOSED TO EXACT in two ports (+2.264 -> -0.300 -> 0), the mirror of line-start.clef-to-first-note.treble -- the SAME clef-only first-note spring bound by a WIDER clef. LilyPond prints the IDENTICAL 5.000000 (bass clef ink 2.683 is still under 5, so max(width, 5.0) = 5.0 absorbs it), the cross-check this pair exists for. PREDICTION: residual = the bass clef's ink width, ~+2.683, DIFFERENT from the treble twin's ~+2.565. MEASURED: +2.264000000, the SAME as the treble twin to nine digits -- the prediction was wrong because the prefix uses a FIXED GClefWidth for every clef, so both clefs read the identical value; the pair agreeing when a difference was predicted is what corrected the mechanism reading. FIXED identically to the treble twin (both went 7.264000 -> 4.700000 -> 5.000000, the pair holding at every stage, residual 0); the second port (left-edge-to-clef, ClefGlyphXOffset 0.3 -> 0.8) closed the -0.300000. Full account on line-start.clef-to-first-note.treble.

line-start.clef-to-time.treble.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (-0.001000 -> 0), the TREBLE half of the defect-3 pair with line-start.clef-to-time.bass. On the first (metered) system the line-start meter binds to the clef through Clef.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.52)), measured off the clef's OWN ink right edge, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance rides on the clef ink width; the clef-ONLY clef->first-note does NOT show it (max(width, 5.0)-absorbed, width-independent). Measured on 2.26.0: clef anchor 0.8, time anchor 4.885, distance 4.085000. OPENED at residual -0.001000: Lily# read 4.084000 because GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returned the advance-derived GClefWidth (2.564) for the G clef rather than its stencil right edge; LilyPond reads the stencil ink (last_ext[RIGHT] = 2.565, break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142,242). THE FIX: LineStartClefWidth now returns ClefG.Right (2.565) for the treble family too, so every clef reads its own stencil ink exactly as LilyPond does -- no advance-vs-ink deviation left. MEASURED after the fix: Lily# 4.085000000, residual -0.000000000 EXACT. (The earlier decision to carry this -0.001 to spare treble snapshots a 0.001 re-space was reversed: byte-churn is not a reason to keep a non-faithful value. The re-space is sub-visual and mostly rounds away at 2-decimal SVG precision.)

line-start.clef-to-time.bass.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (-0.119400 -> 0). defect-3 was CalculatePrefixWidth reserving a FIXED GClefWidth for EVERY clef; the wider F clef (ink 2.6834 vs the treble G's 2.565) still got the treble G's width, so Lily# spaced the line-start meter as if the clef were a treble G. On a metered system the meter break-aligns to the clef through Clef.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.52)) measured off the clef's OWN ink right edge, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance rides on the clef ink width; the clef-ONLY clef->first-note does NOT show defect-3 (max(width, 5.0)-absorbed, width-independent, which is why line-start.clef-to-first-note.{treble,bass} read exact for BOTH clefs). Measured on 2.26.0: clef anchor 0.8, time anchor 5.0034, distance 4.203400 (= the treble control's 4.085 + 0.1184, exactly the ink-width difference 2.6834 - 2.5650). OPENED at residual -0.119400: Lily# printed 4.084000 for the bass, the SAME as the treble twin to the digit (the pair EQUAL where LilyPond DIFFERS -- the cross-check that this was exactly the fixed GClefWidth). THE FIX: GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returns the real per-clef stencil right edge -- ClefF.Right 2.6834 for bass/bass_8, ClefC.Right 2.720 for the C clefs -- and SpacingRules.MaxClefWidth threads the widest clef in the score through CalculatePrefixWidth AND FirstNoteSpring (the SAME width, so the clef-only case still cancels to max(width, 5.0)) AND SharedRenderer's DrawClef flow-anchor (so the drawn meter lands where the note was spaced from, and a grand staff's staves share ONE clef break-align column -- the wider bass F governs the treble staff's meter position too, keeping the two signatures aligned). Every clef -- INCLUDING the treble G (ClefG.Right 2.565, not the advance-derived 2.564) -- now reads its own stencil ink, so both DCT and DCB close to 0 with no advance-vs-ink deviation left (an earlier plan to keep G on the advance to spare treble snapshots a 0.001 re-space was reversed: byte-churn is not a reason to keep a non-faithful value). MEASURED after the fix: Lily# 4.203400000, residual -0.000000000 -- EXACT. Impact: bass/alto/C line-start meters and their metered first notes move ~0.12 right; treble meters move +0.001 (mostly rounds away at 2-decimal SVG precision); snapshots change wherever any clef appears (grand staves included).

note-to-note.quarter.why: EXACT from the moment it was opened, and opened to fill a hole rather than to chase a defect: every other point in this corpus measures FROM something -- barline.next.* from a bar line, line-start.* from the prefix -- so plain note-to-note spacing, the commonest distance on any page, had never been compared at all. Ragged (two measures, one system, which LilyPond and Lily# alike keep at natural width per constrained-breaking.cc:142-148), so this reads the spring's IDEAL and is paper-independent. Paired with note-to-note.eighth: the two differ by exactly the spacing-increment 1.2 on both sides, which is the cross-check -- a defect in the increment moves them apart, one in the base moves them together, and Lily# reproduces both. One pitch throughout so no stem-direction correction and no skyline nesting enters, leaving the duration space alone. WHY IT WAS OPENED: to test whether Lily#'s duration space explains justified.first-system.heads, the line breaker putting 4 bars on a system where LilyPond puts 5. It does not -- the ideals agree to nine digits. Together with the refuted esw hypothesis recorded on that entry, both the IDEAL and the MINIMUM are now eliminated as causes and the disagreement is in the breaker itself.

note-to-note.eighth.why: The eighth-note half of the note-to-note pair, exact from the start. Its value is note-to-note.quarter's less the spacing-increment 1.2 (2.504200 against 3.704200) on both sides; keeping both is what distinguishes a wrong increment from a wrong base. Note the quarter gap here is 3.704200, not score A's 3.002245: the common-shortest-duration of the piece is an eighth here and a quarter there, and the whole scale rides on it (spacing-spanner.cc calc_common_shortest_duration) -- the two probes agreeing on that is itself part of what these points check. Full account on note-to-note.quarter.

note-to-note.across-barline.why: EXACT from the moment it was opened (Lily# 3.772771429 against a LilyPond value recorded to six digits, so the 4.29e-7 is the rounding of the record and not a gap). The third of the plain note-to-note points, and the one that carries the BAR LINE: the two gaps inside a measure being exact leaves this one measuring what a bar line costs a line's total, which is the quantity a line breaker sums. Rendered on 2.26.0: last head of bar 1 at 23.506000, bar line ink 26.188771..26.378771, first head of bar 2 at 27.278771. It was opened to test whether the bar line explains justified.first-system.heads -- Lily# putting 4 bars on the first system where LilyPond puts 5. It does not. With the duration space, the note-to-note minimum, the line width, the three extra demerit terms and the DP's shape all eliminated before it, what is left is that the BREAKER's own per-measure spring totals may not equal the spacing the layout renders -- they are computed on a separate path (SystemBreaker.ComputeMultiStaffSpringData), and section 5.4's rule that the two spring systems and the break gate must agree is asserted for the springs but not for a line's TOTAL.

compressed.line-start.time-to-first-note.why: EXACT (the 4.63e-7 is the rounding of LilyPond's own six-place 3.694465). CLOSED 2026-07-25 by TWO things, and it needed both. (1) THE PAIR WAS MEASURING DIFFERENT MUSIC. This probe's Lily# side had the fixture's three phrases flattened into one melody block, and Lily# resets the relative frame at every phrase reference (Svg/Collector/RelativeResetMarker), so `slurs` opens on the c nearest C4 = c' in the fixture but continues the relative chain from the a that ends `ties` when inlined -- and the nearest c to a' is c''. Bars 4 to 8 were engraved an OCTAVE UP, which flips their stems DOWN, and that alone accounted for 0.314107 ss of natural width: the note-to-bar-line stem correction (note-spacing.cc:288-301 different_directions_correction, halved at :299-300) came out NEGATIVE where LilyPond's is positive (bar 4 measured -0.236707 against LilyPond's +0.236700 -- a clean sign flip), and a stem-DOWN first note after a bar line earns an optical correction that a stem-up one does not (staff-spacing.cc:55, `d == DOWN` only), widening the bar-line-to-first-note springs of bars 4 to 8 by 0.011 to 0.171. THE LESSON, because this was very nearly written up as a spacing defect: a Lily# probe source that INLINES a fixture's phrases is not that fixture's music. (2) THE COMPRESSIBILITY PORT. spring.cc:131-159's setters assign one field and call update_blocking_force only, so a note spring keeps the compressibility Spacing_spanner::note_spacing gave it, fraction * (duration_space - increment); Lily# had been rebuilding the spring through its defaulting constructor and getting ideal - min instead. With the pair fixed but the old compressibility this point would still read about -0.0007 (arithmetic from the measured overflow, not separately re-measured): the line's total compressibility is what converts the overflow into the solved force, and the line start gives up 0.8 * |force|. ALSO RETRACTED: the long-standing claim that 'the natural widths agree to 2e-5, decomposed column by column' per probes/ties-slurs-breaks-ragged.ly. That control omits the final bar line this score carries, so it too measured different music (its 101.907014 is exactly the real natural 102.807014 minus 0.900000), and with the final bar line in place LilyPond will not keep the eight bars on one ragged line at all. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and how to read LilyPond's springs at all (they are settable but not readable from Scheme): probes/compressed-line-force.ly engraves this music twice, ragged on a wide line (CLW) and justified (CLJ), so CLW - CLJ is |force| * inverse_compress_strength per spring and nothing else. LilyPond's natural 102.807014 against the 102.429921 line overflows by 0.377093 and solves force -0.006918750; dividing the per-spring yields by it gives 0.800000 at the line start, 1.698045 quarter-to-quarter, 2.898045 for a half and 0.400000 bar-line-to-note, summing to 54.701125. WHY THE POINT EXISTS: every other line-start point in this corpus is read at force 0, where Spring::length picks the STRETCH strength and neither the line start's fixed distance nor any compressibility is observable at all. Keep it. OLD MECHANISM NOTE, kept so it is not re-derived: the line start's own spring was never the disagreement -- both sides build ideal 2.000000 prefix-relative, min_distance 7.485000, compressibility 0.800000 (LineStartColumnTests.MeteredLineStart_SpringIsLilyPonds), and the 0.3 + min_dist floor of staff-spacing.cc:210-220 is what makes that 0.8 rather than 1.0. The fixture is test/ties-slurs, whose snapshot shares this regime.

note-to-note.half.why: EXACT from the moment it was opened, and opened to fill a hole the corpus did not know it had: every note-to-note point before this one was a QUARTER or an EIGHTH against a BLACK notehead. A half gap is not the quarter's plus the spacing-increment 1.2 -- it is 1.273200 more, because Note_spacing adds the LEFT column's head width and a half notehead is 1.377400 against the black head's 1.304200. So this point reads a glyph metric in the spacing path that nothing else does, and a defect in the half head's ink would move it while leaving every other note-to-note point exact. Measured 4.275445 on both sides; the same value falls out of the ties-slurs decomposition (probes/ties-slurs-breaks-ragged.ly, columns 23 to 24).

note-to-note.quarter-shortest.why: EXACT, and the PAIR against note-to-note.quarter: the same quarter-to-quarter gap, 3.002245 here against 3.704200 there, differing only in what the score's OTHER notes are. Spacing_spanner::find_shortest does not use the shortest note in the score; it takes the most common per-measure shortest and averages it with base-shortest-duration (1/8). NN's most common shortest IS 1/8, so its average is 1/8 again and the averaging is INVISIBLE there -- which means every duration-space point in this corpus was measured in the one regime where that step does nothing. Here the most common shortest is 1/4, global_shortest is 3/16, and a quarter's ratio is 4/3: (2 + log2 4/3) * 1.2 - 1.2 + 1.304200 = 3.002245. Lily# reproduces it to nine digits, so its port of the averaging is right and not merely untested. Section 5.2.1 item 4: exact is not the same as correct, but exact in a regime the corpus never entered is new information.

note-to-rest.half-rest.why: EXACT. Every rest point in this corpus measures a rest against a BAR LINE (F, barline.prev.whole-rest, barline.next.whole-rest); none has ever measured a note against a REST, i.e. a rest as the RIGHT-hand column of a spring. The prediction written before the measurement was that it equals note-to-note.quarter-shortest, since the space is decided by the LEFT column's duration and head width and the rest contributes only its left reach -- and it does, to six digits. That makes the point a guard rather than a discovery: a rest box that started paying its own way on the left would move this one and nothing else.

barline.prev.half-rest.why: EXACT. The closing side of the same measure, against barline.prev.whole-rest (5.598045) as the control: the two differ by exactly the rests' own ink, so the pair says the item-to-bar-line path reads the REST STENCIL's width and not a nominal box. GlyphMetrics.RestWidth / RestHeight are two of the unsourced nominal constants LpProvenanceTests still carries (handoff section 5.2.1 item 1), so this is the point that would catch them if the half rest's box were the nominal one.

justified.first-system.heads.why: CLOSED 2026-07-25 by 4bf72e9e (the break gate priced beamed notes with a flag) together with the removal of the invented OverfullPenalty -- both are needed, and neither alone moves it. The gate built its springs through a MeasureLayouter whose beam predicate was never set, so a beamed eighth took a skyline minimum of 2.532200 instead of 1.704200 and the merge_springs headroom (minimum + 0.3) lifted its IDEAL from LilyPond's 2.504200 to 2.832200 -- +0.984029 per bar of this music, so five bars needed 98.389000 where 95.844900 was available and the gate could not see LilyPond's five-bar first system as a natural fit. With the fix the gate reads LilyPond's own 18.693771 per bar, solves the five-bar line at force +0.0256 (stretched, as LilyPond's is) and cuts 5,5,6 -- but only once OverfullPenalty is gone, because the six-bar third line is compressed and the penalty priced it at 50000 x |force|. Measured (jn-line-forces.ly, JNN/JNJ). ⚠️ THE HYPOTHESIS RECORDED BELOW WAS WRONG, and is kept because being wrong in a stated direction is what made it testable: GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 makes the note-to-note minimum 0.2 too wide, which makes ideal - min SMALLER, the stretched line's force LARGER and a four-line solution look WORSE -- the opposite sign to the split actually seen. It is still an invention (handoff section 2H) and still wants removing; it was simply not this. PREVIOUS TEXT: OPEN. How many notes the LINE BREAKER puts on the first system of a justified score: LilyPond 5 bars (30 heads), Lily# 4 (24). This was opened as the precondition for a justified note-to-note pair -- on a justified line the slack is shared in proportion to inverse_stretch_strength = ideal - min, so the note-to-note MINIMUM is finally observable (every other point in this corpus is ragged-right, i.e. at force 0, where minima are never consulted) -- and it immediately caught the two engravers laying the music out differently. The gap points that were to sit beside it were held back: with 4 bars sharing the width LilyPond gives 5, Lily#'s first-system gaps read 4.909926 and 3.107063 against 3.765697 and 2.534949, and recording those as note-to-note residuals would attribute a line-breaking disagreement to note spacing -- the exact shape section 5.2 forbids. HYPOTHESIS to test when this is worked, not a claim: Lily#'s note-to-note minimum is 0.2 too wide (GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 standing in for the boxes' extra-spacing-width, probe N2N: LilyPond's column distance for two same-pitch quarter heads is 1.504200 where Lily# computes 1.704200), and since inverse_stretch_strength is ideal - min, too large a minimum means too little stretchability, which is exactly the input the breaker's force and demerits are computed from. If so this point closes together with that fix rather than needing one of its own. Measured on the DEFAULT page on both sides -- LilyPond's A4 with 10mm margins is 102.429921 to the final bar line, LayoutOptions.Default 102.429925 -- since unlike every other point here a justified one is paper-dependent.

justified.note-to-note.quarter.why: SEEDED 2026-07-25, the moment justified.first-system.heads went exact and the two engravers finally put the same five bars on this system. The quarter gap on a JUSTIFIED line, read from the same JN dump that gives the head count: `bar= 1 n=30 first= 8.585000 quarter 3.765697 eighth 2.534949`. Its ragged twin note-to-note.quarter is exact at 3.704200, so this point sees only what justification adds. It opened EXACT (+5.3e-8, with the eighth at -4.7e-7 — Pango-quantisation scale), which is a result worth recording for what it REFUTES. ⚠️ PREDICTION WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND WRONG: that this pair would be the ledger key for removing GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4, on the reasoning that a justified line shares slack in proportion to inverse_stretch_strength = ideal - min and so is the first point here that can see a spring's MINIMUM. It cannot. LilyPond's own note_spacing sets `inverse_stretch_strength = fraction * max (0.1, len - min)` with min = the spacing INCREMENT, not the skyline minimum (lily/spacing-basic.cc; SpacingRules.CreateSpring carries the same REF), so a stretched line never consults the skyline minimum at all and MinItemGap is invisible in this regime. The knob binds only where a spring is compressed ONTO its minimum, so the key that removal needs is a COMPRESSED note-to-note point, which this corpus still does not have. What this pair does pin is that justification itself is exact once both sides break alike.

justified.note-to-note.eighth.why: The eighth gap of the same justified line, from the same dump, and the pair with justified.note-to-note.quarter: both springs stretch on ONE solved force, so their residuals must move together. Both opened exact (-4.7e-7 here, +5.3e-8 there). The eighth is the more sensitive of the two — its ideal is smaller, so any error in a spring's stretchability is a larger share of it — which is why both were recorded rather than one, and why their agreeing at 1e-7 is what says the stretch model is right rather than cancelling. See justified.note-to-note.quarter for the prediction this pair REFUTED (that it would be the key for GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4: a stretched line never consults the skyline minimum, so that knob is invisible here and its key must be a COMPRESSED point).

compressed.note-to-note.quarter.why: CLOSED the day it opened, by the port it was opened for: GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 is gone from the note-to-note path and the gap is built the way LilyPond builds it -- each grob's extra-spacing-width folded into its own spacing box (separation-item.cc:166-179), the spring minimum taken as the padding-free skyline distance with skyline-vertical-padding 0.08 (note-spacing.cc:78-83), and the ROD as that distance plus the spacing spanner's padding 0.1 (spacing-spanner.cc:315-316 into separation-item.cc:56). Lily# now reads 1.604200000 against LilyPond's 1.604200. The invented knob was 0.4 of gap on 1.304200 of ink; the port is 0.1 + (0.1 + 1.304200 + 0.1), which is the same number reached from LilyPond's own two steps instead of one made-up one. HISTORY, kept because it is how the point came to be right: The note-to-note gap of a line squeezed until the ROD binds, which is the only regime in which that floor is observable. ⚠️ FIRST MEASURED WRONG, and the correction is the point: with middle C as the pitch LilyPond read 1.956300, and that is not the head-to-head minimum at all -- c' in a treble staff carries a LEDGER LINE, a ledger sticks out past the head on both sides, and it joins the column's horizontal-skylines like any other ink. The probe was measuring the unported ledger geometry (handoff section 2E) on top of the minimum. On g', which sits on a staff line and has no ledger, LilyPond saturates at 1.604200 -- exactly the rod probe N2N records -- for every width from 19.916929 down to 12.519213, and the dumped rods on every column read 1.604200 to the digit. The entry is read at 30mm (17.071654 ss), inside that plateau. SEEDED 2026-07-25. The note-to-note gap of a line squeezed until every spring sits on its MINIMUM -- the only regime in which a spring minimum is observable, and therefore the ledger key that removing GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 has to move. Ragged points read ideals at force 0; the justified pair reads a stretched line, whose inverse_stretch_strength LilyPond builds from the spacing INCREMENT and not from the skyline minimum (lily/spacing-basic.cc), which is why both of those opened exact and neither can see this. MEASURED: LilyPond's gap for this bar falls 3.048125 -> 2.037936 as the line narrows and then STOPS at 1.956300 for every width from 19.916929 down to 12.519213, so the entry is read at 30mm (17.071654 ss), inside the plateau. ⚠️ PREDICTION WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND WRONG: that it would saturate at the ROD, 1.604200, measured on probe N2N as the hard floor under the spring minimum 1.504200. It saturates 0.352100 above that, so the floor that actually binds a compressed line is NOT the rod N2N reads, and what sets it is not yet identified -- that is the open question this entry carries, and it must be answered before MinItemGap is touched, because a port aimed at 1.604200 would be aimed at the wrong number.

staff.tab-pair.staff-staff-inside.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. WHAT UNIT A STAFF-TO-STAFF DISTANCE IS IN when the lower staff is a TAB staff. LilyPond's TabStaff sets StaffSymbol.staff-space = 1.5 for every string count (ly/engraver-init.ly), so a six-string tab staff's LINES span (6-1) * 1.5 = 7.500000 against a notation staff's 4.000000 -- pinned exact by tab.staff.line-span.six-string. The open question was what that does to the DISTANCE above it, and the two candidate answers were nearly a factor of two apart: (a) Align_interface works between VerticalAxisGroup REFERENCE POINTS and staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance is in the PAGE's staff spaces, so the refpoint distance is 9.000000 whatever the lines do; or (b) the distance is measured from the staff's EDGES or in its own space, and a taller staff pushes the pair apart. PREDICTION, written before running: (a), 9.000000 to six digits, with staff.notation-pair.staff-staff-inside as the control. FALSIFIER: 10.750000 = 9 + (7.5 - 4)/2, which would mean LilyPond spaces from the edges and Lily#'s nominal-height arithmetic is accidentally right. THE PREDICTION HELD: measured 9.000000 on both books, and the two are equal to the digit, so the tab staff's extra 3.5 staff spaces of lines change the distance by nothing. ⚠️ THE FLOOR DOES NOT BIND, which is what makes this a reading of the SPEC rather than of the ink: both books came back at exactly the basic-distance rather than above it (the dump also reports the tab staff's own ink below its refpoint as 3.800000 = 7.6/2, i.e. the 7.5 span widened by half a line thickness at each edge and centred on the middle line -- the refpoint really is staff position 0). ⇒ THE FORK TOOK BRANCH (a), so the island is real: Lily# subtracts a flat nominal 4.000000 for the pair's span (MultiStaffLayouter.GapSpan, gated by IsSpecSpacedRowBoundary so only a text-row boundary takes the refpoint frame), which puts a tab pair's refpoints at 9 + (7.5 - 4)/2 = 10.750000. ⚠️ MEASURED PRICE OF THE FIX: removing that gate moves 20 snapshots -- 17 tab and 3 ossia -- which is the '~20 snapshots' HANDOFF has attached to this island for several sessions. THIS ENTRY IS THE KEY THAT JUSTIFIES THAT REBASE (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (3)); it did not exist before, which is why the island kept being deferred. ⚠️ Keep staff.notation-pair.staff-staff-inside exact while this closes, or the fix moved the wrong thing. ---- CLOSED THE SAME DAY, by the port it was opened for: MultiStaffLayouter.GapSpan asks RefpointSpanToGap for EVERY group boundary now instead of only where a text row is involved, and IsSpecSpacedRowBoundary -- the gate that selected between the two frames -- is gone with it. 9.000000 on both sides, and the control did not move. THE 20 SNAPSHOTS MOVED and are approved against this entry. ⚠️ AN OSSIA PAIR IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS and must not be read as if it were: its span is right now, but the caller still multiplies the gap by OssiaScaleFactor, which LilyPond has no counterpart for -- book OSSD (added the same day, an ossia-sized staff under an ordinary one) reads 9.000000 exactly like this one and like the notation control, so LilyPond scales the STAFF and not the distance. That leaves an ossia pair short by the scale alone, and it is a separate named quantity. ⚠️ OSSD IS NOT YET A LEDGER PAIR: it puts the small staff BELOW, while Lily#'s `ossia` renders ABOVE the staff it decorates, so the two sides are not the same arrangement (HANDOFF 5.0, traps 5 and 6). The ossia entry wants a book with the small staff above; what OSSD establishes is the LilyPond FACT that the distance is unscaled.

page.tab-only.first-staff-refpoint.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. WHERE A TAB STAFF SITS ON THE PAGE, which is the question staff.tab-pair.staff-staff-inside asked one frame in. That entry measured a distance BETWEEN two staves of one system and found it 9.000000 whatever the lower staff's line span is; this one measures the PAGE's own anchor against a staff that is not four staff spaces tall. Book TABL is ONE six-string tab staff and many systems, so every distance in it is the page's and none of it is Align_interface's. tab.staff.line-span.six-string.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (-1.000000 -> 0). The DEFECT half of the tab string-spacing pair, against tab.staff.line-span.four-string as CONTROL. LilyPond's TabStaff sets StaffSymbol.staff-space = 1.5 for EVERY string count (ly/engraver-init.ly), so a six-string tab staff spans (6-1) * 1.5 = 7.500000 line centre to line centre; measured on 2.26.0 as staffY -7.600000..0.000000, the 7.6 being that 7.5 widened by half a line thickness at each edge (probe line-start-mindist.ly score CGT). Lily# instead TAPERS the spacing by string count -- EngravingDefaults.TabStringSpace returns 1.5 below five strings, 1.4 at five and 1.3 at six -- so it spans 5 * 1.3 = 6.500000, a full staff space short. The stated reason for the taper is that a five- or six-string staff should not grow too tall, which is a Lily# aesthetic judgement and not a LilyPond quantity; it also works AGAINST Lily#'s own (ratified, HANDOFF section 3) larger fret digits, whose 1.7875 height already overlaps a 1.3 string gap and is what the white occluding background exists to hide. The control lands on 1.5 by accident -- Lily#'s taper happens to agree with LilyPond below five strings -- which is what isolates the taper rather than the tab staff as a whole. THE FIX: TabStringSpace returns 1.5 for every string count, LilyPond's one value; the parameter is kept and deliberately unused so each call site says the spacing does not depend on it. MEASURED after: Lily# 7.500000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT, with the four-string control unmoved at 0 -- the fix moved the taper and nothing else. Impact: five- and six-string tab staves grow (a six-string staff 6.5 -> 7.5 tall), which also gives the deliberately larger fret digits more room; every five- or six-string tab snapshot re-bases.
