Unlike a pitched clef, whose ink starts at the grob origin (ext-left 0), the percussion glyph's ink begins 0.67 ss RIGHT of its origin. Rendered on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score DCP): CLEF anchor 0.13, ext (0.67 . 2.0) => ink-left 0.8 (the LeftEdge->clef offset every clef shares), ink-right 2.13; the meter binds 1.52 off that ink right edge => TIME at 3.65, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance is 3.65 - 0.13 = 3.520000. OPENED at residual +0.565000 (predicted to the digit before measuring): Lily# reserved GClefWidth (2.565) for the percussion clef via LineStartClefWidth's fallback AND drew the glyph at its origin (x + ClefGlyphXOffset) without the 0.67 ink-left offset, so its clef anchor sat at 0.8 (not 0.13) and its time flowed to 0.8 + 2.565 + 1.52 = 4.885 => the twin read 4.085 (the treble value), residual 4.085 - 3.52 = +0.565 -- EQUAL to the treble twin, the cross-check that both the width AND the origin were the fixed-treble approximation. THE FIX (two threaded quantities): (1) GlyphMetricsGenerated now carries ClefPercussion (LILC bbox 0.67,-1.0,2.0,1.0, extracted from the font like every other clef) and GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returns its ink WIDTH ClefPercussion.Right - Left = 1.33 (not the 2.565 fallback), so the shared clef column and the meter it break-aligns reserve the real width; (2) GlyphMetrics.ClefInkLeft returns ClefPercussion.Left 0.67 and SharedRenderer.DrawClef draws the glyph at x + ClefGlyphXOffset - ClefInkLeft, shifting the percussion origin to 0.13 so its ink-left lands on the shared 0.8 column exactly as LilyPond places it. Both are no-ops for the pitched clefs (ink-left 0). MEASURED after: Lily# 3.520000000, residual -0.000000000 EXACT. Impact: the percussion line-start meter and metered first note move ~1.235 LEFT (the over-reserved 2.565 - 1.33) and the percussion clef GLYPH shifts 0.67 left onto its true ink column; snapshots with a percussion clef (drum-groove) re-base. This closes defect-3 for every clef family.

line-start.time-signature-cross-staff-al.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (was ~3.05, now 0). Cross-staff meter alignment in a grand staff whose staves carry DIFFERENT keys (upper transposed to D major = 2 sharps, lower concert C major = none). LilyPond break-aligns the TimeSignature into ONE column spanning both staves -- the KeySignature break-align GROUP extent is the union across staves (break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142, g->extent(g,X_AXIS) over the group; :242 offsets the next column from extents[idx][RIGHT], the union RIGHT), so both meters print PAST the WIDEST key, at the same x. RENDERED on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score TSA): both TIME grobs at x=7.6534 (CLEF 0.8, the shared KEY column 4.3034 even for the empty lower key, HEAD 11.3534) -- spread 0. This is a METRIC-FREE probe: it compares two glyph anchors in the SAME render, depending on no ink width, so LP's 0 is exact by alignment, not a measured distance. BEFORE the fix Lily# spaced each staff's meter off its OWN key, so the concert staff's meter sat ~3.05 LEFT of the transposed staff's (its fixture transpose-multistaff read upper 8.05 vs lower 5.0) -- the fixture comment even claimed 'Verified against LilyPond', falsified by rendering LP. THE FIX: SharedRenderer draws every staff's meter at the system-wide MAX of the per-staff meter x (sharedTimeX = the widest key's column), so a same-key score is byte-identical and only differing-per-staff-key scores re-align. MEASURED after: Lily# spread 0.000000, EXACT. The absolute meter x also now matches LP (see line-start.clef-to-time.keyed): the KeySigTrailingGap 0.4 that DrawKeySignature once added to the drawn column, but the break-align reservation omitted, was removed so draw and reserve are one key-ink-measured model.

line-start.clef-to-time.keyed.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (+0.4 -> 0). Clef -> time on a KEYED staff (D major, 2 sharps): the meter binds through the KEY, not the clef -- KeySignature.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.15)) off the key's ink RIGHT edge, no pad. Rendered on 2.26.0: CLEF 0.8, KEY 4.185 (ext 2.2), TIME 7.535 => clef->time 6.735. The Lily# meter drew a KeySigTrailingGap 0.4 further right than the layout reserved -- a draw-vs-reserve split (SS 5.2.1(2)): DrawKeySignature returned key-ink + 0.4 for the meter to flow from, while BreakAlignSpacing reserved the note column off key-ink alone. THE FIX: the drawn time column (SharedRenderer.sharedTimeX) now uses KeySignatureInkWidth (the ink alone, = the reservation), and DrawKeySignature's now-dead +0.4 return was dropped. MEASURED after: Lily# 6.735000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT -- confirming Lily#'s key ink width already matches LP's 2.2, so the 0.4 pad was the whole of the split. Impact: every keyed score's drawn line-start meter moves 0.4 LEFT onto the reserved column (first notes, layout-driven, do not move); snapshots with a key + time signature re-base.

line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-k.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-0.095264567 -> 0 exact). The CONTROL of the KCS/KCC custom-key pair was non-zero the moment it opened -- the keyed+metered line-start time->first-note regime had no point. LilyPond: head at the meter's ink RIGHT + 2.0 (TimeSignature.space-alist (first-note . (semi-shrink-space . 2.0)), natural length under ragged-right): TIME 7.535, ink 1.700000, HEAD 11.235 => 3.700000. The residual went through TWO wrong decompositions before the PNG showed the truth: (1) 'gap 1.9 vs 2.0' -- refuted by reading FirstNoteSpring, whose time arm is (2.0, 1.0) = LP exactly; (2) 'grob ext vs Pango advance of the digits' -- refuted by LOOKING at the render: Lily# (like LilyPond) draws the default 4/4 as the common-time C GLYPH, not digits. LilyPond's default style prints ONLY 2/2 and 4/4 as glyphs (timesig.C22/C44 -- scm/time-signature-settings.scm:954-964,981-982 make-c-time-signature-markup) and every other fraction as \number markup; the C44 LILC ink is 1.700000 (extracted from the font, = the measured grob ext to the digit). Lily# drew the C glyph but reserved the DIGIT path's Pango width 1.604735433. THE FIX: GetTimeSigWidth mirrors LP's style branch -- (4,4)->TimeSigCommon.Width, (2,2)->TimeSigCutCommon.Width (both LILC 1.7, newly extracted), else the Pango digit path unchanged (barline.next.time-change-to-notehead stays exact on it); DrawTimeSignature's invented flat 2.0 return replaced by the same widths. Every 4/4 first system's notes move +0.095264567 right (snapshot re-base, justified by this key and cut-common going exact).

system.knee-beam-notes.why: EXACT, and what it settles is that a KNEE is a structural divergence that does not reach the page. LilyPond leaves only CROSS-staff grobs out of the vertical skylines (lily/axis-group-interface.cc:850-858, its own comment), so a same-staff kneed Beam and its Stems ARE in them; Lily# seeds NEITHER — SkylineBuilder.AddBeamsToSkyline skips IsKnee and BeamedItemsToSuppress skips it too, so each member keeps the per-note FIXED 3.5 stem, in the member's OWN direction (AddNoteBoxToSkylines takes note.StemUp). WHY THAT SUBSTITUTE IS ENOUGH HERE: a knee's stems point INWARD — the low note stems up to the beam, the high note down to it — so the band and both stems live BETWEEN the two heads, and the heads are the envelope either way. LilyPond's own numbers say the same: its kneed ink TOP is 8.545000 above the refpoint, exactly d''''`s head (8.0 + 0.545), with no beam above it. THE POINT IS NOT SITTING ON A FLOOR, which is what makes it worth keeping: 18.090000 is neither the 12.000000 system-system basic-distance nor the 20.285000 the SAME music gives with the knee forbidden (\override Beam.auto-knee-gap = #100, probe book KNEC) — so the knee is worth 2.195000 of vertical room and this entry is measuring the kneed envelope itself. A future port that seeds the knee's band with the wrong geometry moves this number. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN and held: exact. ⚠️ TWO FIXTURE ERRORS ARE RECORDED IN THE PROBE HEADER, both the same trap: the first control was the same shape WITHOUT the leap (so its 6.090000 was almost all d''''`s own ink, not the knee), and the first pair had 4 bars with an explicit break where Lily# fitted all four on ONE system and the gap could not be read at all.

beam.quant.over-accidental.left.why: EXACT, and it is the first ledger point on the beam QUANTER's own answer (Beam.positions) rather than on the room a beam takes. What it pins is that a beam is scored against the INK of the grobs it covers, in the BEAM's frame: the sharp on dis stands under the sixteenth's beamlet STUB, so the reading binds against the stack's inner beam over that stub's own horizontal extent — which only a scorer that walks the beam SEGMENTS can see (lily/beam-quanting.cc:194-200 add_collision). Three things had to be true together and none of them alone moves this number: the covered grob is booked as a BOX at both x edges with sqrt(width) weighting (:377-392), the x frame is the beam's STEMS and not the note columns (Lily# was a notehead width out, 1.235 ss), and beam_y_ comes from the segments and not from min(neighbouring stem beam counts). ⚠️ NOT ON A FLOOR: score B of the same probe spells the sharp away (d for dis) and LilyPond answers 2.0 . 3.5, so the accidental is worth +0.81 here and +1.0 at the right end. ⚠️ The two ends are separate points on purpose — a sloped beam's height and its slope are two numbers, and their average matches a beam that is both too steep and too low.

beam.quant.over-accidental.right.why: EXACT. The right end of the same beam, which the accidental does NOT touch: it is the slope that carries the reading here, so the pair with beam.quant.over-accidental.left says the collision lifted the LEFT end without tilting the beam into a different quant. LilyPond's control (score B, no accidental) is 3.5, i.e. this end moved a full staff space with the left one.

beam.quant.over-other-voice.covered.why: EXACT — and it opened at +0.310000 for one session's worth of an hour, which is the whole story of this entry. Lily# took 4.500000 (4 + inter) where LilyPond takes 4.190000 (4 + sit): the NEXT quant candidate, not a continuous divergence, so the cause had to be a term that flips a comparison rather than a geometry that drifts. LilyPond named it itself: \override Beam.inspect-quants forces a chosen quant to be scored to completion and leaves the winning score card in Beam.annotation (lily/beam-quanting.cc:1038-1043 force_score, :1093-1096), and the cards for this book read C 700.36 at 2.81, C 560.75 at 3.81, C 40.19 at 4.00 and NO C TERM AT ALL at 4.19. Those three numbers solve for one padding and one only: (COLLISION_PADDING - dist)^3 / COLLISION_PADDING^3 * 500 * sqrt(1.962) fits them at 0.350 exactly, and Lily# was using 0.5 — the FALLBACK in beam-quanting.cc:116 for a grob that does not declare the detail, where Beam declares (collision-padding . 0.35) at scm/define-grobs.scm:508. ⇒ The C++ default of a get_detail call is not the value; the grob's own details alist is. ⚠️ PREDICTED BEFORE THE CHANGE and held on all three branches: this point closes to 0, the over-accidental pair does NOT move (a printed accidental INTERSECTS the beam there, dist 0, which no padding change can reach), and the corpus loses the lifts that only 0.5 was buying.

beam.quant.over-other-voice.free.why: EXACT, and it is the CONTROL for beam.quant.over-other-voice.covered: the second beam group of the same book, past the whole note's ink, so nothing is overhead. LilyPond gives the same 2.81 for BOTH groups of score B (the one-voice control), which is how we know 4.19 in the first group is the head's doing and not the bar's spacing.

beam.quant.chord.left.why: EXACT. The first ledger point on a beam over CHORDS rather than over single note heads, and the only one whose job is to keep a FALSIFIED claim dead. A handoff recorded measure 2 of test/dense-chromatic as 'the chords' stem direction is the opposite of LilyPond's, LP up and Lily# down'. MEASURED: LilyPond puts all four stems DOWN, at heads (1 3 5), (2 4 6), (3 5 7), (3 5 7) — the same positions and the same direction Lily# draws — and both engines quant the beam to (-1.81 . -1.19). There is no divergence in this book at all. ⚠️ What made the misreading possible, and the trap not to repeat: the fixture's first bar holds TWELVE sixteenths in 4/4, and Lily#'s `|` is a bar line while LilyPond's bare `|` is only a bar CHECK that does not reset the measure position. Transcribed with the `|` kept, LilyPond beams the four chords as TWO groups starting three quarters into a bar — a different piece of music, whose beams say nothing about Lily#'s (HANDOFF 5.0, trap 5's family, in the one form the checklist there does not list: not the pitches and not the bar line GLYPH, but whether a bar line RESETS the measure).

beam.quant.chord.right.why: EXACT. The right end of the same beam. Both ends, because a sloped beam's height and its slope are two numbers and one reading cannot separate them — the reason beam.quant.over-accidental is also a pair.

beam.quant.chord.single-note-control.why: EXACT, and Lily# reproduces the identity. The CONTROL for beam.quant.chord.*: the same rhythm with only each chord's BOTTOM note. The stems point down, so the head at the stem's far end is the bottom one, and LilyPond answers the IDENTICAL (-1.81 . -1.19). That identity is what makes the pair worth keeping after the falsification: LilyPond is flat across it, so any difference Lily# shows between the chord reading and this one is a defect by definition, with no LilyPond-side quantity left to explain it away.

beam.quant.chord.spanning.left.why: EXACT, and the point that closed the mean. beam.quant.chord.* (A/B) is a beam over chords too, and it read EXACT for months while Lily# was feeding the quanter the arithmetic MEAN of a chord's heads — LilyPond reads one head and only one, the extreme in the stem's own direction (lily/stem.cc:1214-1215 head_positions (me)[my_dir]; lily/stem.cc:114-122 chord_start_y is last_head, which is that same head). A/B could not tell them apart because their beams sit near the middle line, where lily/stem.cc:1239 clamps the ideal Y to 0 whichever head it came from. D is the chord where nothing clamps: <a,, c, g,> spans the staff (heads -3, -1, +3) with stems UP, so the floor alone decides the left end — shortest_y = 1.5 + 2.24 = 3.74 from the real head against 0 + 2.24 = 2.24 from the mean, and 3.81 is the first quant above 3.74. Lily# answered 2.81 (residual -1.0) until BeamScoringProblem.BeamSideHead replaced the mean at every site that asks a member where its head is. MEASURED on LilyPond's side, not inferred: forced with inspect-quants toward the mean's answer, debug-beam-scoring charges L 942.03 where its own quant costs L 5.91. Found in the notation staff of test/tab-beam-slope, which only became comparable once the exporter stopped spelling that chord's octaves differently from the page. LILYPOND-REF: lily/stem.cc:1214-1215, :1239, :114-122; lily/beam-quanting.cc:1133-1137.

beam.quant.chord.spanning.right.why: EXACT. The right end of the same beam, because a sloped beam's height and its slope are two numbers and one reading cannot separate them. Under the mean this end read 2.00 (residual -0.19) while the left end was a full staff space out — the two errors are not the same size, which is what says the seed moved and not the whole beam.

beam.quant.chord.spanning.beam-side-head.why: EXACT. The CONTROL for beam.quant.chord.spanning.*: the same bar with the chord replaced by its BEAM-SIDE head alone. calc_stem_info reads that one head and no other, so LilyPond must answer the identical (3.81 . 2.19) — measured (score E), it does. LilyPond is flat across the pair, so any difference Lily# shows between the chord reading and this one is a defect by definition. It is also what makes the pair a real observer rather than one number: this control read EXACT while the chord reading was 1.0 out, so the defect showed up as a BROKEN IDENTITY and not as a constant anyone could have absorbed into a fudge.

beam.quant.tab.rising.left.why: EXACT, and the first ledger point on a TAB beam at all. LilyPond runs tab beams through the SAME quanter as notation beams; what differs is the STAFF, and everything the quanter reads is expressed in that staff's own spaces. A TabStaff's space is 1.5, so LilyPond re-tunes exactly two beam constants for it and leaves every LENGTH alone (ly/engraver-init.ly:1234-1246 — beam-thickness, length-fraction, staff-symbol-staff-space): beam-thickness 0.32 (= 0.48/1.5, the absolute thickness kept) and length-fraction 0.62. The quanter divides both thicknesses by the staff space again (lily/beam-quanting.cc:232-234 beam_thickness_ and line_thickness_), which puts the sit/hang quants at 0.12667 and the beam translation at 0.480667 — MEASURED, by reading the drawn separation of a 16th beam's two lines off LilyPond's own stencil (0.721 absolute = 0.480667 tab spaces), which is what exposed the 0.62 in the first place. Until 2026-08-02 Lily# did not quant tab beams at all: TabBeamQuant placed them with 0.6*tanh of the string contour and three LILYSHARP-OWN constants (2.4/1.4/1.6 string gaps), reading 0.297 past LilyPond on a flat group, while its own class doc claimed it went through BeamScoringProblem. LILYPOND-REF: lily/beam.cc:142-144 Beam::get_beam_translation; lily/beam-quanting.cc:80-87 Beam_quant_parameters::fill (the exp(-8*|1-length-fraction|) weighting that all but silences the forbidden-quant scorer here).

beam.quant.tab.rising.right.why: EXACT. The right end of the same beam, because a sloped beam is two numbers. This end is also the one that made the port's last term visible: with the beam translation left at a notation staff's 0.81/1.5, the forbidden-quant gap at this end swallowed the string line at -1.5 and charged 6.22 for LilyPond's own answer, which LilyPond charges nothing for.

beam.quant.tab.falling.left.why: EXACT. The same group mirrored — the strings run 1 to 4 instead of 4 to 1 — so the pair asserts that nothing in the reading depends on the direction of travel. LilyPond answers the first group's numbers swapped, and so does Lily#.

beam.quant.tab.flat-lowest-string.why: EXACT. A flat group on the LOWEST string, stems up: LilyPond lands on the outer string line exactly, and this is the reading that was 0.297 past it before the port. Flat groups are where the staff's own LINE GRID decides (the quant is 1 + inter), sloped ones where its translation does, so the two kinds are kept as separate points. ⚠️ It is also the point that caught the third staff constant: the horizontal-inter-quant scorer charges 500 only INSIDE the staff (lily/beam-quanting.cc:1248 score_horizontal_inter_quants), and a four-line staff's radius is 1.5, so 1.5 is not inside it. With the notation staff's 2.0 left in place Lily# refused this quant.

beam.quant.tab.flat-highest-string.why: EXACT. The same flat group on the HIGHEST string with stems DOWN, which LilyPond answers as the exact negative. The pair is the up/down control: a reading that had absorbed a constant on one side would break the symmetry.

beam.quant.over-stem.beamed.why: EXACT. A covered grob is booked TWICE by LilyPond: once as its own box, and once as its `stem` object — an interval that starts at Stem::chord_start_y and runs to INFINITY in the stem's direction, weighted by STEM_COLLISION_FACTOR (lily/beam-quanting.cc:401-418). Lily# supplied only the box, and BeamQuantParameters.StemCollisionFactor had been DELETED by a dead-code sweep as unreferenced (9cbb407c) — the handoff's note that it merely 'has no reader' was itself stale. Here voice two's sixteenths hang a fifth above voice one's beamed eighths with their stems pointing DOWN into the beam's path: the covered HEAD's box clears the beam by 0.76, well past the 0.35 padding, so nothing but the stem interval can lift it. ⚠️ Its own Stem grob is not a covered grob either — Beam_collision_engraver drops every BEAMED stem (lily/beam-collision-engraver.cc:179-181) — so :401-418 is the only door. MEASURED AS AN LP-SIDE IDENTITY PAIR: the same book scored again with Beam.details.stem-collision-factor at 0 answers 3.0, i.e. exactly Lily#'s reading, so the whole gap is this one supply and nothing else is mixed in. ⚠️ NOT A FLOOR: beam.quant.over-stem.free is the same beam with nobody overhead and LilyPond puts it at 3.0. The regime is real and it is worth staff spaces, not hundredths: of the sixteen books in LilyPond's own input/regression/beam-collision-opposite-stem.ly, SIX move when the supply is switched off, by as much as 5.0. PREDICTED BEFORE THE PORT and held on all four branches: this lands on 0, beam.quant.over-stem.unbeamed lands with it, beam.quant.over-stem.free does NOT move (a port that moves the control has changed the beam's own seat, not what it is quanted against), and beam.quant.over-other-voice.covered does NOT move either — a whole note has no normal stem, so that book is not in this regime at all. ⚠️ THE CORPUS DID NOT MOVE ONE BYTE: no snapshot changed, so nothing in the fixtures meshes stems. Byte-invariance is not evidence of a port; these three points are.

beam.quant.over-stem.unbeamed.why: EXACT, and the FORK against beam.quant.over-stem.beamed rather than a repeat of it: the covering note is a quarter, so its stem carries no beam, and LilyPond then weights the interval 1.0 instead of 0.1 (lily/beam-quanting.cc:415-416) — AND that stem is a covered grob in its own right, whose drawn box already spans head to tip. So this reading is reachable two ways and the beamed one only one way. Both land on the same 5.81, which is what makes them a fork: a port that books only the Stem's box closes this point and leaves the beamed one open, and a port that books only the interval closes both. ⇒ The port took the interval, and both closed. ⚠️ The covered Stem's own BOX is still not booked, and there is deliberately no point for it: the interval CONTAINS that box in y (it starts at the head's centre and runs past the tip) and carries the heavier weight, so a second booking could only be dominated. ⚠️ No override reaches the hard-coded 1.0, so this book has no LilyPond-side identity twin; beam.quant.over-stem.free is its control.

beam.quant.over-stem.free.why: EXACT. The CONTROL for the two above: the same two eighths with nobody overhead. It says the 5.81 they record is 2.81 of real lift and not a floor, and it is the falsifier for the port — a change that moves this reading has changed the beam's own seat rather than what it is quanted against. The second voice is kept as a bar of skips rather than deleted, because a lone voice would let Lily# take the stem direction from the pitch and b sits ON the middle line.

beam.beamlet.peak-8-16-8.left.why: EXACT, and it is the half of the pair that must STAY exact: the defect is on the right side, and a port that merely stopped clamping would put a second beam here too. Both sides are recorded for every book in this family because the answer is a PAIR — LilyPond's `beaming` is one rank list per side — and a rule that chips the wrong side gets one of the two right for free.

beam.beamlet.peak-8-16-8.right.why: EXACT — this was the reported defect, and it is closed. BeamDetector.CreateBeamGroup used to give an interior member left = min(count, prev) and right = min(count, next), so a sixteenth between two eighths got min(2,1) on BOTH sides and drew no stub at all. LilyPond starts a stem with its OWN count on both sides (lily/beaming-pattern.cc:50-62 Beam_rhythmic_element) and, for interior stems only, keeps one side whole and chips the other (:121-183 flag_directions): here the flag points RIGHT, so the right side keeps 2 and only the left is reduced. ⚠️ THE BRANCH THIS BOOK REACHES IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE: the two neighbours have equal counts, so the rule falls past `right_count > left_count`; the sixteenth neither starts on a beat nor ends on the next one, so it falls past the moment test; and the decision comes from `rhythmic_importance_`, a second pass (:291-404 set_rhythmic_importance). The simplest case anyone would report needs all of it — a one-line clamp removal could not have closed this point. PREDICTED BEFORE THE PORT AND HELD ON ALL THREE BRANCHES: this landed on 0; beam.beamlet.peak-8-32-8.right landed on 0 with it (had it stayed at -2 the chip would have been written as a constant 1 instead of max(count - neighbour, 1)); and none of the twelve points recorded 0 in this family moved — each is a stem LilyPond leaves alone, so any of them moving would have meant the `count > min(left, right)` gate was wrong rather than the chip. ⚠️ THE CORPUS DID NOT MOVE ONE BYTE: no snapshot changed, i.e. no fixture has an interior stem whose beam count exceeds BOTH its neighbours'. Byte-invariance is not evidence of a port; these fourteen points are.

beam.beamlet.valley-16-8-16.left.why: EXACT. The eighth between two sixteenths exceeds NEITHER neighbour, so LilyPond's gate (`count > min(left, right)`, :131-132) never opens and both sides keep the stem's own single beam. A control for the port: this is the shape a rule that always kept its own count on one side would also produce, which is why it is paired with step-down/step-up, where keeping the own count is visible.

beam.beamlet.valley-16-8-16.right.why: EXACT. The mirror side of beam.beamlet.valley-16-8-16.left, and the same control: no chip on either side of a stem that exceeds neither neighbour.

beam.beamlet.step-down-16-16-8.left.why: EXACT. The interior sixteenth exceeds exactly ONE neighbour (the eighth on its right), so the flag points LEFT and the LEFT side keeps both beams. This is where min() and LilyPond agree BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by accident: with one neighbour lower, the side min() deletes is the side LilyPond chips, so the two rules cannot be told apart here. That is the point of recording it — the port must not move a reading the two rules already share.

beam.beamlet.step-down-16-16-8.right.why: EXACT. The chipped side of the step-down book: reduced by max(count - neighbour, 1) = 1, from 2 to 1 (lily/beaming-pattern.cc:179-181). min() lands on the same 1, for the different reason recorded on the left half of this pair.

beam.beamlet.step-up-8-16-16.left.why: EXACT. step-down mirrored: the lower neighbour is now on the LEFT, so the flag points RIGHT and it is the left side that is chipped. Both orientations are recorded because LilyPond's first branch is an inequality BETWEEN the two neighbours (`point_right = right_count > left_count`, :147-148) and a port that got its sense backwards would still satisfy the step-down pair.

beam.beamlet.step-up-8-16-16.right.why: EXACT. The kept side of the step-up book — the stem's own two beams, untouched.

beam.beamlet.plateau-16-8-8-16.first.lef.why: EXACT. The only book in this family with TWO interior stems, and neither is touched: each eighth's neighbours are a sixteenth and an eighth, so `count > min(left, right)` is false for both. It is the point that says the port did not make the counts depend on the group's LENGTH — the chip loop, and the CENTER-correction pass at :161-167, both run over a four-element pattern here. ⚠️ The LilyPond probe's header claims this book gives that correction pass something to correct. It does not: both interior stems come out CENTER, and the pass only rewrites a CENTER standing next to a LEFT or a RIGHT.

beam.beamlet.plateau-16-8-8-16.first.rig.why: EXACT. See beam.beamlet.plateau-16-8-8-16.first.left — the other side of the same untouched stem.

beam.beamlet.plateau-16-8-8-16.second.le.why: EXACT. The SECOND interior stem of the plateau book. Recorded separately from the first because the two are the only pair in the family that could come out asymmetric — everything the rule reads about stem i (its neighbours' counts, its start moment, its rhythmic importance) differs between them, and an off-by-one in the loop bounds would show here and nowhere else.

beam.beamlet.peak-8-32-8.left.why: EXACT, and NOT a coincidence with the reading it shares with peak-8-16-8.left: here the chip is 2, not 1. The thirty-second has three beams and the left neighbour one, so LilyPond reduces the flagged-away side by max(3 - 1, 1) = 2, landing on 1; Lily#'s min(3, 1) lands on 1 by deleting instead. The two rules meet at the same number from opposite directions, which is why this side is recorded as well as the right one.

beam.beamlet.peak-8-32-8.right.why: EXACT — peak-8-16-8 with the gap TWO beams wide, and the point that separates 'the stub is one line' from the actual rule. LilyPond keeps the flagged side WHOLE (three beams here, two of them stubs, since the neighbouring eighths carry one) and reduces only the other side, by max(count - neighbour, 1) (lily/beaming-pattern.cc:179-181 beam_count_drul_). Lily#'s min(3, 1) left one. PREDICTED WITH beam.beamlet.peak-8-16-8.right and landed with it: a port that closed the 16th book and left this one at -1 would have written the chip as a constant 1; one that closed this and left the other open would have skipped set_rhythmic_importance, since only that decides which side a symmetric 1 2 1 peak points to.

beam.grouping.four-eight.groups.why: EXACT. Before the port Lily# drew NO beam here at all, and the residual was the whole beam rather than a misplaced one. LilyPond's beatStructure for this meter is the table entry (2 2) (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:125 default-time-signature-settings), so its beats fall at 0 and 2/8 and the four eighths beam as two pairs; BeamDetector had a SECOND, flatter spelling of the beat grid — the dotted quarter for compound meters and one over the denominator otherwise — which made every eighth its own group, and a group of one note was dropped for want of a second. The grid is now BeamingPattern.Options, the one house the beamlet rule also reads. PREDICTED BEFORE THE PORT and held: this and its first-group partner landed on 0 with the five-eight, eight-eight and two-eight pairs, and none of the six control meters moved.

beam.grouping.four-eight.first-group.why: EXACT. The companion reading to beam.grouping.four-eight.groups: the group count alone cannot tell 2+2 from 1+3, so both are recorded for every meter in this family.

beam.grouping.five-eight.groups.why: EXACT. 5/8 is the table's (3 2) (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:165-166), so LilyPond beams three then two. This is the book the defect was first SEEN in — five flagged eighths where a musician expects 3+2 — and the one that made the island worth opening.

beam.grouping.five-eight.first-group.why: EXACT, and the reading that pins the grid's SHAPE rather than its mere presence: three, not two. A port that installed an even (1 1 1 1 1) or a (2 3) would satisfy beam.grouping.five-eight.groups and fail here.

beam.grouping.eight-eight.groups.why: EXACT. 8/8 is the table's (3 3 2) (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:170-171) — note that this is NOT what the default rule for a numerator over three and divisible by three would give, since 8 is not divisible by three; the entry exists precisely for that.

beam.grouping.eight-eight.last-group.why: EXACT, and the only THIRD reading in the family: for 8/8 the group count and the first group cannot tell 3+3+2 from 3+2+3, so the last group is read as well. The short group belongs at the END, which is where the table puts it.

beam.grouping.two-eight.groups.why: EXACT, and it does NOT come from the beat structure: 2/8's structure is the default (1 1), which would break the beam between the two eighths. What joins them is the beamException `(end (1/8 . (2)))` (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:81) — a separate mechanism that beams eighths BEYOND the beat, of which Lily# implemented only the 4/4 and 3/4 entries. This book and beam.grouping.three-eight are what separated the two halves of the port: fixing the beat grid alone would have left this one at -1, and would have BROKEN three-eight.

beam.grouping.three-eight.groups.why: EXACT — AND IT WAS EXACT BEFORE THE PORT FOR THE WRONG REASON, WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED. LilyPond beams 3/8 as one group because of the beamException `(end (1/8 . (3)))` (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:104); its beat structure is the default (1 1 1). Lily# used to get the same answer because its flat beatLength took the COMPOUND branch (denominator 8, numerator divisible by three) and handed back a dotted quarter — the whole measure. ⚠️ THE TWO MECHANISMS AGREED ON THE ANSWER AND ON NOTHING ELSE: installing LilyPond's beat structure WITHOUT its exception turns this book from right to wrong, three groups of one note and no beam at all. That is why the exception table grew in the same commit as the grid. ⚠️ TWO FIXTURES RIDE ON THIS (test/beamed-rest and test/timesig-grandstaff are both 3/8), so here — and only here in this family — the corpus staying byte-identical is real evidence rather than the absence of it.

beam.grouping.three-eight.first-group.why: EXACT — see beam.grouping.three-eight.groups, and the reason it was exact before the port too.

beam.grouping.common-time.groups.why: EXACT. CONTROL. 4/4's eighths beam by the HALF MEASURE, from the beamException `(end (1/8 . (4 4)))` (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:120) rather than from its (1 1 1 1) beats. A change to the beat grid that moved this reading would have broken what was already right; it did not move.

beam.grouping.three-four.groups.why: EXACT. CONTROL. 3/4's eighths beam by the WHOLE measure, from `(end (1/8 . (6)))` (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:99). The longest exception group in the corpus, which is what makes beam.grouping.rest-inside-exception askable at all.

beam.grouping.two-four.groups.why: EXACT. CONTROL, and the one that says the exceptions are not applied everywhere they would fit: 2/4 has NO table entry, so its eighths group by the bare quarter beat, two and two. A port that beamed eighths by the measure whenever it could would fail here and nowhere else in this family.

beam.grouping.six-eight.groups.why: EXACT. CONTROL. The compound default: a numerator over three and divisible by three groups in threes (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:367-381 calc-simple-fraction-structure), which was the one case the old flat grid already knew. It had to survive the port unchanged, and did.

beam.grouping.nine-eight.groups.why: EXACT. CONTROL. The compound default again, with three beats rather than two, so a port that hard-coded the number of groups rather than deriving it fails here.

beam.grouping.common-time-sixteenths.gro.why: EXACT. CONTROL, and the only book in the family that is NOT pure eighths: the 1/8 exception does not apply to sixteenths, so 4/4's bare beat structure answers and they group by the QUARTER, four beams of four rather than two of eight. Without it a port could satisfy every other book by beaming eighths per exception and never consult the beats at all.

beam.grouping.rest-inside-exception.grou.why: EXACT — a SECOND defect, found by the control meters rather than aimed at, and closed with them. 3/4 beams eighths by the whole measure, and this bar holds two runs of eighths either side of a rest. LilyPond draws two beams, of two and three: a rest ends a beam whatever the exception says. Lily# drew ONE BEAM STRAIGHT OVER THE REST, because MergePureEighthNoteGroups joined consecutive pure-eighth groups inside the exception's length without ever asking whether they were ADJACENT IN TIME. The merge now asks (the previous group's last note must END where the next begins), which also lets a group of ONE note be carried safely to it — see beam.grouping.beat-split-inside-exception.first-group, whose fix needs that. ⚠️ 3/4 is the only meter that can show this: 4/4's exception group is four eighths, which cannot hold two runs of two AND a rest, and every other group is shorter still. ⚠️ A tuplet boundary passes the adjacency test, taking no time, which is why the separate tuplet guard beside it stays.

beam.grouping.rest-inside-exception.firs.why: EXACT, and it was the only residual in this family with a POSITIVE sign: Lily#'s single group held five stems where LilyPond's first holds two. A count too HIGH is the signature of a merge that should not have happened, as against the too-low counts everywhere else in the family, which were beams never built. See beam.grouping.rest-inside-exception.groups.

beam.grouping.beat-split-inside-exceptio.why: EXACT, and it is the HALF of the pair that could not see the defect — one beam was drawn either way, and only its size was wrong. Recorded so that a port which splits this bar in two is caught: see beam.grouping.beat-split-inside-exception.first-group.

EXACT — a third defect in this family, and the point that watches the other half of the grid port. The half measure from 1/2 holds eighths at 1/2, 5/8 and 3/4; 4/4's beat boundary at 3/4 falls between the second and the third, and the eighth-note exception beams all three straight through it. Lily#'s first pass grouped by the BEAT and threw away any group holding a single note, so the eighth at 3/4 was gone before the exception could claim it, and the bar printed a beam of two plus a flagged eighth. ⚠️ THIS IS WHY THE GRID PORT COULD NOT JUST SWAP THE BEAT LENGTH: with the beats now LilyPond's, every meter whose exception spans several beats depends on those one-note groups surviving — 3/8 becomes three groups of one and would lose its beam entirely (see beam.grouping.three-eight.groups). Groups of one are now carried through both passes and dropped only at the very end, where a beam group is turned into a BeamGroup. That is safe ONLY with the adjacency test from beam.grouping.rest-inside-exception, which is what stops a surviving singleton being merged across a rest: the two fixes are one claim and went in together.

beam.grouping.eighth-triplets-three-four.why: EXACT, AND NO CODE WAS WRITTEN FOR IT — the 1/12 exception was opened as an unported mechanism and closed by measurement. 3/4 carries a second beamExceptions entry at 1/12 (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:100), whose own comment says what it is for: 'Anything shorter by beat … we set triplets back to every beat'. A tuplet's notes are looked up by their ACTUAL length, so an eighth inside a 3/2 tuplet is a twelfth. ⚠️ WHAT THE ENTRY ASKS FOR IS THE BEAT: threes of a twelfth is a quarter, which is exactly what the bare beat structure already gives. Its whole job is to keep the EIGHTH entry — which would beam this bar as nine notes — away from a run of triplets. Lily# keeps it away by a different route (it ends a beam at every tuplet boundary), so the answers agree. ⚠️ THAT AGREEMENT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS beam.grouping.three-eight: right answer, different device. It is recorded rather than assumed because the day the tuplet-boundary rule goes (see beam.grouping.sixteenth-triplets.groups, where it is wrong), this bar has to keep its three beams — and then only the 1/12 entry can hold it.

beam.grouping.eighth-triplets-common-tim.why: EXACT. The same in 4/4, whose 1/12 entry is (3 3 3 3) (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:121) — four beats rather than three, so a port that hard-coded the count fails here. See beam.grouping.eighth-triplets-three-four.groups.

beam.grouping.triplet-then-eighths-three.why: EXACT. Two grouping rules in one bar: the triplet's run has a shortest duration of a twelfth, so the 1/12 entry ends its beam at the quarter, and the plain eighths that follow have a shortest of an eighth, so the 1/8 entry carries them to the bar line — three then four. ⚠️ THE BREAK BETWEEN THEM IS NOT 'A TUPLET EDGE': it is two different entries answering for two different runs. beam.grouping.sixteenth-triplets is the book that proves the distinction, by NOT breaking at one.

beam.grouping.triplet-then-eighths-commo.why: EXACT. The same mixture in 4/4: two triplets and then four eighths, which is 3, 3 and 4.

EXACT, and the third reading this book needs: the count plus the first group cannot tell 3+3+4 from 3+4+3. The FOUR belongs at the end — it is the second half measure's worth of plain eighths, joined by the 1/8 entry.

beam.grouping.sixteenth-triplets.groups.why: EXACT, and it is the point that retired the invention. These triplets are SIXTEENTHS, a twenty-fourth each, and LilyPond groups them by the QUARTER: four beams of SIX, each running straight ACROSS the boundary between two tuplets. There is no entry AT 1/24, and LilyPond does not thereby fall back to the beat structure — scm/auto-beam.scm:48-49 larger-setting takes the SMALLEST exception key that is still >= the tested duration, here 1/12, and counts that entry's grouping in that entry's key: (3 3 3 3) twelfths, which is the quarter. (In 4/4 the beat structure says quarters too, which is why this reading could not tell the two mechanisms apart and why the wrong one went unnoticed for a session; 6/4 is where they differ, and beam.grouping.six-four-sixteenths.groups is that book.) Lily# used to draw EIGHT beams of three, because BeamDetector ended a beam at every tuplet boundary unconditionally — a LILYSHARP-OWN rule whose comment claimed 'a tuplet is its own rhythmic group'. LilyPond has no such rule, and the guard is gone: what breaks the beam in the 1/12 books is the exception LOOKUP changing between two runs of different shortest duration, which AutoBeamCheck now performs. ⚠️ THE RESIDUAL WAS POSITIVE, the signature of beams that were broken and should not have been, as against the negative ones elsewhere in this family, which were beams never built.

beam.grouping.sixteenth-triplets.first-g.why: EXACT. The companion reading: LilyPond's first beam joins six sixteenths, two tuplets' worth, and so does Lily#'s. See beam.grouping.sixteenth-triplets.groups.

beam.voice-span.outside-span.why: EXACT — and it opened at +5.690000, which is the whole point of the pair. The quantity is a beam ONE BAR OUTSIDE a `voice { } voice { }` span, and its control (beam.voice-span.no-span-control) is the same bar with no span in the part at all. LilyPond prints the two identically: `\\` wraps each sublist in its OWN Voice context with make-voice-props-set at its head (scm/music-functions.scm:1042-1057 voicify-sublist, :666-674 make-voice-props-set), so \voiceOne lives and dies with the span and the surrounding music keeps the pitch-derived direction. Lily# asked `Voices.Length > 1` — a PART-wide question — in EIGHT places (MeasureCollector.ResolveVoiceStemDirections, SharedRenderer, SkylineBuilder, DynamicEngraver, ArticulationEngraver, TupletBracketEngraver, VoiceCollector, BeamDetector x2), so ONE span anywhere pinned every bar of voice 1 stem-up and this beam came out 5.69 above LilyPond's while the control did not move. All eight now ask VoiceDefaults.IsPolyphonicAt(voices, measureIndex). ⚠️ VERIFIED AGAINST LILYPOND STEM BY STEM, not just here: Stem.after-line-breaking printed `direction` for the twins of voice-mixed / voice-grandstaff / voice-dynamics-mid / voice-dynamics-multistaff / hara-kiri, and every stem outside a span is pitch-natural in all five while the spans alternate +1/-1. That sweep is what justified the seven snapshot rebases in the same commit. ⚠️ The reach is still measured at MEASURE granularity, and off the model rather than from the span itself — see the LILYSHARP-OWN note on IsPolyphonicAt for the one case (later voices running out before voice 1 does) where LilyPond would keep forcing and Lily# stops.

beam.voice-span.no-span-control.why: EXACT, and it was exact before the fix too — that is its job. Without this reading the +5.690000 of beam.voice-span.outside-span could have been a paper, spacing or quanter difference in the book rather than the span's reach; the two books share the beamed measure byte for byte and differ only in whether a `voice { }` span appears one bar later, so a term that moves only one of them can be nothing else. See beam.voice-span.outside-span.

beam.quant.knee.left.why: EXACT, and it took BOTH halves of one claim — the frame and the spacing under it — landed in the same commit. The old residual -0.00058644 was a COINCIDENCE: the quanter measured in the note COLUMNS' frame and the renderer drew between the stem ATTACHMENTS, which under a knee are a different distance apart, so the drawn beam was the quanted line stretched about its centre. The frame is scm/define-grobs.scm:3471 (X-offset . ly:stem::offset-callback) -> lily/stem.cc:1090-1114, MEASURED at 1.2392 up / 0.065 down (audit/lp-geometry/probes/beam-stem-x.ly), and the quanter now reads it through LayoutUtilities.StemX, the same house the renderer and the collision collector use. ⚠️ The frame alone was tried TWICE and regressed this point to +0.19 both times, because the columns it was built on were wrong: LilyPond widens a gap where a beam's stems change direction (lily/note-spacing.cc:288-293 knee_correction) and Lily# had never ported that term, so `c'8 c' c' c'''` had its last gap at 2.58 against LilyPond's 3.6784 and the least squares fitted a different slope in EITHER frame. With knee_correction ported (SpacingRules.KneeCorrection) that gap is LilyPond's 3.6784 and this reading is exact. The kneed bars of showcase/05-special-techniques stay at LilyPond's exact (0.19 . 0.81) and (-2.0 . -0.81) — every beam Y in that snapshot is unchanged; what moved is x.

beam.quant.knee.right.why: EXACT. The other end of the same sloped beam, and it is the end that says WHICH defect closed: the old residual was ANTI-symmetric (-0.00058644 left, +0.00058644 right), a SLOPE error and not a height one, and a stretched-about-its-centre line is exactly what an anti-symmetric pair looks like. Both ends going to zero together is the frame claim landing, not a height coincidence. See beam.quant.knee.left for the frame, the spacing term it had to land with, and why neither works alone.

beam.quant.knee.three-stem.why: EXACT — was +0.62, a whole quantisation step, and it closed WITHOUT anything looking at the knee. LilyPond's least_squares_positions (lily/beam-quanting.cc:551-580) has a branch BEFORE the least squares: when the ideal Y of the first and last stems agree there is no fit at all — the beam is flat at that ideal and least-squares-dy is 0, which is what makes score_slope_direction demand a flat beam (800 demerits for any tilt) and score_slope_musical charge it again. This book's outer stems are the SAME NOTE (c' … c'), so it is flat for that reason and not for a kneed one. Lily# always ran the least squares, and the middle c''' pulled the fit. MEASURED (audit/lp-geometry/probes/beam-least-squares.ly): LilyPond prints least-squares-dy 0.0 here and for `c'8 d' e' c'`, against 1.997 for the same book ending on g'. ⚠️ The pair still earns its keep: this is the reading that made the regime worth chasing, and beam.quant.knee.left — the same regime with the symmetry restored — is still open for an unrelated reason.

beam.quant.knee.no-leap-control.why: EXACT. CONTROL — the same rhythm with no leap, so no knee and every stem up, which is the regime where the column-versus-stem offset provably cancels. It must stay exact whatever the knee points do: if it ever moves, the fix broke the ordinary beam. ⚠️ It is also what makes the knee readings above attributable at all — a quanter that were wrong in general would move this one too.

beam.quant.mixed-count.rising-first.left.why: EXACT, and it is the anchored end of a beam that is NOT right — read it with rising-first.right (+0.19). PREDICTION, written before any port: Lily# gives every member its OWN beam count (BeamScoringProblem._memberBeamCounts, fed to StemCalculator.CalculateBeamedStemInfo); LilyPond gives them all the beam's MAXIMUM count for that direction (lily/stem.cc:1158 -> Beam::get_direction_beam_count, lily/beam.cc:1517-1532). MEASURED in the probe: LilyPond's three ideal Ys here are 0.26 / 0.76 / 1.26, i.e. ONE ideal LENGTH of 3.26 = beamed-lengths[count 2] 3.5 minus half the beam thickness (stem.cc:1169-1174), for stems whose own counts are 1, 2 and 2. Per-stem counts give the leading EIGHTH 3.26 - 0.24 = 3.02 instead, so its ideal Y is 0.02 and the fitted dy 1.24 rather than 1.0 — a beam steeper by one quantisation step, which is what the readings say (dy 0.81 against LilyPond's 0.62). FALSIFIER: porting the maximum must close rising-first.right and rising-second.left, must make max-count FLAT, and must leave this point, rising-second.right, falling-control and uniform-control where they are. If max-count closes and the rising pair does not, the slope has a SECOND term and the maximum was only half of it.

beam.quant.mixed-count.rising-first.righ.why: EXACT — was +0.19, one whole quantisation step, and the cause was the count. Lily#'s quanter took each stem's beam count from the stem; LilyPond takes the beam's MAXIMUM count for that direction (lily/stem.cc:1158 -> lily/beam.cc:1517-1532 get_direction_beam_count), and the count is what buys the ideal stem LENGTH out of beamed-lengths (3.26 3.5 3.6). The leading eighth of an eighth-plus-two-sixteenths group was therefore 0.24 short, the least squares fitted dy 1.24 where LilyPond fits 1.0, and the quanter rounded the extra tilt onto whichever end scored better — here the right. Ported as BeamScoringProblem.DirectionBeamCount. ⚠️ Which end moved was not the defect: the next beam of the same bar carried the same tilt on its LEFT (rising-second.left). Read the two together or neither.

beam.quant.mixed-count.rising-second.lef.why: EXACT — was -0.19, the SAME defect as rising-first.right and the same magnitude, landed on the other end. This is the second rising beam of the bar (f-g-a), the same rhythm a third higher: MEASURED LilyPond ideals 1.76 / 2.26 / 2.76, one ideal length of 3.26 across counts 1, 2, 2, positions (2.19 . 2.81). Before the port Lily# printed 2.00 / 2.81 — dy 0.81 against LilyPond's 0.62, exactly as in the first beam. It is not a repetition of that beam: it is what proved the divergence was a slope rather than an end, because the sign of the residual flipped with the end the quanter chose while the tilt did not. See rising-first.left.

beam.quant.mixed-count.rising-second.rig.why: EXACT — the anchored end of the beam whose left end is -0.19. See rising-second.left. Recorded because a beam's height and its slope are two numbers: this reading is what says the height is right and only the tilt is wrong, and it must STAY exact when the tilt is fixed.

beam.quant.mixed-count.falling-control.l.why: EXACT. CONTROL — the third beam of the same bar (g-f-e), the same counts (8th, 16th, 16th) with the pitch line mirrored. MEASURED LilyPond ideals 2.26 / 1.76 / 1.26, positions (2.19 . 1.81). The defect is present here too and does not show: per-stem counts shorten the LEADING stem, which makes a falling beam SHALLOWER (ideal dy -0.76 against LilyPond's -1.0) where it makes a rising one steeper (+1.24 against +1.0), and shallower survived the quantisation while steeper did not. ⚠️ So this point is not evidence that falling beams are safe — it is the point that must NOT move when the maximum is ported. If it does, the term is right but something else was cancelling it.

beam.quant.mixed-count.falling-control.r.why: EXACT. CONTROL — see falling-control.left. Both ends, because a control that holds only one end can be tilted by a slope error and still look green — which is precisely what happened to the two beams next to it.

beam.quant.mixed-count.max-count.left.why: EXACT — was +0.62, and this is the point that NAMED the defect. LilyPond's own comment at lily/stem.cc:1196-1202 says `\score { \relative c'' { a8[ a32] } }` must be horizontal, and that is why lily/stem.cc:1158 asks Beam::get_direction_beam_count (lily/beam.cc:1517-1532) — the MAXIMUM multiplicity over the stems pointing that way — instead of the stem's own. MEASURED: LilyPond gives both stems stem-info (-0.62 -0.11) although one carries a single beam and the other three, and the beam comes out (-0.81 . -0.81). Lily# printed -0.19 / -0.50: not flat. The two stems are the SAME PITCH, so nothing but the count can separate their ideals — this reading is the mechanism with everything else held still. Ported as BeamScoringProblem.DirectionBeamCount, and the beam went flat at LilyPond's height in one step.

beam.quant.mixed-count.max-count.right.why: EXACT — was +0.31, against +0.62 at the other end: Lily# tilted this beam by 0.31 where LilyPond keeps it FLAT. Both ends, because flatness is the claim — LilyPond's comment does not say where the beam sits, it says the two ends are equal, and one reading cannot see that. The tilt had the sign the mechanism predicts: the 32nd stem (right) is the one whose own count IS the maximum, so it was the end Lily# already placed nearly correctly, and the eighth (left) was the one it left too short. See max-count.left.

beam.quant.mixed-count.uniform-control.l.why: EXACT. CONTROL and IDENTITY PAIR for max-count: the same two stems with their counts made equal, so there is no maximum to take. MEASURED: both stem-infos (-0.02 0.76), positions (0.0 . 0.0). LilyPond answers BOTH books flat, so the LP-side difference in SLOPE between this and max-count is exactly ZERO — and Lily# puts 0.31 between them, which is therefore the defect and nothing else (HANDOFF 5.0). ⚠️ The two books are NOT identical in height: three beam lines need more room than one, so LilyPond puts max-count 0.81 lower. The identity is in `right - left`.

beam.quant.mixed-count.uniform-control.r.why: EXACT. CONTROL — see uniform-control.left. A port of the maximum must leave this point untouched: this is the ordinary beam, and a change that moves it has broken every beam in the corpus rather than the mixed ones.

beam.quant.mixed-count.peak-32.unforced..why: EXACT. CONTROL for peak-32.forced-stem, and the half of this pair the maximum-count port CLOSED. Bar 1 of test/beamlet-peaks: an 8-32-8 group clear of the staff, every stem in its natural direction. MEASURED LilyPond ideals -2.86 / -1.86 / -0.86, a clean 1.0 step per third with ONE ideal length of 3.36 (beamed-lengths[count 3] 3.6 minus half the beam thickness) across counts 1, 3, 1, positions (-3.0 . -1.81). It must stay exact while the forced pair is chased: if it moves, the fix broke the case that already works.
EXACT. CONTROL — see peak-32.unforced.left. Both ends, because the pair is being used to separate a height error from a slope error and a one-ended control cannot hold either.

beam.quant.mixed-count.peak-32.forced-st.why: EXACT — was +0.5, and it closed because the maximum-count port had a THIRD call site nobody had counted. ScoreStemLengths (lily/beam-quanting.cc:1114-1171) was still building this stem's floor and ideal from the stem's OWN beam count while the seed had moved to the direction maximum, so the scorer graded the new seed against the old ladder. With the stem's own count the leading eighth's shortest_y is -2.74; with LilyPond's it is -3.61, and Lily#'s -3.50 sits 0.11 the wrong side of it — a quant LilyPond charges STEM_LENGTH_LIMIT_PENALTY 5000 × 0.11 for and therefore never picks. ⚠️ THE FLOOR WAS THE RIGHT SUSPECT AT THE WRONG ADDRESS: the prediction below named ShiftRegionToValid, and the reader was the scorer. ★ AND THE FORK WAS MIS-DRAWN — see peak-32.forced-stem.right. ★ The arithmetic that stands, and that is worth keeping: LilyPond's ideals here are -3.776667 / -2.776667 / -1.776667 against D's -2.86 / -1.86 / -0.86 — NOT a translation, because a third is 1.0 staff space and the ladder moved 0.916667, i.e. 1.0 minus 1/12.
