beam.grouping.six-four-sixteenths.groups.why: EXACT since the one-pass port. The beamException keyed on 1/16 (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:133, (4 4 4 4 4 4)) ends this bar's beams every QUARTER; Lily# used to end them every dotted half, because it consulted the beat structure for everything that was not a run of pure eighths. This is the plainest book in the family — no tuplet, no rest, no bracket — and it is the one that said the missing half of the table asks for groups FINER than the beat, which a merge pass (which can only make groups coarser) could not reach. It was 2 beams of 12 against LilyPond's 6 of 4.

beam.grouping.six-four-sixteenths.first-.why: EXACT. The companion reading, and the one that carried the SIGN: a beam three times too long was a POSITIVE residual here and a negative one on the count. See beam.grouping.six-four-sixteenths.groups.

beam.grouping.four-two-sixteenths.groups.why: EXACT since the one-pass port. The same 1/16 entry (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:112) against a different beat: 4/2's structure is (1 1 1 1) of HALF notes, so the entry's quarter is four times finer, where 6/4's was three times. Two books, because a port that hard-coded 'sixteenths beam by the quarter' would satisfy both and then fail beam.grouping.nine-four-sixteenths. See beam.grouping.six-four-sixteenths.groups.

beam.grouping.four-two-sixteenths.first-.why: EXACT. The companion reading. See beam.grouping.four-two-sixteenths.groups.

beam.grouping.two-two-thirtyseconds.grou.why: EXACT since the one-pass port. The 1/32 entry (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:74, (8 8 8 8)) — the same defect one duration lower. ⚠️ 2/2's SIXTEENTHS were exact before the port and must stay exact: a sixteenth is LARGER than a thirty-second, so larger-setting (scm/auto-beam.scm:48-49) finds nothing for them and the beat structure answers. The entry moves the thirty-seconds only, which is why this book is written in them.

beam.grouping.three-two-thirtyseconds.gr.why: EXACT since the one-pass port. 3/2's 1/32 entry (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:90), the same rule in the meter whose beat structure is (1 1 1). See beam.grouping.two-two-thirtyseconds.groups.

beam.grouping.nine-four-sixteenths.group.why: EXACT. CONTROL, and the point that says the rule is the LOOKUP rather than 'these meters beam by the quarter'. 9/4 carries an exception too (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:144) but keyed on 1/32, and larger-setting takes the smallest key that is AT LEAST the type (scm/auto-beam.scm:48-49) — a sixteenth is larger than a thirty-second, so nothing is found and the beat structure (3 3 3) answers: three beams of twelve, which is what Lily# already draws. ⚠️ The standing handoff listed this book as divergent alongside 6/4; measuring it showed it is not. A port that applied every 1/16-and-finer entry to every short note would beam this bar in nine and fail here.

beam.grouping.twelve-four-sixteenths.gro.why: EXACT. CONTROL — the same shape as beam.grouping.nine-four-sixteenths.groups in the meter with four dotted-half beats (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:155).

beam.grouping.three-four-thirtyseconds.g.why: EXACT. CONTROL, and the MIRROR of beam.grouping.nine-four-sixteenths.groups: here the lookup DOES find an entry — a thirty-second is smaller than a twelfth, so larger-setting takes 3/4's 1/12 entry (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:100) — and the groups it asks for, three twelfths, ARE the quarter, which is what the beat structure would have said anyway. Exact before the port and after it, for two different reasons. ⚠️ Also listed as divergent by the standing handoff; it is not.

beam.grouping.common-time-thirtyseconds..why: EXACT. CONTROL — the same via 4/4's own 1/12 entry (scm/time-signature-settings.scm:121, (3 3 3 3)). See beam.grouping.three-four-thirtyseconds.groups.

beam.grouping.offbeat-triplet.groups.why: EXACT, and it is the half of this pair that CANNOT see the defect: both engines draw exactly one beam in this bar, for different reasons and over different notes. See beam.grouping.offbeat-triplet.first-group.

beam.grouping.offbeat-triplet.first-grou.why: EXACT since the one-pass port, and it is the only point that ever observed Lily#'s SECOND tuplet guard (BeamDetector's tupletInteriors, which suppressed the beat flush inside a tuplet — a triplet that starts ON a beat is already inside one beat, so an OFF-beat one was all it could be suppressing). LilyPond's end test is exact membership of the measure position in the ending moments, and this run has none: the triplet's notes fall at 1/8, 5/24 and 7/24, never on the quarter its 1/12 entry ends groups at, and the plain eighth after them at 3/8 is not an ending moment either — so ONE beam holds all five stems, straight through both edges of the tuplet. Lily# used to cut at both edges (tupletBoundaries) and then drop the two lone eighths as groups of one, leaving a beam of three. Both guards went with the port; nothing replaced them, because exact membership is the whole rule.

beam.grouping.half-measure-start.groups.why: EXACT. CONTROL for the START rule (scm/auto-beam.scm:66-79), which forbids a beam from STARTING at the half measure of a 3/N meter so as not to suggest a 6/N beat structure — but only when beamHalfMeasure is false, and the default is TRUE (ly/engraver-init.ly:880), so the first branch is always taken. This book is what makes it safe to write that rule down literally in the one-pass port: it holds the default answer at the one position where the rule has anything to say.

line-start.clef-to-time.mixed-key-grand-.why: EXACT, and it is a CONTROL for a defect that lives one layer away — raised so the fix for that defect cannot be applied in the wrong direction. WHAT IS MEASURED: clef to meter on a grand staff where only the UPPER staff engraves a signature (its part is transposed, so it prints D major = 2 sharps, beside a concert-pitch C-major lower staff). The distance therefore SPANS a key column that the score-level key knows nothing about — the score key here is C major, which books nothing at all. LilyPond dumps CLEF 0.800000, KEY 4.303400 (ext 2.200000), TIME 7.653400, first HEAD 11.353400; Lily# reproduces 6.853400 to 9 digits, because its line-start reservation unions the staves' OWN signatures (SpacingRules.WidestActiveKeyInk / ActiveKeyInkForStaff, the model built for line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed). ⚠️ THE SIBLING POINT CANNOT SEE THIS: line-start.time-signature-cross-staff-alignment is an identity (both meters at one x) and holds however wide the shared key column is, INCLUDING not at all. THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS AGAINST: the BREAK GATE prices the same line start from score.LeadingKey instead (SystemBreaker.cs:66-69, IncrementalCompiler.cs:170-174), which on this score books 6.703400 against the layout's 9.353400 — 2.650000 short, being the key's 2.200000 plus the Clef->Key and Key->Time gaps that only open when a signature is engraved. That is a Lily#-internal disagreement with no LilyPond number of its own (LilyPond's breaker uses the real spacing — constrained-breaking.cc — so it HAS no second model), and it is held by SpacingInvariantTests.BreakGateAndLayout_PriceTheSameLineStart rather than by a corpus point: its only visible consequence is a line break, and a break flips inside a 2.650000 window, which would make a knife-edge ledger entry. When that gate is fixed, the fix must move the GATE up to this number and not this number down to the gate — which is what this point exists to say.

line-start.time-to-first-note.custom-key.why: CLOSED IN TWO STEPS THE SAME SESSION (-2.745264567 -> -0.095264567 -> 0 exact; the second step is the shared C-glyph meter width, see line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-key).The defect: the same two sharps declared as a CUSTOM signature reserved NO key column, because the reservation read KeySignature.Sharps only (WidestActiveKeySharps and the KeySignatureChangeItem scan dropped Custom; a custom key is KeySignature(0, custom), MeasureCollector.Form.cs:385) while the draw walk drew the signature -- the drawn meter overlapped the first note. THE FIX: one key-width model. SpacingRules.KeySignatureInkWidth(KeySignature) is now the single source (custom = per-glyph advance sum, standard = count x advance); SolvePrefixColumns/CalculatePrefixWidth/FirstNoteSpring take the key INK width instead of a sharps count; WidestActiveKey returns the full KeySignature record, widest by ink (the break-align group extent is an ink union, break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142), and preserves Custom through mid-piece key changes; MultiStaffScore.LeadingKey replaces LeadingKeySharps. LilyPond's KCC dump is byte-identical to KCS (one key model, keyAlterations) and Lily# now mirrors that structure. The whole existing corpus is byte-invariant (standard keys compute the identical width; zero snapshots moved).

line-start.time-to-first-note.cut-common.why: OPENED EXACT as the cut-common half of the C-glyph width pair (with line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-key). LilyPond's default style prints ONLY 2/2 and 4/4 as glyphs (timesig.C22/C44, make-c-time-signature-markup); C22's LILC ink is 1.700000 like C44's, so time -> first note is 3.700000 for BOTH -- the pair's equality is the cross-check that the two C widths ride one (glyph) path while every other fraction stays on the Pango digit path. Lily# reserved 2/2 from the digit table too (GetTimeSigWidth max digit '2' = 1.4657 Pango) under a drawn cut-C glyph; the same fix (GetTimeSigWidth's LP-style branch) closes both.

line-start.ossia-key-alignment.sharps.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-3.365 -> 0 exact). The ossia (no clef on its first appearance) above a keyed main staff: its key signature must sit in the ONE KeySignature break-align column spanning the system, exactly like the grand-staff clef/time columns (break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142, group extent = union across staves). METRIC-FREE: ossia key X minus main key X in the same render; LilyPond prints 0 (OKEY anchor == KEY anchor == 4.185, for the NR fontSize+staff-space recipe AND under \magnifyStaff -- probe scores OKN/OKM). The PREDICTION written before the LP dump said 'LeftEdge -> key-signature extra-space 0.8 (define-grobs.scm:2097)' -- the dump REFUTED it: column sharing wins; the 0.8 alist entry never binds because the system-wide Clef column exists (the main staff has a clef). Lily# drew the ossia key at systemStartX + Clef->Key 0.82 off a clef that was not there. THE FIX: the drawn walk places every staff's key at the SHARED key column (sharedKeyX = widest-clef right + Clef->Key), the same expression the reservation's SolvePrefixColumns KeyX carries -- for a staff with a clef this is byte-identical to the former per-staff walk, so only the ossia moved. ALSO fixed with it, per the coordinate-frame rule: the ossia signature's INTERNAL glyph advances were unscaled (1.1 real ss inside a magstep(-3) staff -- mixed frames); DrawKeySignature now scales its advances by the staff's notation scale, matching LP's scaled stencil (OKN dump: OKEY ink 1.5558 ~ 2.2 x magstep(-3); the sub-0.1% remainder is LP's design-size font metrics, the clef-sliver family, not opened here).

line-start.ossia-key-alignment.flats.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-3.365 -> 0 exact). Flats half of the ossia key-alignment pair (B-flat major; see the sharps entry for the mechanism and the fix). LilyPond: OKEY == KEY == 4.185, offset 0 -- the same 0 as sharps, the pair's content-independence cross-check. Lily# now prints 0 on both halves: the shared key column is one expression, so it cannot depend on the key's content.

line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-concer.why: CLOSED TO EXACT (+0.400000 -> 0) by porting merge_springs. CONTROL of the tab-key pair (a tab staff beside a concert notation staff, both in C major). It opened NON-ZERO and its residual was NOT the defect the pair was cut for: the LilyPond value is 3.300000, not the single-staff 3.700000 of KCS/KC2, because the line-start spring is merge_springs (spring.cc:104) AVERAGING one wish per staff and the two staves wish for different things -- their last prefatory grob differs. Notation staff: last grob TimeSignature, (first-note . (semi-shrink-space . 2.0)), staff-spacing.cc:193-198 -> fixed 6.82+1.0, ideal 8.82. Tab staff: last grob Clef, (first-note . (minimum-fixed-space . 5.0)), :183-187 -> ink-left 1.0 + max(2.6, 5.0) = 6.0, then the SHARED min_dist floor (:212-215, 0.3 + min_dist) lifts it to 8.02. Average (8.82+8.02)/2 = 8.42 = TIME ink right 6.82 + 1.6. Two ORDINARY staves keep 3.700000 exactly (measured on a treble+bass twin: TIME 5.0034 -> HEAD 8.7034) because equal wishes average to themselves -- which is why no earlier multi-staff point could see this. THE FIX, ported literally: spacing-spanner.cc:492-517 breakable_column_spacing collects one Staff_spacing wish per staff from the left column's spacing-wishes and ends in merge_springs, so LineStartColumn.LineStartSpring now builds one wish per staff (LineStartColumn.PrefatoryGrobs -> Spacing_interface::extremal_break_aligned_grob, spacing-interface.cc:190-230, which SKIPS empty extents -- that is why a tab staff's stencil-less TimeSignature drops out and its TAB clef becomes the extremal grob) and Spring.MergeSprings averages them (spring.cc:101-129, N at once). The prediction written before the measurement -- both halves exact, no other ledger point moving -- held for this half to 15 digits and for every other point; the keyed half kept a small residual from a SECOND defect, recorded there.

line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed.why: CLOSED TO EXACT IN THREE STEPS (+7.450000 -> +0.400000 -> +0.067135965 -> 0), and the LAST step was a defect this pair EXPOSED rather than one it was cut for. After merge_springs went in, the control half (tab-concert) was exact while this half kept +0.067135965 -- and the pair's LilyPond side is an IDENTITY (TKC and TKT dump equal to 15 digits, because nothing engraves the tab part's key), so any difference between the two Lily# halves is a Lily# defect by construction. It was this: Lily# attached an ACCIDENTAL to a tab staff's notes. LilyPond removes the Accidental_engraver from both TabVoice and TabStaff (ly/engraver-init.ly:1189, :1213, 'No accidental in tablature !'), so a tab note has no Accidental grob at all -- it neither draws NOR reserves. Lily# spelled the tab part's `c,` in F# major as c-natural (accidentals are decided once per PART, before the score binds it to a staff) and let that phantom natural into the spacing: MusicalColumnLeftReach 0.100000 -> 1.234272 on every tab note, i.e. 1.13 ss of blank paper in front of every fret number, which raised the measure's own spring-0 minimum by 0.134272; LineStartSpringForLine floors the tab staff's Staff_spacing wish at that minimum (the LILYSHARP-OWN grace/lyric floor) and merge_springs halved it: 0.134272 / 2 = 0.067136, to 15 digits. THE FIX is TabResolver.RemoveAccidentals, applied to the tab staff's own copy of the voice -- the same context boundary LilyPond removes the engraver at, so the same part on a notation staff beside it keeps its accidentals and a shared paper column still sees THOSE. Measured: min_dist was NOT what moved (7.720000 on both halves before and after); the tab clef's box never reached as far as the notation staff's meter. HISTORY OF THE EARLIER STEPS: the defect half is the SAME score as TKC with the tab part opening in F# major (6 sharps). Nothing engraves that key -- LilyPond's TabStaff removes the Key_engraver (engraver-init.ly:1214) and Lily# draws no key on a tab staff either -- so the two LilyPond twins are geometrically IDENTICAL (all 13 dumped grobs equal to 15 digits) and the pair's LP side is an identity. Lily# disagreed by exactly 7.050000000 = Clef->Key 0.82 + 6-sharp ink 6.6 + Key->Time 1.15 - Clef->Time 1.52, the prediction written before the measurement, to 15 digits: SpacingRules.WidestActiveKey walked EVERY staff (tab, text row and ossia included) while the drawn walk skipped tab/text/ossia, so the reservation booked a key column nobody engraves and shoved the first note that far right of the meter it is spaced from -- a gaping hole, with no fixture in the corpus to show it. THE FIX is the break-align group itself, ported literally: one predicate (SpacingRules.ContributesToKeyColumnWidth = the staves that ENGRAVE a signature, tab and text rows removing their Key_engraver per engraver-init.ly:1214,297) selects the staff set for BOTH the reservation and the drawn shared-time walk, and both union the ENGRAVED widths (WidestActiveKeyInk -> EngravedKeyInkWidth), which is what break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142 unions. An ossia is IN that union like any Staff, contributing its reduced-size stencil (probe OKN: ossia key ink 1.5558 = 2.2 * magstep(-3) at the unscaled shared column X) -- the reservation now carries a WIDTH rather than one staff's KeySignature, which is what makes a scaled contribution expressible at all. The pair read as an identity on the Lily# side too (both halves 3.700000), the cross-check that the staff set was the whole of what differed THEN; the residual left on both was the merge_springs averaging recorded under tab-concert, closed since.

staffless.line-start.chords-vs-staff.why: CLOSED (-0.438600 -> 0) BY PORTING THE ChordName ANCHOR, 2026-07-25, and it closed at the number the point had already named. WHAT IS MEASURED: the same progression over a staff minus the same progression alone, a difference of two anchors read the same way on each side -- so the point is blind to a symmetric convention error and stays blind now that the convention is right (LpGeometryLedgerTests.ChordSymbolsAreAnchoredAtTheirInkLeft is what asserts THAT). WHY IT WAS OPEN: Lily# centred a chord symbol on its column (TextAnchor.Middle) and LilyPond does not. CS was already right on both sides -- both engravers put the first symbol on 8.585000 -- so the whole disagreement was CO, the staff-LESS half: LilyPond stands its first column on 0.500000 (standard_breakable_column_spacing's min_dist + 0.5 with min_dist 0, spacing-basic.cc:71-77) and its ChordName sits ON that column with its ink starting there, because ChordName declares no X-offset and no self-alignment-interface at all (scm/define-grobs.scm:837-855). Lily# reached the same 0.500000 spring, then hung half the symbol left of the column, and the keep-inside-line rod (simple-spacer.cc:431-432,556-560) correctly refused to let that ink cross the margin: it pushed the column out to the half width 0.938600, and 0.938600 - 0.500000 = 0.438600 was this residual to 6 digits. THE FIX WAS THE ANCHOR ALONE -- the spring and the rod were already LilyPond's and neither was touched. The symbol is now drawn with TextAnchor.Start, its keep-inside-line reach is its WHOLE width to the right and nothing to the left, and its spacing reservation is the matching asymmetric (-0.5 . w + 0.5) of extra-spacing-width. The rod then goes inert on a staff-less line and the column falls back to the bare 0.500000. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN and held to 9 digits: 8.085000000. The user was asked first, because centring might have been a deliberate divergence like the tab fret size (docs/HANDOFF.md section 3); the decision was to follow LilyPond. ⚠️ Chord GRIDS are a DIFFERENT grob and are NOT covered by this: GridChordName centres its ink in the measure square (grid-chord-name::calc-X-offset, scm/output-lib.scm:3744-3768), and Lily#, having no measure squares, leaves its chords-only sheet on the ChordName path. As predicted, meter-identity, key-identity and chord-symbol-over-notehead did not move -- none of them can see a symmetric shift.

staffless.line-start.meter-identity.why: EXACT, and it guards a defect that was live until 2026-07-25. The pair's LilyPond side is an IDENTITY: a ChordNames context has no Time_signature_engraver (ly/engraver-init.ly:703-725), so the same chords under 3/4 and under 4/4 put their first symbol on 0.500000 both times, to 15 digits -- which makes any Lily# difference the size of a Lily# defect by construction. Lily# used to book GetTimeSigWidth(beats, beatType) into the line-start prefix of a system with no staff, and that width is NOT the same for 4/4 and 3/4, so this pair would have opened at the difference between the two meter stencils. SpacingRules.AnyStaffEngravesTime now asks whether any row engraves a meter before the prefix books one. ⚠️ EXACT here means 'the meter column is shut', not 'the line start is right': a symmetric error cancels out of an identity by definition, and one was live underneath this point until 2026-07-25 -- these same scores stood 0.438600 away from LilyPond in absolute terms the whole time it read 0, which is what chords-vs-staff was opened to say.

staffless.line-start.key-identity.why: EXACT. The second identity of the staff-less prefix: ChordNames has no Key_engraver either (ly/engraver-init.ly:703-725), so the same chords in E major and in C major are geometrically identical on LilyPond's side. This half was ALREADY closed before the point existed -- SpacingRules.ContributesToKeyColumnWidth excludes a text row, the fix made for line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed -- so it opened exact, and that is the finding: it is a CONTROL proving the key column really is shut for a text row, and the reason the clef and meter columns could be fixed without disturbing it. Same caveat as meter-identity: an identity cannot see a symmetric error.

staffless.lead-sheet.narrow-syllable-flo.why: CLOSED (0.151200 -> 0) BY PORTING THE ALIGNMENT EXTENT, 2026-07-25, together with its three siblings. Lily# placed a syllable at -w/2 and LilyPond at -w/2 + he.centre, so Lily# reached past the line-start spring where LilyPond does not. WHAT IS MEASURED: adding a LYRIC row to a chords-only staff-less line must not move the first column at all, and on LilyPond's side it does not -- CLI and CO both stand it on 0.500000, so this pair's LilyPond half is an IDENTITY and any Lily# difference is a Lily# defect by construction, in Lily#'s own units, with no LilyPond text metric in it. THAT IS THE POINT OF THE NARROW SYLLABLE. LilyPond centres a syllable on the PaperColumn placeholder X-alignment-extent (0 . 1.35) -- self-alignment-interface.cc:117-176 with self-alignment-X = left-align-at-split-notes returning CENTER when the column holds no note heads (output-lib.scm:1642-1673), define-grobs.scm:2749-2750 -- giving x = -w/2 + 1.35/2. The keep-inside-line rod is a MINIMUM (simple-spacer.cc:556-560), so while w/2 - 0.675 stays under the 0.5 that standard_breakable_column_spacing already gives (spacing-basic.cc:71-77), the rod is SLACK and the column never moves. MEASURED: CLI's syllable is 0.990156 wide and sits 0.179922 to the RIGHT of its column (-0.495078 + 0.675 = 0.179922, exact); CLA's is 1.365732 and reaches 0.007866 left, a real reach that still does not bind; both columns dump 0.500000. Lily# has no placeholder: its reach is w/2, which clears 0.5 for any syllable over 1.0 ss, so the rod binds and the column leaves the floor. Lily#'s "I" is 1.302400 in its own serif at 3.2 ss, and 1.302400/2 - 0.500000 = 0.151200 = this residual to 9 digits. THE FIX is the placeholder in the lyric's offset; the rod and the spring are already LilyPond's. A raw comparison on the WIDE-syllable CL cannot do this job: the two engravers do not measure the same w (Lily#'s lyric face is ~27% wider -- "Twin" 7.587200 against LilyPond's 5.975079), so a CL point would mix the missing 0.675 with a font metric. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN, both sides: LilyPond 0.000000 and Lily# +0.151200; both held. ⚠️ IT IS STILL WORTH KEEPING NOW THAT IT IS EXACT, and not because it re-states the sibling points: it is the only one that watches the SPACING side, i.e. that the keep-inside-line rod is fed the syllable's reach FROM ITS ALIGNMENT POINT rather than from its column. A port that fixed the drawn offset and left the rod input centred would draw the syllable correctly and still shove the column.

staffless.lead-sheet.narrow-syllable-wid.why: CLOSED (0.238400 -> 0) with its siblings, 2026-07-25. It said something the floor point did not: inside that floor window LilyPond's first column is BLIND to the syllable's width, and Lily#'s tracks it. The two scores differ in one letter -- "I" against "a" -- and nothing else, so LilyPond's half is again an IDENTITY (both columns 0.500000, even though the syllables are 0.990156 and 1.365732 wide and the wider one does reach 0.007866 left of its column). Lily# moves by exactly half the width difference: (1.779200 - 1.302400)/2 = 0.238400, this residual to 9 digits, which is the signature of a grob CENTRED on its column with the rod passing that half width straight through. ⚠️ THIS IS KEPT SEPARATE FROM narrow-syllable-floor ON PURPOSE. That one could be closed by any constant that happens to push Lily# back onto the floor for this one syllable; this one cannot -- it fails for as long as the column responds to w at all in the regime where LilyPond's does not. Porting x = -w/2 + 0.675 closed both, because w/2 - 0.675 is negative for both syllables and Lily# now lands on the same 0.5 floor. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN: LilyPond 0.000000, Lily# +0.238400; both held, and the port took both to 0 as predicted.

lyric.syllable-centre.placeholder-column.why: CLOSED (-0.675000 -> 0) ON THE DAY IT WAS RAISED: Lily# centred a syllable ON its column where LilyPond centres it on the column's ALIGNMENT EXTENT, which is not the same point. WHAT IS MEASURED: the syllable's ink CENTRE minus its column, the one lyric quantity comparable across two engravers whose lyric faces differ -- with self-alignment-X and parent-alignment-X both CENTER, self-alignment-interface.cc:117-176 gives x = -w/2 + he.centre, so ink centre = column + x + w/2 = column + he.centre and the syllable's own width cancels identically. The column is read through the chord symbol standing on it, which IS the column (ChordName has no X-offset, scm/define-grobs.scm:837-855). LilyPond's answer here is 0.675000 = 1.35/2: a staff-less column holds no note heads, so Paper_column::get_interface_extent returns an EMPTY note-column extent and `he` falls back to the placeholder X-alignment-extent (0 . 1.35), 'as wide as a note head' (define-grobs.scm:2749-2750, self-alignment-interface.cc:121-139 -- LilyPond's own comment names lyrics without associatedVoice as the case). MEASURED and font-free by construction: probe scores CLI and CLA put the ink centre on 1.175000 over a column at 0.500000 for syllables of 0.990156 and 1.365732, i.e. 0.675000 both times. Lily# reported 0.000000 -- it drew the syllable centred on the column itself -- so the residual was the whole of he.centre, and it now reports 0.675000000. ⚠️ This is the DRAWN half of the defect; staffless.lead-sheet.narrow-syllable-floor and -width-blind are the SPACING half (the same missing offset seen through the keep-inside-line rod), and all four closed in one commit. THE PORT IS LilyPond's FORMULA, not this number: LyricEngraver adds he.centre from SpacingRules.ParentAlignmentCentresPerColumn, which unions the column's note heads and rests and falls back to EngravingDefaults.PaperColumnXAlignmentExtentWidth / 2 -- so 0.675 appears in the code exactly once, as half a grob property, and the staff-ful case reads a note head instead without a second constant.

lyric.syllable-centre.note-column.why: CLOSED (-0.688700 -> 0) with its siblings: the SAME defect on the branch that is normally taken. When the parent column holds note heads, `he` is their combined extent and the placeholder never comes into it (self-alignment-interface.cc:121-141), so LilyPond centres the syllable on the NOTE HEAD's centre rather than on a nominal 1.35. MEASURED (probe LSH, a plain vocal line): the head is 1.377400 wide and the syllable's ink centre sits 0.688700 right of its column -- half a note head, and NOT the 0.675000 the staff-less scores give. That the two numbers differ is what proves this branch is live rather than dead code for lyrics; the prediction written before the run named 'half a note head, not 0.675' with '0.675 again' as its falsifier, and the falsifier did not fire. Lily# reported 0.000000 here too: it centred on the column in both regimes, so it was not that Lily# ported one branch and missed the other -- it never had the offset at all. It now reports 0.688700000, reading the head's own box rather than a second constant. ⚠️ THIS POINT IS WHY THE PORT WRITES BOTH BRANCHES (section 5.2 'write every branch'). A port that only added 0.675 where there are no note heads would have closed the staff-less points and left every vocal score 0.688700 out, with nothing in the corpus to say so -- and 0.675 would have been WRONG here by 0.013700, which is small enough to look like rounding and never be questioned. ⚠️ WHAT IS IN `he` WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: probe LSA adds an accidental and LSD a dot, and BOTH leave this at 0.688700 (so neither joins the extent), while LSR replaces the head with a rest and gives 0.750000 (so a rest does). Two of those three predictions were written down first and were wrong; the port unions heads and rests only because of them.

staffless.chord-symbol-over-notehead.why: EXACT ON ARRIVAL, and the honest reading is that it measures LESS than it looks like it does. LilyPond's value is 0 by construction: over a staff its ChordName and the note head it stands over share an anchor exactly (score CS dumps both at 8.585000), because ChordName has no X-offset and no self-alignment-interface (scm/define-grobs.scm:837-855). Lily# agrees to 0.000000 -- the symbol IS on the note's column. ⚠️ What this CANNOT see is the anchor convention, and it did not see it when the convention was WRONG either: the recorder stores the ANCHOR POINT a text was drawn at, which is the column whether the ink is centred on it (Lily# until 2026-07-25) or starts at it (LilyPond, and Lily# since). This number was 0.000000 through both. It is kept as a cheap guard that a chord symbol stays bound to its note's column (a lead sheet where the symbol drifts off the note would show here), NOT as evidence the anchor convention is right -- LpGeometryLedgerTests.ChordSymbolsAreAnchoredAtTheirInkLeft asserts that directly, for exactly this reason.

page.natural.staff-staff-inside.why: EXACT. THE CONTROL of the pair that asks whether the distance between two staves of a system comes out of the PAGE's spring chain. Same music and same bar count as page.stretched.staff-staff-inside, on the same six-systems-per-page paper, with ragged-bottom on so nothing stretches. PREDICTION, written before running: 9.000000 on both sides -- staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance, because this music asks ensure_min_distance for less than that (the treble c hangs 3.545 below its middle line, the bass staff's deepest up-stem reaches 3.0 above its own, 3.545 + 3.0 + 1 = 7.545 < 9). Measured on LilyPond 2.26.0: 9.000000 on all three pages, and Lily# reads 9.000000 too, so the control is flat on both sides and every digit the stretched entry moves is the stretch. NOT SITTING ON A FLOOR in the sense HANDOFF 5.0 warns about: 9 is the spring's IDEAL, not its minimum, so a force reaches it -- which is exactly what the twin entry shows.

page.stretched.staff-staff-inside.why: THE STAFF SPRING INSIDE A SYSTEM, on a page that stretches. Page_layout_problem::append_system pushes one spring per spaceable staff into the SAME chain as the system-to-system springs (page-layout-problem.cc:651-720): ideal = staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance 9, inverse stretch strength = its stretchability 5 (define-grobs.scm:3352-3355). Lily# has no such spring -- PageLayouter.PositionSystemsOnPage builds one spring per SYSTEM boundary, and every system on every page is drawn at the score-wide MultiStaffLayouter.CalculateSystemHeight, the Align_interface minimum, at any force. PREDICTION, written before running: LilyPond 9 + 5f and Lily# 9.000000 flat, so the residual is the whole stretch. THE PREDICTION HELD AND ITS OWN FALSIFIER CONFIRMED IT: measured 9.495460 with the system gap on the same page at 17.945524, i.e. (9.495460 - 9) / 5 = 0.0990920 and (17.945524 - 12) / 60 = 0.0990921 -- one force, seven digits, which is only possible if the staff distance is a spring in that chain. Lily# reads 9.000000 -- the same number as the ragged control, on the same paper -- so the residual -0.495460 IS the stretch, in one piece, with nothing else mixed in. Read on PAGE 1; page 2 and the short page 3 solve to their own forces (both 9.491922 under the cap). This is also the answer to the older question of whether BuildSystemSkylines should offset the last staff by the MINIMUM translation (page-layout-problem.cc:1080-1095) or by the final position: they were the same number in Lily# because nothing ever stretched them apart, so that divergence could not be measured until this spring existed -- and now that it does, the skylines are still built at the MINIMUM height, which is what makes them LilyPond's. PORTED: the staff springs now go into the page's chain (PageLayouter.PositionSystemsOnPage, from MultiStaffLayouter.StaffSprings), and this entry went -0.495460 -> -0.002480 with system.stretched-distance.two-staff going +0.373744 -> -0.029762 in the same commit. WHAT IS LEFT IS ONE QUANTITY, not two: read as a force, Lily# now solves this page to 0.09859604 by BOTH entries -- (9.492980179 - 9) / 5 and (17.915762143 - 12) / 60 agree to nine digits -- against LilyPond's 0.09909207. So the chain's SHAPE agrees and only the page's total slack differs, by dF = 0.000496. That remainder is NOT the staff spring; it is whatever the top and last-bottom springs are floored by. CLOSED, and the sentence that used to end this entry -- 'the notehead reserved at a nominal 1.0 where LilyPond's LILC ink is 0.545' -- was WRONG, in both halves. The skyline had already been on the LILC ink since cff877c8 (EngravingDefaults.NoteheadHeight was a dead pass-through parameter, which is how the claim survived a session as the HANDOFF's next move), and the notehead was not the binding ink here at all: seeding it at 0.550 instead moves NINE other ledger entries and not one of these four. What the four were is TWO FORCES, not four distances -- residual divided by the spring's own strength is one number per page (0.002480/5 = 0.029762/60 = 0.000496; 0.006666/2 = 0.013334/4 = 0.003333) -- and a force is the page's slack over its strength, so the fault had to be a FIXED term in the chain, not a spring. Solving the chain for it from both regimes at once named the term before it was measured: with the top spring free (6+6f stretched, 6-6f compressed) and the last-bottom spring rigid on its floor, Lily#'s floor comes out 336*0.000496 = 0.166664 too tall from the stretched page and 50*0.003333 = 0.166664 from the compressed one -- the SAME number from two independent regimes, which is what made it a term and not a coincidence. Measured after that prediction, the probe agrees exactly: LilyPond puts 3.333333 of ink below the last staff's refpoint on JSS, JSSC and JSK alike, Lily# reserved 3.500000, and the bass staff's deepest ink is a middle-line down stem. LilyPond shortens it -- stem.cc:522's guard is dir * hp[dir] >= 0, which INCLUDES position 0 -- from 7 to 20/3 half-spaces, and Lily#'s port had spelled that guard as two strict inequalities, so a middle-line stem was both drawn and reserved at the full 3.5. Fixed by matching the guard and by having SkylineBuilder reserve the stem StemCalculator computes instead of a flat EngravingDefaults.DefaultStemLength (the 'draws right, reserves stale' double model its own comments already named for BEAMED stems). All four now read within 5e-7.

system.stretched-distance.two-staff.why: WHERE THE SLACK WENT INSTEAD. The SYSTEM spring on the same stretched page as page.stretched.staff-staff-inside, measured last-staff-refpoint to next-system-first-staff-refpoint (the probe script prints it from the raw doubles rather than leaving two F6 prints to be subtracted -- arithmetic on a rounded gap is how 3.544994 for 3.550000 got into system.stretched-distance). It is here because the slack has to go somewhere: LilyPond shares this page's stretch between 5 system springs at stretchability 60 and 6 staff springs at 5, while Lily# has only the system springs. PREDICTED DIRECTION, written before running: Lily#'s gap opens WIDER. IT DOES -- 18.319268 against 17.945524, i.e. Lily# solves the same page to force 0.105321 where LilyPond solves it to 0.099092. ⚠️ THE MAGNITUDE WAS NOT PREDICTED CORRECTLY and is NOT yet accounted for: the guess was +0.53 from sharing the same slack over 300 units of stretchability instead of 330, and the truth is +0.373744. The two chains differ in more than the staff springs (top-system-spacing, last-bottom-spacing and the ink extents that floor them are Lily#'s own numbers on this page: its first refpoint and foot slack are not LilyPond's either), so the arithmetic that would close this entry has not been done -- do not read the residual as 'the staff springs' share' until it has. What the entry IS good for: a port that adds the staff spring must close this and page.stretched.staff-staff-inside TOGETHER, and one that closes only the staff entry has moved the money rather than the model. PORTED, and it did close together: +0.373744 -> -0.029762 while the staff entry went -0.495460 -> -0.002480. It also CROSSED ZERO, which is the honest reading -- the gap was too wide because it was carrying the staff springs' share, and now it is a hair too narrow because the whole page solves to a slightly smaller force (0.09859604 against 0.09909207; both entries report that same force to nine digits, so what is left is the page's total slack and not this spring). ⚠️ The +0.53 magnitude guess recorded above stays wrong and stays recorded: the arithmetic that would have predicted +0.373744 was never done, and the port did not do it either. CLOSED with the other three: this residual divided by its own stretch strength (0.029762/60) equals the staff entry's divided by ITS strength (0.002480/5), so the pair was never two quantities -- it was one force, and the arithmetic that had been skipped here is the one that finally named the cause. See page.stretched.staff-staff-inside for it. What that entry says about the money holds in the end: the port that closed this one had to close both together, and this time it did because it moved the MODEL (a middle-line stem is shortened, stem.cc:519-555, and the skyline reserves what the renderer draws) rather than the money.

page.compressed.staff-staff-inside.why: THE THIRD REGIME OF ONE SPRING: page.natural.staff-staff-inside reads it at rest (9.000000), page.stretched.staff-staff-inside stretched, this one SQUEEZED. Same music and same bar count as both, on a page packed with eight systems instead of six -- which is what the breaker picks for this score unaided, and it compresses them. COMPRESSION USES A DIFFERENT STRENGTH FROM STRETCHING and that is the point of the entry: alter_spring_from_spacing_spec sets minimum-distance 7 and then set_default_strength, so inverse_compress = ideal - minimum = 9 - 7 = 2 (spring.cc:205-211), while the ensure_min_distance that follows raises the FLOOR to the alignment minimum without recomputing the strength. Stretching used 5. So a port that has the spring but reads its strengths from one place is green on the stretched pair and wrong here. PREDICTION, written before running: inside < 9, above the 7.545 alignment floor (so the spring is not sitting on it), and (9 - inside) / 2 = (12 - system-to-system) / 4 for one negative force. THE PREDICTION AND ITS FALSIFIER BOTH HELD: measured 8.651797 with the system gap at 11.303595, i.e. 0.3482030 / 2 = 0.1741015 and 0.6964050 / 4 = 0.1741013. Read on PAGE 1. ⚠️ There is no ragged control here and there must not be one: ragged-bottom suppresses stretching only, so a full ragged page compresses identically -- the control is the natural entry. WHAT THE ENTRY FOUND, filed and closed in one commit because it was a defect in the port that filed it: the staff spring was floored at the DRAWN distance, which already carries basic-distance, so it could not compress at all and read 9.000000 flat. LilyPond's minimum translation does NOT include basic-distance -- align-interface.cc:234-238 is behind INT_MAX == end && 0 == start, the PURE estimate, while the placement path calls with start = end = 0 (:128-134) -- so basic-distance reaches the placement only as the spring's IDEAL. Lily# folded it into the minimum, which is invisible at rest (a spring at rest IS max(floor, ideal)) and fatal under compression. Now -0.006666. AND THE REMAINDER IS ONE QUANTITY AGAIN: Lily# compresses this page at 0.17743462 by BOTH entries -- (9 - 8.645131) / 2 and (12 - 11.290261) / 4 agree -- against LilyPond's 0.17410134, and the two residuals stand in the ratio 2 : 4, i.e. their springs' compress strengths. Lily# squeezes slightly HARDER because its content is slightly taller, the same ink-extent family that makes it stretch slightly LESS on the stretched pair. One cause, opposite signs, which is the shape a slack difference has. CLOSED, and 'slightly taller' was exactly right while 'the same ink-extent family' pointed at the wrong grob: the notehead was already on its LILC ink and moving it moves nine OTHER entries and none of these. The content was taller by 1/6 staff space of STEM. This regime is what proved it: the stretched pair alone could not distinguish a too-tall content from a too-short page, but the same fixed term read through the compression strengths (50*0.003333) and the stretch strengths (336*0.000496) gives the SAME 0.166664, and only a fixed term at the foot of the chain does that. LilyPond's middle-line down stem is 20/3 half-spaces, not 7 -- stem.cc:522's guard is >= 0 and so fires on position 0 -- and both the drawn stem (StemCalculator's guard was two strict inequalities) and the reserved one (SkylineBuilder seeded a flat DefaultStemLength) were 3.5. Both fixed; see page.stretched.staff-staff-inside.

system.compressed-distance.two-staff.why: The system spring on the same compressed page as page.compressed.staff-staff-inside, measured last-staff-refpoint to next-system-first-staff-refpoint. Here for the reason its stretched twin is: the two springs of the page have to move TOGETHER and at their own strengths (4 for this one against the staff spring's 2), so reading only one of them cannot tell a page that compressed correctly from one that put the whole squeeze in the wrong spring. CLOSED with its three siblings, and the two strengths earned their keep: 0.013334/4 and 0.006666/2 agreeing is what said 'one force', and a force is slack over strength, so the fault was a fixed term and not a spring. The term was the ink under the last staff -- a middle-line down stem LilyPond shortens (stem.cc:519-555) and Lily# drew and reserved at full length. See page.stretched.staff-staff-inside.

page.compressed.two-staff.staves-on-firs.why: The structural guard for the two entries above, which read gaps by INDEX: eight two-staff systems = sixteen staves. Same role as page.stretched.two-staff.staves-on-first-page, and the same reason -- when systems-per-page put the Lily# side on a page that did not exist, the count entry was the only one that noticed.

page.stretched.two-staff.staves-on-first.why: The structural guard for the three entries above, which read gaps by INDEX: gap 0 is a system's INSIDE distance and gap 1 the distance to the next system only while the page holds six two-staff systems. Six is forced on both sides (systems-per-page = 6 / PageBreakingParameters.SystemsPerPage), so this counts the staves that reached the page: 12.

page.stretched.last-staff-to-foot.why: THE FOOT OF THE PAGE'S SPRING CHAIN, which the corpus has never read. Page_layout_problem appends one last spring after every system (page-layout-problem.cc:538-545) and what it spans is the LAST SPACEABLE STAFF's refpoint to the bottom of the page's band -- not the system origin, not the ink -- so the reading is paper-height minus that refpoint, and it is the term that closes the chain whose middle the six entries above read. WHY IT IS WORTH AN ENTRY: every one of those six reads a GAP, i.e. a spring's length at the page's force, and a force is the page's slack over the chain's total strength. An error in a FIXED term therefore lands in all of them at once, each scaled by its own spring, and the corpus shows N residuals for ONE cause with nothing to attribute them to. That is not hypothetical -- page.{stretched,compressed}.staff-staff-inside and their two system twins stood at four residuals for a session and were TWO forces, and naming the cause took dividing each residual by its own strength and then solving the chain from both regimes at once, precisely because there was no reading down here. LILYPOND'S NUMBER IS THE SAME IN BOTH REGIMES, 10.023885 stretched and compressed alike, and that is a mechanism rather than a coincidence to pin: the spring is ideal 1 with stretchability 30 (ly/paper-defaults-init.ly:84-87), and ensure_min_distance raises only its FLOOR -- to padding 1 + the last staff's own ink 3.333333 -- without recomputing that strength (spring.cc:156-159), so it blocks at f = (4.333333 - 1) / 30 = 0.111111 and neither page reaches it (stretched f = 0.099092, compressed f = -0.174101). It is rigid for a reason that stops being true on a page that stretches harder: a book that opens this reading above f = 0.111111 is measuring a different quantity and needs its own entry. PREDICTION, written before running: EXACT, here and on the compressed twin. The four gap entries closed to within 5e-7 in 96641db7, and they can only be that close if the term they close against is already right -- read as a force the stretched page now agrees with LilyPond to seven digits, and agreeing on the force means agreeing on the slack, which is this. AN ENTRY THAT OPENS EXACT IS THE POINT HERE (HANDOFF 5.2.1④): this is not a hunt for a new defect but the net under the one just fixed -- the middle-line down stem that was reserved at 3.5 instead of 20/3 half-spaces moved THIS number by 0.166667, and no reading in the corpus could say so directly. If it opens non-zero the prediction fails in a useful direction: the gaps would agree while the chain's ENDS did not, which puts the fault in the top spring or in the floor arithmetic and not in any spring between them. THE PREDICTION HELD: Lily# reads 10.023884333 against a recorded 10.023885, i.e. -6.67e-7, and that residual is not a defect at all -- it is the F6 the probe script prints, since LilyPond's own value is bottom-margin 5.690551 + padding 1 + ink 3.333333 = 10.0238843 and the ledger can only carry six digits of it. Recorded as 0 for that reason, which is also the entry's own limit: it cannot resolve a fault smaller than 1e-6, and the fault it was opened to guard against was 0.166667.

lyrics.natural.staff-to-lyric.why: CLOSED. WHERE A LOOSE LINE SITS, at rest. A Lyrics line is not spaceable, so Page_layout_problem keeps it out of the page's spring chain and places it afterwards with a SECOND Simple_spacer over the lines between two already-placed spaceable ones (page-layout-problem.cc:919-942 collects, :1025-1054 solves). The spring from the staff to its own lyric row is nonstaff-relatedstaff-spacing -- basic-distance 5.5, stretchability 1. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-07-26: this sentence used to read 'set_default_strength makes the inverse stretch strength the ideal itself', which is WRONG -- ly/engraver-init.ly:648-652 DECLARES (stretchability . 1) for the Lyrics context, so set_default_strength never runs on it and the strength is 1, not 5.5. The conclusion is unaffected and in fact strengthened (1 against LARGE_STRETCH 10e5 / HUGE_STRETCH 10e7 gives the row an even smaller share of the slack than 5.5 would), and Lily# was already right -- both LooseLineSpacer.NonStaffRelatedStaff and StaffSpacingParameters.NonStaffRelatedStaff carry 1. The error was in this record only, which is the dangerous direction: a port taken from this 'why' would have CHANGED CORRECT CODE to 5.5 (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (1), a REF beside a different claim). ⚠️ The COMPRESS strength IS ideal - minimum-distance = 5.5 - 0 = 5.5, and that is the one every reading on book LYRV depends on -- the two are different quantities and the old sentence conflated them. Read on the first system of page 1, staff refpoint to the row's baseline. ⚠️ NEITHER SIDE CARRIES A FONT METRIC, and that is by construction rather than by luck: LilyPond's Lyrics VerticalAxisGroup refpoint IS the syllable baseline (its Y-extent on this probe is -0.037044 . 1.820098, an overshoot below and the ascender above) and a Lily# syllable is drawn at its baseline. That only holds while the BASIC-DISTANCE binds: the spring's floor is the alignment minimum, made of the staff's ink plus the LYRIC'S OWN INK plus padding 0.5, and the first draft of this pair -- melody on c', a head 3.55 under the middle line -- put that floor at 5.865115, which beats 5.5. The reading would then have been the syllable's ascender, i.e. the font, and the two engravers' lyric faces differ by about 27% (HANDOFF 5.3). The melody is up at g''/a'' so the floor falls under 5.5 and drops out. ⚠️ This entry therefore says NOTHING about the floor; a low-melody book measures a different quantity and needs its own entry. PREDICTION, written before running: Lily# does not have the loose-line pass at all -- a text row keeps the offset it was laid out with (PageLayouter.PositionSystemsOnPage's remarks) -- so this entry reads whatever Lily#'s own lyric spacing produces, and there is no reason for that to be 5.5. Expect a NON-ZERO residual here, and the SAME residual on the stretched twin. THE PREDICTION HELD, and the number is round: Lily# reads 4.500000 against 5.500000, residual -1.000000 exactly, identical on both regimes. OPEN, and the defect is named: LILY# HAS NO nonstaff-relatedstaff-spacing. Its basic distance for a note-bound lyric line was built in LyricEngraver.CalculateLayouts as staffBottom + LyricParameters.StaffPadding (the pre-port name; now RelatedStaffBasicDistance) = 2.000000 + 2.500000, measured from the staff refpoint to the syllable's baseline, where LilyPond's is basic-distance 5.500000 refpoint to refpoint (scm/define-grobs.scm Lyrics VerticalAxisGroup / engraver-init.ly's Lyrics context). Both engravers then take a max against an ink floor and this pair is built so NEITHER floor binds, which is what makes the residual one quantity instead of two models. VERIFIED LIVE BY PERTURBATION rather than by grep (HANDOFF 5.2.1-6): StaffPadding 2.5 -> 3.0 moves the reading with coefficient 1. ⚠️ AND ONE CONSTANT THAT LOOKS LIKE THE ANSWER IS NOT IN THIS PATH AT ALL: LyricEngraver.LyricRowBaseline = 2.6 is the baseline of an INDEPENDENT lyrics row inside its own band; perturbing it to 3.0 moves this entry by ZERO, because `staff ... with lyrics ...` is note-bound and takes the other branch. A port that fixes 5.5 by editing that constant would move a different score and leave this one wrong. PORTED, same session: LyricParameters.RelatedStaffBasicDistance = 5.5, measured refpoint to refpoint, with the frame conversion (BasicDistanceBelowBottomLine) on the parameters so the page breaker's band estimate reads the same number instead of its own copy of the 2.5. Both entries now read 5.500000. THREE SNAPSHOTS MOVED and no more: test/lyric-break-pricing and test/lyrics-volta by 2.00 each (two systems x 1.0) and test/lyrics-after-rest-bar by 0.19, that last one because its skyline floor was already at 5.31. ★ THE OTHER FOURTEEN LYRIC FIXTURES DID NOT MOVE, and that is the interesting half: placement is max(basic, ink floor), so an unchanged fixture proves its floor was already at or past 5.5 -- i.e. ordinary music with notes under the staff is floor-bound in Lily# exactly as it is in LilyPond, which is why this defect could sit in the shipping output without looking wrong.

lyrics.stretched.staff-to-lyric.why: CLOSED. The same quantity as lyrics.natural.staff-to-lyric on a page STRETCHED to staff-to-staff gaps of 43.841185 instead of 12 -- and LilyPond's answer is the same 5.500000. ★ THAT IS THE FINDING, and it contradicts the obvious reading of the missing pass: 'Lily# does not redistribute loose lines, so on a stretched page its lyric row is in the wrong place' is FALSE for one row, because LilyPond's redistribution keeps the row with its staff too. get_spacing_spec hands the spring from a loose line to a NULL neighbour add_stretchability(SCM_EOL, HUGE_STRETCH = 10e7) and to a staff on its non-affinity side LARGE_STRETCH = 10e5 (page-layout-problem.cc:1257-1338), against an ordinary 5.5 for the spring to its own staff -- LilyPond's own comment there says this is deliberate, so that 'a spacing-affinity UP line at the bottom of the page will still be placed close to its staff'. The second solve therefore gives this spring about one part in 10e7 of the slack. MEASURED, and the sliver is visible and is the falsifier: 5.500000001945665 ragged against 5.500000181705927 stretched, two orders of magnitude apart in the excess, exactly as a share-of-slack term should be. Where the missing pass CAN show is a case this pair does not build: two or more loose lines between the same pair of staves, where the springs between them are ordinary nonstaff-nonstaff-spacing and the group really is distributed. PREDICTION, written before running: the same non-zero residual as the natural twin, to the digit -- Lily#'s row travels with its staff, so its number cannot depend on the page's force either. ⚠️ If the two residuals DIFFER, the prediction fails in the informative direction: it would mean Lily#'s row does move with the page, which is not what its code is documented to do. THE PREDICTION HELD TO THE DIGIT: 4.500000 here and 4.500000 on the natural twin, residual -1.000000 both. So the two engravers AGREE about the regime-independence and disagree only about the distance -- see the natural twin for the named defect (Lily# has no nonstaff-relatedstaff-spacing; its basic distance is staffBottom 2.0 + StaffPadding 2.5). ⚠️ WHAT THIS PAIR RETIRES: 'Lily# does not redistribute loose lines, so a stretched page puts its lyric row in the wrong place' -- which is what HANDOFF listed as the next porting target. For ONE loose line that is false on both sides, and porting distribute_loose_lines would not move either entry. What is worth porting is the 5.5. PORTED, same session -- see the natural twin. This entry keeps its own job afterwards: it is the one that fails if a future change makes Lily#'s lyric row depend on the page's force, which LilyPond's does not.

lyrics.verse-step.why: THE STEP TO A SECOND VERSE, which comes from a DIFFERENT SPEC than the line above it. With two loose lines between the same pair of staves, get_spacing_spec takes its loose-loose branch (page-layout-problem.cc:1315-1332): neither neighbour is spaceable, the upper line's affinity is UP so `before_affinity != UP` fails, and `after_affinity != DOWN` -- true of a second UP line -- returns the UPPER line's nonstaff-nonstaff-spacing, which ly/engraver-init.ly:653-656 sets to ((basic-distance . 0) (minimum-distance . 2.8) (padding . 0.2)). ⚠️ THAT IS THE OPPOSITE SHAPE from the spring holding the first line: a ZERO ideal with a MINIMUM, so the realized step is whatever ensure_min_distance leaves -- max(2.8, the two lines' own ink + 0.2) -- and LilyPond's verse spacing therefore RESPONDS TO THE TEXT, falling back to 2.8 only when the text is short. PREDICTION, written before running: 2.800000, because the syllable is `no`, with neither ascender nor descender, so the ink term (about 0.037 of overshoot + an x-height + 0.2) stays well under 2.8 and the minimum binds -- which also keeps the reading free of both engravers' faces. THE PREDICTION HELD, and something unpredicted came with it: the same dump reads 'staff/loose -> next loose line = 3.737890, 2.800000, 5.500001'. ★ THE LOOSE CHAIN IS COMPRESSED on this book. That equality is the point of the rung: it is what distinguishes a PER-GLYPH term from the per-inter-glyph-step term the ottava entry named (a per-step reading would predict three times, not four). text.width.aa.why: OPENED 2026-08-02 (session 74), the POSITIVE pair adjustment. MEASURED (LilyPond): 94 px where 'A' twice is 90 -- the A-A pair is placed FOUR PIXELS apart, and probe book TK1 'AAA' reads 143 px = 3 x 45 + 2 x 4, so the term is PER PAIR and not once per string. Pango shapes through HarfBuzz with the kern feature on; TextFontMetrics.AdvancePerEm asks SKPaint.MeasureText once per CODE POINT and cannot see a pair at all -- CHECKED, not assumed: MeasureText('8va') equals the sum of its three characters to 1e-4 font units, so Skia is not silently kerning either. PREDICTION for Lily# (before its run, sign certain NEGATIVE -- the only entry in this family that is): 2 x 1.548800000 = 3.097600000, residual -0.111870866. That sign is the family's strongest single statement: text.width.av beside it must come out POSITIVE from the same two glyphs, and no scale factor, no em and no face can move two readings of the same two glyphs in opposite directions. MEASURED (Lily#): 3.097600000, residual -0.111870866 -- the prediction to nine digits, and the opposite sign to text.width.av's +0.195418898 landed. The em (2.2) and the face (C059-Italic and the bundled TeX Gyre Schola Italic return the same advance for every glyph in these books) are therefore both dead as explanations, measured rather than argued. STAGE 1 PORTED (same day): -0.136573228, EXACTLY -4 pixels and exactly the prediction. This entry GREW because the rounding half was carrying part of it in the other direction; what is left is now the A-A pair adjustment ALONE, which is the point of doing the two halves separately. ⚠️ It closes only with real shaping (HarfBuzz), never with a table of pairs typed in here. STAGE 2 PORTED (same day) AND THIS ENTRY DID NOT MOVE AT ALL -- the sentence above was wrong, and being wrong is the finding. OPEN: THE +4 PIXELS ARE NOT IN THE FONT. HarfBuzz -- the shaper Pango itself calls -- gives A-A no adjustment whatsoever (shaped advances 704, 704 at upem 1000), while it gives A-V -90 and v-a -75, and those two ported to EXACT. The face has no legacy `kern` table to hide it in either: its tables are CFF GPOS GSUB OS/2 cmap head hhea hmtx maxp name post. FOUR MORE BOOKS WERE ADDED RATHER THAN A GUESS (text-advance.ly TM1-TM4, and they narrow it hard): "An" is 84 = 45 + 39 and "nA" is 84 = 39 + 45, so the term is NOT any pair containing an A; "AAAA" is 192 = 4x45 + 3x4, so it is PER PAIR and not a wider A in a run; and \concat of two separately-italicised "A" markups reads exactly 90, so it DIES when the two glyphs stop sharing one shaped run -- which makes it a shaping term that our shaping does not produce. ⚠️ WHAT IS RULED OUT, MEASURED: the font (no pair value, no kern table), a per-glyph effect (An/nA clean), a run-position effect (AAAA is linear in pairs), capital spacing (cpsp would move VV, which reads exactly 90). SOLVED THE SAME SESSION, AND IT IS THE FACE: LilyPond was asked what it actually drew -- ly:stencil-expr of the TextScript's stencil prints the pango glyph-string, and it names the file: `(glyph-string ... C059-Italic 3.865234375 #f ((1.6730220472440944 ... A) (1.5364488188976377 ... A)) C:/bin/lilypond-2.26.0/.../C059-Italic.otf ...)`. LilyPond's "LilyPond Serif" alias resolves to C059-Italic; Lily# bundles TeX Gyre Schola, chosen because the two agree on every ADVANCE and C059 is AGPL. THEY DO NOT AGREE ON KERNS -- shaped through HarfBuzz, per pair, in font units: A-A is +61 in C059 and 0 in Schola; V-A is -84 against -95; A-V -83 against -90 (both land on 40 pixels, which is why text.width.av reads EXACT); v-a -75 in both (which is why text.width.8va does). The +4 pixels are 61 units at em 2.2 quantised, to the digit. ⇒ PROVEN AT THE ENGINE LEVEL, not by arithmetic alone: probe books TS1/TS2 pin the SAME LilyPond to TeX Gyre Schola and read "AA" 90 px and "VA" 84 px -- EXACTLY Lily#'s two numbers. So the algorithm is now LilyPond's (same shaper, same per-glyph pixel snap) and this residual is ENTIRELY the bundled font file. ⚠️ DO NOT close it by adding 4 pixels for A-A, and do not close it by pinning the probe to Schola either: a stock LilyPond resolves C059, so that is what fidelity means. The decision it waits on is a LICENSING one -- C059 is AGPLv3 with a PostScript/PDF embedding exemption that does not cover shipping the font program in an application -- and it belongs to the project owner, not to this entry. DECIDED 2026-08-02 (user): KEEP TeX Gyre Schola. This entry and text.width.va are therefore PERMANENT, and they are the ledger's record of a deliberate divergence rather than a defect -- do not chase either of them. The size was measured before deciding, not after: the two faces' kern tables differ on 438 of 471 kerned pairs, 11.2% of two-character combinations (475/4225) land on a different reserved width once quantised, and real strings run 0 to 4 pixels apart ("Violoncello" 4, "poco a poco" 2, "Allegro" 1, "Ave verum corpus" 0) -- 0 to 0.137 ss. ⚠️ AND IT IS NOT ONLY KERNS: both faces form the ff/ffi ligatures, with DIFFERENT glyph widths (ff 605 units against 686, ffi 878 against 904; fi agrees), so the drawn page differs typographically and not just in what gets reserved. ⚠️ Only the ITALIC face was scanned pair-by-pair; the regular, bold and bold-italic faces are unmeasured and expected to differ the same way. See HANDOFF §3 for the decision and what would have to change to revisit it.

Two mechanisms, two ports. MEASURED (Lily#): 3.097600000, residual +0.195418898 -- the prediction to nine digits. 0.195418898 ss is 5.72 px, i.e. the pair's 5 px of kern plus the two glyphs' 0.72 px of rounding: BOTH mechanisms, and reading this entry alone would price the kern 14% high. text.width.va.why: OPENED 2026-08-02 (session 74, stage 2) as LILYPOND'S OWN IDENTITY: "VA" reads 85 pixels, EXACTLY what "AV" reads, so LilyPond contributes no difference between this entry and text.width.av and whatever Lily# shows between them is Lily#'s alone (HANDOFF §5.0: the strongest pair is the one where LilyPond is an identity). It is opened WITH the kerning port rather than before it because the port is what made the two readable apart: the font's own pair values are not symmetric (HarfBuzz gives A-V -90 units and V-A -95), so a shaper that quantises them per glyph lands them on DIFFERENT pixel counts while LilyPond lands both on 85. This entry is therefore the same one-cause residual as text.width.aa and closes with the same decision. ⚠️ The pair-of-entries argument still holds and is now sharper: a rounding rule that satisfies av must satisfy this one, and the CURRENT rule does, against the same face. DECIDED 2026-08-02 (user): the bundled face stays TeX Gyre Schola, so this entry is PERMANENT and deliberate -- see text.width.aa for the measured size of the divergence and HANDOFF §3 for the decision.
