Before trusting a residual, count the apostrophes on both sides. ⚠️ AND THE HYPOTHESIS THE OLD why RECORDED WAS WRONG IN ITS EXPLANATION WHILE RIGHT THAT SOMETHING WAS THERE: it said Lily# was not reserving the up-stem flag's ink AT ALL. It was reserving it, in the wrong PLACE. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY UNDER IT, once the octave was gone: 0.164800 - 0.100000 = 0.064800, the FOURTH site of the advance-versus-extent claim that closed three others in session 69. ItemSkylineFactory hung an UP stem's flag on GlyphMetrics.StemUpSE.X = NoteheadBlackAdvance = 1.304000 where the stem stands at 1.239200 = the attachment EXTENT 1.304200 minus half a stem thickness. Routing both directions through LayoutUtilities.StemX -- the one house -- predicted +0.100000 and delivered it to six places. ⚠️ WHAT IS LEFT IS THE SAME +0.100 THE DOWN PAIR CARRIES, and that is now the whole of this island's remaining error: all three flag points read ONE number. It is NOT diagnosed -- see flag.down.reach.high-neighbour-control, which is the cleanest statement of it because it never had a flag term in it. That the up-stem book lands on the identical +0.100 by a completely different route (a different stem direction, a different neighbour, a different Y band) is itself evidence that the +0.100 is one mechanism and not three coincidences.

column.floor.accidental.why: OPENED AND CLOSED IN ONE MOVE 2026-08-02 (session 72), which is allowed here because the point is not the fix -- it is the FLAGLESS statement of a defect that three flag points could only carry. Two quarters, the right one with a sharp: 3.354200 = 1.404200 (the head's ink 1.304200 plus its own 0.1 extra-spacing-width) + 1.650000 (the sharp's ink 1.450000 plus the Accidental grob's declared 0.2 on the left, scm/define-grobs.scm:40) + 0.3. Lily# read 3.454200 -- the same +0.100000 the flag island carried, in a book with no flag in it. THE MECHANISM: MeasureLayouter computed only the ROD for this pair (the skyline distance plus the spacing spanner's 0.1, lily/separation-item.cc:47-68) and handed it to EnsureMinDistance BEFORE merge_springs' headroom, so the floor became skyline + 0.1 + 0.3. LilyPond raises TWO constraints over one column pair and the headroom is measured from the FIRST: the spring's minimum is the padding-free skyline distance (lily/note-spacing.cc:78-83), lily/spring.cc:122 floors the ideal at min_distance + 0.3, and the rod stands beside it 0.2 lower, where it can only matter under compression. The layouter now computes both and applies them in that order. NO ACCIDENTAL-FREE BOOK CAN REPLACE THIS ONE and the probe measures why rather than asserting it: the duration ideal bottoms out at 2.504200 -- a 32nd pair and a 64th pair both report it, the same number an eighth pair does -- while a head-to-head floor is 1.404200 + 0.100000 + 0.3 = 1.804200, so an accidental-free pair in this shape is spring-bound at every duration.

column.floor.accidental.spring-control.why: A NULL RESULT KEPT AS A POINT. The same book as column.floor.accidental with the accidental taken away, which makes it SPRING-bound: 3.002245 is the quarter's duration space, not a floor. It was exact before the floor was fixed and exact after, and that is the whole of its job -- it is what says the duration side of the spring was never what moved, so the 0.100000 the accidental books carried could not be blamed on the ideal, on the head's metric, or on the drawing. Together with column.floor.accidental it is a one-variable pair: the only difference between the two books is the accidental, and only one of them was wrong.

column.floor.accidental.wide.why: THE SAME FLOOR 0.468000 WIDER, because the double flat's ink is wider than the sharp's. Under the defect this book read 3.922200 -- the SAME +0.100000 as the narrower floor at column.floor.accidental, not a scaled one. That is what said the term was a CONSTANT sitting under the floor and not a glyph width, an accidental padding, or anything else that would have tracked the ink. A residual that stays put while the quantity under it changes by 0.468000 is a much stronger reading than the same residual seen once.

column.floor.accidental.wide-flagged.why: THE SAME BOOK WITH THE LEFT COLUMN FLAGGED, at an eighth instead of a quarter, and LilyPond answers column.floor.accidental.wide to six places. That identity is the arithmetic statement that the flag contributes NOTHING to this gap: a down stem stands at the head's LEFT edge, so its flag hangs inside the head's shadow and never sets the column's reach at the head's own height (flagged-stem-reach.ly's FSD8/FSD16/FSD32 report 1.404200 at every duration). Kept so that the next reader who finds a common offset on a flagged book has a point that removes the flag from the question instead of having to build one.

courtesy.meter.barline-to-meter.why: OPENED EXACT 2026-08-02 (session 75) WITH THE COURTESY METER ITSELF. Lily# printed the courtesy KEY at a line end but never the courtesy METER, so a book going 2/4 -> 4/4 across a break lost the C at the end of the previous line -- found by an owner reading his own score, not by this corpus, which had no book that changes meter at a break at all (the fix moved ZERO of 210 snapshots). The rule is not that key changes are special: TimeSignature's own break-visibility is all-visible (scm/define-grobs.scm:3922-3953), and Time_signature_engraver::process_music overrides it with initialTimeSignatureVisibility -- end-of-line-invisible, ly/engraver-init.ly:867 -- for the FIRST signature only, guarded by scm_is_null (last_spec_) at lily/time-signature-engraver.cc:114-118. So the INITIAL meter never shows at a line end and every CHANGED one does. THREE CASES MEASURED, and this point is one of them: meter only -> the meter alone (this book, 0.750000 off the bar line's ink right edge); key and meter -> cancellation, new key, meter (courtesy.meter.barline-to-cancellation); neither -> the line end stays bare. ⚠️ THE THIRD CASE CANNOT BE A POINT and is held as an assertion instead: nothing is drawn, so there is nothing to measure, and a corpus that only measures ink is structurally blind to a courtesy that should NOT have appeared. ⚠️ ITS PAIR OPENS NON-ZERO ON PURPOSE -- see courtesy.meter.barline-to-cancellation. Do not 'fix' this one to match it.

courtesy.meter.barline-to-meter.double-b.why: EXACT (0.750000) -- and its FIRST reading was 1.240000, which was the INSTRUMENT and not the engine. RenderedGeometry listed each drawn stroke as a bar line, so on a double bar it named the FIRST stroke where LilyPond's BarLine grob covers both; every distance off it was short by the kern plus a stroke. Both engines in fact draw the pair 0.680000 wide (Lily# 99.40..100.08 with the meter at 100.83 = 0.750000). Fixed by grouping strokes closer than one staff space into one bar line -- LilyPond's (kern . 3.0) is 0.300000 ss and two different bar lines are a measure apart -- and no other point moved. ⇒ HANDOFF §5.0 'the first disagreement a new instrument shows is the instrument': the reading was old but the TEXTURE was new, and a compound bar had never been read before. SEEDED 2026-08-03 to discharge the debt that 0.750000 had been measured on ONE book (HANDOFF §7.7: do not turn a single book's texture into a constant). PREDICTION WRITTEN FROM THE SOURCE BEFORE MEASURING, and it was structural rather than empirical: lily/break-alignment-interface.cc:180-210 takes the space-alist off the LEFT grob and keys it by the RIGHT grob's break-align-symbol, then :241-243 places the next group at extents[idx][RIGHT] + distance - extents[next_idx][LEFT] -- so the INK-TO-INK gap is exactly `distance` and BOTH extents cancel. PREDICTED that changing either glyph cannot move it. MEASURED: this book has a DOUBLE bar (ink 0.680000 against CMT's 0.190000) and a NUMERAL 3/4 (extent 1.604735 against the C's 1.700000), and the gap is 0.750000 again -- bar ink right 31.288572, meter 32.038572. ⇒ THE NUMBER IS A TRANSCRIBED VALUE, NOT A MEASURED NET: it is BarLine's own (time-signature . (extra-space . 0.75)) at scm/define-grobs.scm:293. ⚠️ THIS OVERTURNS WHAT WAS RECORDED. SpacingRules.BarlineToCourtesyKey's remarks said the declared entry is not the printed gap, citing TimeSignature's (staff-bar . (extra-space . 1.0)) at :3953 and concluding the three courtesy constants were nets that could not be cited to the alist. That read the WRONG alist: TimeSignature's entry applies when a TimeSignature is on the LEFT and a bar line on the right, which is not this walk. All four printed gaps are alist entries read off the left grob -- bar->time 0.75 (:293), bar->cancellation 1.00 (:297), cancellation->key 0.50 (:1944), key->time 1.15 (:1989). ⇒ THE OPEN -0.2 ON courtesy.meter.barline-to-cancellation IS NOW ADDRESSED, not merely measured: Lily# spells 0.8 where LilyPond declares 1.0.

courtesy.meter.barline-to-cancellation.why: EXACT since 2026-08-03 (user approved the port). CLOSED BY TRANSCRIBING THE ALIST ENTRY: SpacingRules.BarlineToCourtesyKey is now 1.0, which is what BarLine declares for BOTH (key-cancellation . (extra-space . 1.0)) at scm/define-grobs.scm:297 and (key-signature . (extra-space . 1.0)) at :296 -- so one constant is right whether the courtesy group opens with a cancellation or straight with the new signature. ⚠️ THE WARNING BELOW WAS HONOURED, NOT IGNORED: it said not to move 0.8 to 1.0 without re-measuring, because KeyCourtesySuffixWidth RESERVES off the same constant that SharedRenderer DRAWS off. That is exactly why it was safe -- there is ONE constant and both sites read it, so the reserved width grew by the same 0.200000 the draw moved right, and the signature cannot run off room that widened with it. Had they been two constants this would have been the §7.7 defect. ⚠️ NO SNAPSHOT MOVED, and that is a COVERAGE FACT rather than a reassuring one: no fixture in the corpus changes key across a line break, so this point is the only observer of the end-of-line courtesy key. A fixture for it would be cheap and is worth having before the BreakAlignSpacing port moves this group again. ⚠️ THE REAL FIX IS STILL OUTSTANDING (see below): 1.0 is a literal now, but three constants where LilyPond has one break-align group is still the debt. Below is the account of the defect. OPENED AT -0.200000000 2026-08-02 (session 75), AND THE DEFECT IS ALREADY NAMED: SpacingRules.BarlineToCourtesyKey is 0.8 where LilyPond stands the cancellation 1.000000 past the bar line's ink right edge. It is not a rounding or a glyph term -- it is a CONSTANT that was never measured, because until this session nothing measured the end-of-line group off the bar line at all. THE PAIR IS THE READING: its twin courtesy.meter.barline-to-meter takes the SAME quantity off the SAME edge in the SAME book family with the key change removed, and opens EXACT at 0.750000. Two different LilyPond numbers off one edge, so a single 'space after the bar line' constant is wrong by construction on one side or the other; Lily# spells one (0.8) and lands 0.05 over on the meter side and 0.2 under on the key side -- the meter was given its own constant (BarlineToCourtesyTime = 0.75) when it was ported, which is why only this side is open. WHY LILYPOND HAS TWO: each break-aligned grob carries its own space-alist entry. ⚠️ THIS SENTENCE USED TO CITE TimeSignature's (staff-bar . (extra-space . 1.0)) at scm/define-grobs.scm:3953, WHICH IS THE WRONG ALIST -- break-alignment-interface.cc:180-210 reads the LEFT grob's alist keyed by the RIGHT grob's break-align-symbol, so the entries that govern here are BarLine's own, and TimeSignature's staff-bar entry governs the opposite walk. ⚠️ DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY MOVING 0.8 TO 1.0 WITHOUT RE-MEASURING THE KEY GLYPHS: the constant is also what KeyCourtesySuffixWidth reserves, so the reservation and the draw move together or the signature runs off the staff. THE REAL FIX is to put the end-of-line group through BreakAlignSpacing the way the line-START prefix already goes -- LilyPond has ONE break-align group at each end of a line, not a solver at one end and constants at the other -- and this point is what would prove it landed.

tie.y.seconds.lower.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81) WITH tie.y.triad.lower, AND THE TWO ARE ONE CLAIM. Same pitch, same head position (-6), same role (the FRONT of its tie column), different column: LilyPond answers -3.750000 here and -4.000000 in the three-tie book, because it varies a whole Ties_configuration together (tie-formatting-problem.cc:915-1001 generate_configuration / find_best_variation) and the front's chosen variation moves with the rest of the column (-7 here against -8 there, read off the debug-tie-scoring card). Lily# solves a column ONE TIE AT A TIME bottom-to-top and fixes the front before the others exist, so it cannot answer two different numbers to two columns whose front is identical. ⇒ THE PREDICTION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE READING: Lily# gives BOTH books the same height, so AT LEAST ONE of this pair must open non-zero. If both come back EXACT the prediction is wrong and the greedy solve is somehow reproducing the joint search's front, which would be worth knowing precisely because it is not what the source says. ⚠️ WHY THE HEIGHT AND NOT THE WIDTH: six width points over the same two three-tie books opened EXACT the same day. The width of the front tie is 3.875445 in BOTH columns -- the chosen position moves the tie without changing its span -- so a corpus of widths cannot see this approximation at all. That is the whole reason this reading exists. ⇒ THE CLOSED SIDE, 2026-08-04 (session 82): the restructuring landed and THIS reading did not move -- still -3.750000, EXACT -- while tie.y.triad.lower went -3.750000 -> -4.000000. That is this half's whole job: it is what lets the pair say the port taught the front tie to depend on its column, rather than seating every front tie a quarter space lower. KEEP IT: it is the regime where greedy and joint agree, and any future change to the column search has to leave it alone.

tie.y.triad.lower.why: CLOSED TO 0.000000000 2026-08-04 (session 82) BY THE RESTRUCTURING IT NAMED: TieFormattingProblem is handed the whole tie COLUMN and varies its ties together (generate_base_chord_configuration / find_best_variation / generate_extremal_tie_variations, tie-formatting-problem.cc:938-1023). ⚠️ THE NUMBER SAYS WHICH BRANCH DID IT: -3.750000 -> -4.000000 is exactly one half-space DOWN, so the front tie moved off the base position -7 onto the EXTREMAL variation -8 (:1086-1118) -- the one step a greedy solve cannot take, because it moves the FRONT for reasons that live in the rest of the column. ⚠️ THE CONTROL HELD: tie.y.seconds.lower is still EXACT at -3.750000, which is what the pair was opened to be able to say -- the port taught the front tie to depend on its column rather than shifting every front tie by a quarter space. ⚠️ THE CORPUS DID NOT MOVE (0 snapshots), AND THAT IS COVERAGE RATHER THAN SAFETY: the three-tie chords in the corpus sit around the middle line, where the base configuration already wins, so this probe is the only book in the repo that reaches the extremal branch. THE ACCOUNT AS OPENED, 2026-08-03 (session 81), at +0.250000, as the other half of tie.y.seconds.lower, which holds it: THE PREDICTION LANDED AND THE PAIR IS THE PROOF: Lily# answers -3.750000 to BOTH books, because it solves a tie column one tie at a time and the FRONT is fixed before the rest of the column exists. LilyPond answers -3.750000 to the two-tie column and -4.000000 to the three-tie one, because it varies the whole Ties_configuration together (tie-formatting-problem.cc:915-1001) and the front's chosen variation moves with its neighbours (-7 against -8 on the debug-tie-scoring card). So the residual is not a constant or a glyph term: it is the ordering itself, and it is the FIRST reading this repo has that the greedy-against-joint approximation can fail. ⚠️ ITS SIBLING IS EXACT AND MUST STAY THAT WAY: tie.y.seconds.lower is the same quantity in the column where greedy and joint happen to agree, so it is the control that says a port has not simply shifted every front tie by a quarter space. ⚠️ THE SIX tie.width.* POINTS OVER THESE SAME BOOKS ARE ALL EXACT and are not evidence of anything about this: the front's WIDTH is 3.875445 in both columns, so the width cannot see the position move at all. That is why they were opened first and why they were not enough. CLOSING IT is the restructuring named at TieFormattingProblem.ScoreColumnSymmetry and ScoreDirectionAgainstStems: hand the whole column to one problem and vary its ties together. ⚠️ THAT MOVES OUTPUT wherever a chord has three or more ties, so it needs approval and a snapshot pass.

tie.y.triad.middle.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81). The MIDDLE tie is in neither of LilyPond's two symmetry terms (tie-formatting-problem.cc:890-908 reads only ties->front() and ties->back()) and Lily# does not charge it either, so what the two engines can still differ about is the configuration it sits in rather than its own charge. See tie.y.seconds.lower.

tie.y.triad.upper.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81). The column's BACK -- the only tie Lily# charges the symmetry to, and the only one whose score reads layouts already fixed. See tie.y.seconds.lower.

tie.width.triad.lower.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81) WITH ITS FIVE SIBLINGS, as the pair the greedy-against-joint tie approximation has been waiting for. THE PREDICTION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE READING: this one EXACT. It is the column's FRONT, so Lily# solves it first against nothing and its answer cannot depend on the order at all -- tie.width.seconds.lower, the same role in a two-tie column, is exact. If THIS one is off, the defect is not the ordering but the outline, and the whole set means something else. WHY THREE TIES: LilyPond varies a whole Ties_configuration together (tie-formatting-problem.cc:915-1001) and charges its two symmetry terms only to ties->front() against ties->back() (:890-908); Lily# solves a column one tie at a time bottom-to-top against the finished layouts below, so the front is fixed by the time the term exists and only the back pays. With TWO ties front and back are the whole column and the two readings differ only in who is charged -- they cannot be told apart. Three gives a MIDDLE tie in neither term, which the joint search may move the outer two to suit and the greedy one cannot. LILYPOND MEASURED FIRST-HAND, and the two books say something before Lily# is consulted: TW3 (<c e g>) and TW3S (<c d g>) give the SAME THREE WIDTHS -- 3.875445 / 2.363045 / 3.051745 -- although their middle tie differs in BOTH position and direction (-4 dir -1 against -5 dir +1). The widths are therefore not a function of the middle tie's own placement, which is what makes them a clean reading of the column rather than of one tie. ⇒ 2026-08-04 (session 82): the one-tie-at-a-time solve is GONE -- the problem now takes the whole column -- and all six of these widths stayed EXACT, exactly as the set predicted they would. The reading that moved was the HEIGHT (tie.y.triad.lower); see it for what the widths could not see.

tie.width.triad.middle.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81). PREDICTION WRITTEN FIRST: EXACT, and this is the one the whole set was built for. A middle tie is in NEITHER of LilyPond's symmetry terms (:890-908 reads only front and back) and Lily# does not charge it either, so the two engines agree about what it is NOT charged. What they need not agree about is the configuration it sits in: LilyPond may have moved the outer ties to suit this one. ⇒ 2026-08-04 (session 82): so can Lily#, now that the problem is handed the whole column; this stayed EXACT through the change. See tie.width.triad.lower for the full account.

tie.width.triad.upper.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81). PREDICTION WRITTEN FIRST: this is the one most likely to open non-zero, because it is the column's BACK -- the only tie Lily# then charged the symmetry to, and the only one whose score depended on layouts already fixed. ⚠️ IF ALL SIX OF THIS SET COME BACK EXACT, THAT IS A RESULT AND NOT A DISAPPOINTMENT: it says the joint search happens to land where the greedy order does on these textures, so the books are a CONTROL and the restructuring still has NO observer. The honest next step would then be a book where the joint search MUST move the front -- not a port on the strength of a source reading. ⇒ ALL SIX DID COME BACK EXACT, AND THAT IS WHAT HAPPENED: the reading was taken in HEIGHT instead (tie.y.*), the front moved there, and the port followed the observer rather than the source. See tie.width.triad.lower.

tie.width.triad-second.lower.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81) as TW3's texture pair: the bottom interval is a SECOND, so the middle head is reversed to the other side of the stem and its tie runs past a head the outer two never see. LilyPond answers the same three widths as TW3 (see tie.width.triad.lower), which is what makes the two books a pair that moves the middle tie and holds the reading fixed.

tie.width.triad-second.middle.why: OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81). The middle tie with a REVERSED head beside it -- LilyPond places it at position -5 pointing UP where TW3's sits at -4 pointing DOWN, and still answers the same width. See tie.width.triad.lower.

flag.x.down.origin-from-head.why: EXACT since 2026-08-03 (user approved the port). CLOSED BY MOVING THE DRAW, NOT THE RESERVE: LayoutUtilities.FlagDrawX is the one house for the term now, and all three draw sites read it (notation staff, tab staff, grace). ⚠️ THE RESERVATION WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT WHERE IT IS -- that is LilyPond's own shape and not a split to tidy away: Flag::width declares the stencil's extent MINUS the same [RIGHT], so offset + extent puts the RESERVED ink back on the stem's centre while the DRAWN glyph stays on its right edge. Moving the reserve too would have been inventing an agreement LilyPond does not have. 18 snapshots rebased with approval, which is the honest measure of how wide this reached: every book with a flag, on notation, tab and grace staves alike. Below is the account of the defect. OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81), PREDICTION WRITTEN FIRST AND LANDED: -0.065000 on BOTH directions, because LilyPond puts the flag on the stem's RIGHT EDGE and Lily# on the stem's CENTRE, and half a stem thickness is 0.065. LILYPOND-REF: lily/flag.cc:198-205 Flag::calc_x_offset = stem->extent(stem, X_AXIS)[RIGHT]; lily/flag.cc:118-165 Flag::print returns the stencil UNTRANSLATED so the glyph lands exactly on that offset; lily/stem.cc:889-906 Stem::width makes a stem's extent (-1,1)*thickness/2. WHY THIS POINT EXISTS AT ALL: ItemSkylineFactory's remarks state this divergence in full and then say, in the same breath, that it was READ OFF THE SOURCE AND NOT MEASURED -- and that on this very line the previous read-off-the-source number only became trustworthy once a pair measured it. It ends with 'Open a point before moving it.' This is that point, and nothing may move the draw x until it reads. THE THREE flag.* POINTS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER CANNOT SEE THIS: they read the COLUMN's skyline, which is what the flag RESERVES, and the reservation was already brought onto the stem's centre deliberately (the self-cancelling offset+extent pair in flag.cc). Reserve and draw are the two spellings here, and only one of them has ever been measured. LILYPOND MEASURED FIRST-HAND on probe flagged-stem-reach.ly score FLXD: head x=8.585000, flag x=8.715000, so the flag origin is 0.130000 right of the head's -- a WHOLE stem thickness, not half, because a down stem's LEFT edge sits on the head's left edge and calc_x_offset takes its RIGHT. THE READING IS HEAD-RELATIVE so the column's own position divides out of both engines; what is left is the flag's placement inside its column, which is the only thing in dispute. Its pair is flag.x.up.origin-from-head, where the stem stands on the other side of the head -- a sign error in the placement would read as agreement on one book alone.

flag.x.up.origin-from-head.why: EXACT since 2026-08-03 (user approved the port) -- see flag.x.down.origin-from-head, which holds the account of the fix. THE PAIR DID ITS JOB: both directions closed to EXACT on the same one-line change, which is what says the term is half a stem thickness and not a sign error that happened to fit one side. OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81) as the DIRECTION PAIR of flag.x.down.origin-from-head, which holds the whole account. LILYPOND MEASURED FIRST-HAND (score FLXU): head x=8.585000, flag x=9.889200, so the flag origin is 1.304200 right of the head's -- exactly the notehead's own width, i.e. the up stem's centre at 1.239200 plus the same 0.065 the down book shows. THE PAIR IS THE POINT: the stem stands at the head's LEFT edge on a down stem and at its RIGHT on an up one, so the two books put the flag on opposite sides of the head and no single sign error can satisfy both. If these two ever read DIFFERENT residuals, the defect is not the 0.065 term but the stem X itself, and LayoutUtilities.StemX is where to look -- that house was already the fourth site of the advance-versus-extent confusion (1.304000 read where 1.239200 was meant), which the existing flag.up.reach point hid behind an OCTAVE error in its twin.

courtesy.key.cancellation-to-key.why: EXACT since 2026-08-03 (user approved the port), and it closed WITH the end-of-line group going through BreakAlignSpacing rather than as a fourth hand-placed literal, which is what this entry asked for. The bare 0.4 is gone from all THREE places it was spelled -- the standard cancellation branch and the custom-key branch of SharedRenderer.DrawKeySignatureChange, and SpacingRules.KeyCourtesySuffixWidth -- and all three now read SpacingRules.BreakAlignGap(KeyCancellation, KeySignature), which is the alist. The three NAMED constants (BarlineToCourtesyKey, BarlineToCourtesyTime, CourtesyKeyToTimeGap) were deleted in the same commit and moved nothing, exactly as predicted: each was already its entry. Five snapshots moved and were rebased with approval (keysig-treble, keysig-bass, keysig-change, keysig-cancel-naturals, key-change-linebreak) -- the FIRST four are mid-measure key changes, which is worth noting: this gap was never only an end-of-line quantity, the draw walk is shared, so the fix reaches every cancellation in the corpus. Below is the account of the defect. OPENED 2026-08-03 (session 81), AND THE PREDICTION WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE READING AND LANDED: -0.100000, because SharedRenderer.DrawKeySignatureChange advances the pen by AccidentalNatural.Width + 0.4 after the cancellation naturals where LilyPond's KeyCancellation declares (key-signature . (extra-space . 0.5)) at scm/define-grobs.scm:1944. If the residual comes back anything but -0.1 the reading is not this constant and the instrument is the first suspect. LILYPOND MEASURED FIRST-HAND on probe courtesy-meter.ly score CMK (not taken from the handoff): KEYCANCEL x=24.543507 ext (0 . 2.449800) so its ink ends 26.993307, KEY x=27.493307 -- 0.500000 exactly, and the same walk's other two gaps come back 1.000000 (bar->cancellation) and 1.150000 (key->meter), which are the alist entries the three ported constants already carry. WHY IT WAS MISSED: the 2026-08-03 audit of the courtesy group found all THREE named constants to be their alist entry exactly, and stopped there -- but the group has FOUR gaps and the fourth is not a named constant at all, it is a bare 0.4 inside the draw walk. No ledger point reached it, no fixture could see it (test/key-change-linebreak was added the same day and pins the group's total, not this gap), so it survived an audit that was looking straight at it. THE RECORDED JUSTIFICATION FOR 0.4 IS THE SAME SHAPE TWICE OVERTURNED THIS SESSION: the comment says LilyPond's 0.5 is 'trimmed by their (extra-spacing-width . (0.0 . 1.0)) overlap -- a spring, not a fixed pad, whose net in this inline model is ~0.4'. But break-alignment-interface.cc:241-243 places the next group at extents[idx][RIGHT] + distance - extents[next][LEFT], so BOTH extents cancel and the ink-to-ink gap IS the entry; extra-spacing-width does not enter that walk. That is the same 'measured net' claim that was false for the other three. ⚠️ CLOSING THIS MOVES OUTPUT -- every book with a cancellation shifts its new signature right by 0.100000 -- so it needs approval, and it should land WITH the end-of-line group going through BreakAlignSpacing rather than as a fourth hand-edited literal. The reservation side (SpacingRules.KeyCourtesySuffixWidth) spells the same 0.4 and must move in the same commit: they are TWO spellings of one quantity, which is the §7.7 defect this group already carries.

stem.reach.accidental-above-head.why: OPENED EXACT 2026-08-02 (session 75), and it is the point the STEM belongs to. LilyPond's column skyline holds a stem because nothing takes it out -- every acknowledged Item goes into the column's `elements` (lily/paper-column-engraver.cc:246-261) and every element becomes its own box (lily/separation-item.cc:152-187, axis groups skipped at :160-161 so head and stem enter separately). Lily# built the same skyline from a HAND-WRITTEN LIST of parts and the stem was not on it; worse, SpacingRules.CalculateNoteheadRightExtent said 'excluding stems and flags' with the separation-item citation standing directly under it, so the omission read as ported. In this book g's two heads and ceses''s are 1.5 ss apart and never share a Y, so the ONLY part of the left column standing opposite the double flat is the stem: 3.822200 = 1.404200 (head ink + its own 0.1) + 2.118000 (the double flat's ink + the Accidental grob's 0.2 on the left) + 0.3 (merge_springs' headroom). ⚠️ THE PAIR CANNOT BE READ ON THE LILYPOND SIDE: a stem never reaches further right than its own head (lily/stem.cc:889-906 Stem::width is +/-thickness/2 about an X-offset that puts its right edge ON the head's), so LilyPond answers the SAME 3.822200 to the control, where the head does the standing. What a stem changes is not how far a column reaches but AT WHICH Y it reaches at all -- which is exactly why an opt-in list of parts could lose one and stay green. FALSIFIER, MEASURED and not argued: with the stem taken back out of ItemSkylineFactory this book reads 3.163357961 (residual -0.658842039) and the control stays EXACT. ⚠️ THE PREDICTED FALSIFIER VALUE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED IT: it was written as the bare quarter duration space 3.002244999; the 0.161112962 on top is the optical stem correction this pair carries because the two stems point opposite ways, a term no skyline touches. NOT PORTED and stated here too: the stem's Y range is the UNBEAMED one (lily/stem.cc:393-398 Stem::internal_pure_height with calc_beam = false); the beamed branch at :399-444 unites it with the beam's other same-direction stems, and :443 clips the union back on the non-stem side, so what Lily# uses can only UNDER-reserve. A book whose stem is not its beam group's extreme one would measure that, and none exists yet.

stem.reach.accidental-in-head-band-contr.why: THE CONTROL FOR stem.reach.accidental-above-head, moving ONE thing: the neighbour's pitch. aeses sits one staff position above g instead of three, so the two HEADS share a Y and the head is what stands opposite the double flat. Because a stem stands at its own head's right edge, the distance is the same 3.822200 either way -- so this book is BLIND to whether the skyline holds a stem, and that is its job. MEASURED both ways: EXACT with the stem in the skyline and EXACT with it taken out, while its pair falls 0.658842039. Without it, 'the stem fixed SRA' would be indistinguishable from 'something about double flats, or quarters, or that pitch, fixed SRA'. ⚠️ DO NOT DELETE THIS AS A DUPLICATE OF ITS PAIR BECAUSE LILYPOND RETURNS THE SAME NUMBER FOR BOTH -- the identity on the LilyPond side is the reason the pair exists, not a reason to drop half of it. The whole reading lives on the Lily# side, where the two books disagreed.

cue.column.step.why: UNMOVED BY THE 2026-08-03 CUE PORT, WHICH IS EVIDENCE AND NOT A NON-EVENT: replacing Lily#'s invented 0.66 with LilyPond's own recipe (font-size -4, the THIRTEEN design read at magstep(-4)) closed cue.accidental.to-notehead to nine digits and left this reading unchanged to the digit. So the cue COLUMN residual is not the font-size, not the scale and not the design -- all three are now ported and it is still here. Whatever remains is a SPACING law, and it is isolated. OPENED 2026-08-02 (session 72) AS THE DIRECT READING OF THE CUE HEAD'S WIDTH. LilyPond refines a note spring's ideal by the LEFT column's head width (lily/note-spacing.cc:77), so a cue-to-cue step is the ordinary quarter's 3.002244999 with the cue head's shortfall taken out: 3.002244999 - (1.304200 - 0.815348908) = 2.513393907, nine places. IT OPENED AT THE FULL-SIZE STEP -- Lily# reads 3.002244999, the control's number to nine places -- so Lily#'s SPACING does not know about cue at all: the residual +0.488851092 IS 1.304200 - 0.815348908 exactly, the whole head-width term, missing. (The renderer does shrink the drawn head, by EngravingDefaults.CueScale = 0.66; only the spacing ignores it.) PREDICTION FOR THE PORT, written before it: giving the cue head the THIRTEEN design at font-size -4 and routing the SPACING through the same metric closes this to EXACT. If it moves but not to zero, the remaining part is not the head width. ⚠️ 0.66 CANNOT CLOSE IT EVEN IF THE SPACING IS WIRED UP: 1.304200 * 0.66 = 0.860772 against LilyPond's 0.815348908, so a wired-up 0.66 would leave +0.045423 here -- which is the falsifiable half of the claim that the scalar is wrong and not merely unused. Its control is cue.column.control (same shape, no cue), which OPENED EXACT.

cue.column.main-to-cue.why: OPENED 2026-08-02 (session 72) AS THE OTHER HALF OF THE PAIR: the step INTO the cue, where the left column is full size and the right one is not. Lily# reads 3.002244999 -- the control's number -- so this term is missing too. ⚠️ WHAT PRODUCES LilyPond's 0.104200 IS NOT IDENTIFIED, and saying so is the point of opening it separately. It CANNOT be the left column's head width: lily/note-spacing.cc:77 refines the ideal by the LEFT head, which is full size in this book, so that path predicts the control's 3.002244999 exactly. Something on the RIGHT (the cue column) shortens the spring by 0.104200 and it has not been named. PREDICTION, written before the port: porting the head width alone should close cue.column.step and leave THIS one at +0.104200. If the head-width port moves this number as well, it is reaching a term it should not, and the pair is what says so. ⚠️ Do not fit 0.104200 to anything -- name it or leave it open (HANDOFF 5.2).

cue.column.control.why: THE DOWRY, AND IT ARRIVED (2026-08-02, session 72): the same four quarters with no cue anywhere, EXACT at open. That is worth more than a non-zero control (HANDOFF 5.0): it says the ordinary note spacing around this shape is already right, so every difference the cue books show is the cue machinery and nothing else -- not the paper, not the duration space, not the book. ⚠️ IT MUST NOT MOVE when the cue sizing is ported. If it does, the port reached outside its island, and this point is the only thing that would say so.

cue.accidental.to-notehead.why: EXACT since 2026-08-03 (user approved the port): the CueVoice recipe landed and this reading closed to -0.000000000, nine digits. It was +0.033043423, and the cause was BOTH halves of one mistake -- Lily# read the TWENTY design and multiplied it by a hand-written 0.66, where LilyPond's cue states font-size -4, which asks 12.599pt and lands on the THIRTEEN design read at magstep(-4) = 0.629961. EngravingDefaults.CueFontSizeStep / CueScale / CueFont / CueDesignSize are the four names that replaced the one number, mirroring GraceNoteItem. ⚠️ THE THREE cue.column.* POINTS DID NOT MOVE AT ALL, which is the useful half of this result: the same port that closed this one left them at 0.488851 / 0.104200 / 0.561117 to the digit, so the cue COLUMN residual is not the font-size and never was. Whatever it is, it is now isolated. Below is the account of the defect. OPENED 2026-08-02 (session 72), AND IT OPENED WITH THE TWO HALVES ALREADY SPLIT -- which is exactly what the grace accidental's entry predicted would happen here. Lily# reads 1.076000000 = 0.350000 + 1.100000 * 0.66, so the PADDING is already LilyPond's (0.350000, unscaled, ported in session 70) and the GLYPH is still the twenty design times the invented 0.66. LilyPond's 1.042956577 = 0.350000 + 0.692956577, where 0.692956577 is the THIRTEEN design's sharp -- the same number the grace accidental already reads, because a cue's fontSize -4 and a grace accidental's font-size -4 select the same face. MEASURED in the column frame so no spring can hide it: the cue sharp's extent is (-1.042956577 . -0.350000), i.e. its right edge sits at exactly -0.350000, the full-size right-padding + padding that lily/accidental-placement.cc:391-416 position_apes reads raw. PREDICTION, written before the port: replacing 0.66 with the design lookup closes this to EXACT, and the padding term must NOT move -- if the residual overshoots to negative, the port has scaled the padding too, which is the mistake session 70 had to undo for the grace.

cue.grace.column.to-main.why: OPENED 2026-08-02 (session 72): a GRACE inside a CUE, where the two sizes COMPOUND. MEASURED (cue-span.ly C-GRACE): the grace head inside the region answers font-size -7.0 -- the CueVoice context's -4 plus the grace's own -3 -- and its box is 0.574399405 against a full-size black head's 1.304200. Lily# reads 1.938627215, which is 1.938627065 to seven places: grace.column.single.to-main, THE ORDINARY GRACE STEP. So Lily# is engraving an ordinary full-size-context grace inside the cue and the compounding is absent entirely, not merely mis-scaled. ⚠️ AND IT IS NOT A SCALE EITHER: 0.574399405 / 1.304200 = 0.440421 while magstep(-7) = 0.445449 -- the third time in this corpus that a font-size's box is not the twenty design scaled. WHICH Emmentaler design -7 selects is NOT MEASURED; the number above is the target and naming the design is the port's job (GlyphMetrics.ForDesign has 11/13/14/16/18/20/23/26). PREDICTION, written before the port: making a grace inherit the enclosing cue's font-size step and reading the resulting design closes this; if it lands near but not on the target, the design choice is wrong rather than the compounding.
